Selects a field of the pod (or container) to use as the value of the environment variable. The fieldPath subfield specifies the field to select, such as metadata.name, status.podIP, or spec.nodeName.
The API version of the schema that fieldPath is written in terms of. Defaults to 'v1'.
The path to the field in the referenced object from which to select the value. For example, 'metadata.name' or 'status.podIP'.

Boolean flag indicating whether the referenced key is optional. If true, a missing key does not prevent the container from starting; the environment variable is simply not set. If false, the key must exist.
The name of the volume that contains the file referenced by this file key reference.
ResourceFieldRef selects a resource field (such as limits.cpu or requests.memory) from the container. The value of that field is used as the value of the environment variable.
Container name: required if the resource is a container resource, ignored if it is a pod resource.
Divisor is the value by which the resource value is divided. Defaults to 1 if not specified.
The name of the resource to select from the container, such as 'limits.cpu' or 'requests.memory'. This is a standard Kubernetes resource quantity name.
Selects a key of a Secret in the pod's namespace.
The key of the secret to select from. Must be a valid secret key.
The name of the Secret from which to select the key.
Specifies whether the referenced secret key must exist. When set to true, the key is optional and its absence is tolerated; when false (default), the key must exist or an error is raised.
List of sources to populate environment variables in the ephemeral container. Each entry can reference a ConfigMap or Secret to inject environment variables.

configMapRef specifies the ConfigMap to use as a source for environment variables in the container. The referenced ConfigMap must exist in the same namespace, and its keys become environment variable names.
The name of the ConfigMap to reference for environment variables. The ConfigMap must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap must exist. If set to true, the ConfigMap is optional; if false (default), the ConfigMap must exist or the container will not start.
An optional identifier to prepend to each key in the referenced ConfigMap or Secret. Must be a valid C identifier.
Selects a Kubernetes Secret whose keys and values are exposed as environment variables. The block contains 'name' (the Secret name) and 'optional' (whether the Secret must exist).
Name of the Secret to reference. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Specify whether the referenced Secret must be defined. If set to true, the Pod will start even if the Secret is missing; if false (default), the Secret must exist before the Pod starts.

Determines when the kubelet pulls the container image for the ephemeral container. Valid values are Always, IfNotPresent, and Never; if not specified, the default is Always if the image tag is 'latest', otherwise IfNotPresent.

Lifecycle describes actions that the container runtime should take in response to container lifecycle events (postStart and preStop). It defines handlers executed at container startup and before termination.
postStart represents the lifecycle hook that is executed immediately after a container is started. It can specify an exec command or a TCP/HTTP request to perform at container startup.
Exec specifies the action to run a command inside the container as the post-start lifecycle hook. This object contains a 'command' field that is a list of strings to execute.

The command line to execute inside the container. The working directory is '/' and it is not run inside a shell, so shell directives like pipes or redirection won't work unless you explicitly invoke a shell.
HTTPGetAction describes an action based on an HTTP GET request. It configures the HTTP request sent to the container's endpoint to trigger the lifecycle hook.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the HTTP GET request. If not set, defaults to the pod IP. You probably want to set the 'Host' header in httpHeaders instead.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the GET request. Each item is an object containing a header name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to send in the HTTP GET request.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request.
Path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/' if not specified.
Name or number of the port to access on the container. If a number, it must be in the range 1 to 65535. If a name, it must be an IANA_SVC_NAME.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The URI scheme used for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS', with a default of 'HTTP'.

Configures a sleep action in the postStart lifecycle hook, pausing the container for a specified duration before it continues startup. This field corresponds to the Kubernetes SleepAction, available from v1.29.
The number of seconds the container sleeps when this lifecycle hook is triggered. Must be a non-negative integer.
Defines a TCP socket check to be performed during the postStart lifecycle hook, with fields for host and port.
Optional host name to connect to for the TCP socket. Defaults to the pod IP.
The TCP port to connect to. Can be a numeric port or a string referencing a named port in the pod.
Configuration for a lifecycle hook that runs before the container is terminated. This can specify an exec command or an HTTP request to perform actions such as graceful shutdown.

Exec specifies the action to take, which is to run a command inside the container as a pre-stop lifecycle hook. It corresponds to a Kubernetes ExecAction and contains the command to be executed before the container is terminated.

The command line to execute inside the ephemeral container as part of the pre-stop lifecycle hook. The command is run directly without a shell, so shell features like pipes or redirects are not interpreted; the first element is the executable and subsequent elements are arguments.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to run as part of the pre-stop lifecycle hook. It configures the endpoint (host, path, port, scheme) and optional headers for the request.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP; can be overridden, e.g., to use a service name.
HTTP headers to send in the HTTP GET request. Each item is an object containing the header name and value.
The name of the HTTP header, such as 'X-Custom-Header'.
The value of the HTTP header. In a Kubernetes lifecycle hook's HTTP GET request, each header is a name-value pair, and this field provides the value.
Path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/'.
The port number to access on the container for the HTTP GET request. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or the name of an existing container port.
The URL scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'; defaults to 'HTTP'.
Sleep action for the preStop lifecycle hook. It defines a duration in seconds (via the 'seconds' field) for which the container will sleep before being terminated.
Seconds specifies the duration, in seconds, to sleep before the container is terminated, as part of the preStop lifecycle hook.

Represents a TCP socket action as part of a pre-stop lifecycle hook. This action attempts to open a TCP connection to the specified port on the container's IP address to determine whether the hook succeeds.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket check. If not specified, the pod IP is used.
The TCP port number or named port on the container to send the pre-stop hook request to. The value can be an integer port number or a string naming a port in the container's ports list.
Liveness probe configuration for the ephemeral container. Specifies how to check container health and whether to restart it if unhealthy.

Exec specifies the exec action, which runs a command inside the container to check liveness. It is a list of command arguments where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments.
Command to run inside the container for the liveness probe's exec action. A list of strings where the first element is the executable and the rest are arguments.
Minimum consecutive failures for the liveness probe to be considered failed after having succeeded. Defaults to 3. Minimum value is 1.
Configuration for a gRPC health check, used in place of an HTTP or TCP probe. Requires a port number, and may specify a service name (as defined by the gRPC Health Checking Protocol).
The port number of the gRPC service that the probe will connect to.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default behavior is defined by the gRPC health check protocol.

Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform as the liveness probe. If the probe receives an HTTP response with a status code between 200 and 399, the container is considered healthy; otherwise, it is considered failed.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
Custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request for the probe.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the request, such as 'X-Custom-Header'.
The value of the HTTP header field. This is combined with the header name to form a header sent in the HTTP GET request for the liveness probe.
Path to access on the HTTP server for this HTTP GET request of the liveness probe.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container.
The protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) to use for the HTTP GET request from the liveness probe.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request, either HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP.
Number of seconds after the container has started before liveness probes are initiated. Defaults to 0.
How often (in seconds) to perform the liveness probe. Defaults to 10 seconds; minimum value is 1.
The minimum consecutive successes required for the liveness probe to be considered successful after a failure. For liveness probes, this value must be set to 1.
Specifies a TCP socket probe for the liveness check. This object configures the host and port to attempt a TCP connection, and the probe is considered successful if the connection is established.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket liveness probe. If omitted, the pod IP address is used.
Number or name of the port to access on the container. Number must be in the range 1 to 65535. Name must be an IANA_SVC_NAME.
Number of seconds after which the liveness probe times out.

List of ports to expose from the ephemeral container. Each item typically includes containerPort, protocol, and optionally hostPort, hostIP, and name, following the Kubernetes container port specification.
Port number that the container listens on. Must be a valid port number between 1 and 65535.
The host IP address to bind the container port to. When set, the port will be exposed only on that specific host IP.
The port on the host node that maps to the container port. This allows the container to be accessed externally via the node's IP and this port.
Optional name for the port. Must be a valid IANA_SVC_NAME and unique among container ports. Required when multiple ports are specified in the same container.
The network protocol for the port, such as TCP, UDP, or SCTP. Defaults to TCP if not specified.
The readiness probe for the ephemeral container. Kubernetes does not support readiness probes on ephemeral containers, so this field is rejected by the API server if set.
Exec specifies a command to run inside the container. The probe succeeds if the command exits with status 0.

The command to run inside the container for the readiness probe. It is specified as an array of strings, where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments. If omitted, the container's entrypoint is used.
Specifies the number of consecutive failures required for the readiness probe to be considered failed. The default is 3.
Specifies the gRPC health check configuration for the probe. It contains the port to connect to and an optional service name.
The port number to connect to for the gRPC health check. Must be a valid TCP port (1-65535).
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not set, the default is empty, meaning no service name is sent.
Specifies the HTTP GET request to perform for the readiness probe. This block configures parameters such as the path, port, scheme, and headers used to check the health of the ephemeral container.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the HTTP GET request. If not specified, the pod IP address is used.
List of custom HTTP headers to include in the probe request. Each header is a name-value pair, with 'name' and 'value' fields.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the request.
The value of the HTTP header sent in the readiness probe's HTTP GET request.
Path to access on the HTTP server.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container for the HTTP GET probe. Must be a valid integer port (1-65535) or an IANA service name (e.g., 'http').
The network protocol to use for the HTTP probe: either 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the readiness probe is initiated.
Specifies the frequency (in seconds) at which the readiness probe is performed. Defaults to 10 seconds.
The minimum consecutive successes required for the probe to be considered successful after having failed. For readiness probes, the default is 1; set higher to require multiple consecutive successes.
The TCP socket action for the readiness probe. It checks whether a TCP connection can be established to the specified port on the container, typically defined with a 'port' field.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket probe. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP address.
The TCP port to connect to. Can be a numeric port or a named port on the container.
Number of seconds after which the readiness probe times out. If the probe does not respond within this time, it is considered failed. Minimum value is 1, and the default is 1 second.
Resize policy for the ephemeral container, specifying how each resource can be resized and the restart policy applied (e.g., NotRequired or RestartContainer).
The name of the resource to which the resize policy applies. In Kubernetes, valid values are 'cpu' and 'memory'.
Specifies the compute resources required for the ephemeral container, including requests and limits for resources such as CPU and memory.

A list of resource claims that this ephemeral container uses. Each claim references a resource defined in the pod's spec.resourceClaims, enabling the container to request dynamic cluster resources. This field corresponds to the Kubernetes ResourceRequirements `claims` field, which is an alpha feature.
Name must match the name of one entry in pod.spec.resourceClaims of the Pod where this field is used. It makes that resource available inside a container.

Limits describes the maximum amount of compute resources allowed. The keys of the map are resource names (e.g., cpu, memory), and the values are quantities (e.g., "100m", "1Gi"). More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/

Requests describes the minimum amount of compute resources required for the ephemeral container. It is a map of resource names (e.g., cpu, memory) to quantities; if requests are omitted, they default to limits if limits are explicitly specified, otherwise to an implementation-defined value.
The comparison operator used to evaluate container exit codes against specified rules, determining whether a restart policy applies.
The list of container exit codes that trigger this restart policy rule. The rule applies when the container exits with one of these numeric codes.

SecurityContext defines the security options the ephemeral container should be run with, including user ID, group ID, Linux capabilities, SELinux options, and whether the container is privileged. If set, these settings override the Pod-level security context for this container.
Controls whether a process can gain more privileges than its parent process. When set to true, privilege escalation is allowed; when false, it is prevented.
Defines the AppArmor profile for the container, including the profile type (RuntimeDefault, Localhost, Unconfined) and an optional localhost profile path.
Specifies a profile loaded on the node that the pod is running on. This is required when the AppArmor profile type is set to Localhost.

Type of AppArmor profile to use. Valid values are: 'RuntimeDefault' uses the container runtime's default profile, 'Localhost' uses a profile pre-loaded on the node, and 'Unconfined' disables AppArmor enforcement.
The Linux capabilities to add to or drop from the container's process, specified as add and drop lists. Part of the security context for ephemeral containers.
Linux capabilities to add to the ephemeral container's capability set. Each entry is a capability name, such as 'CAP_SYS_ADMIN'.
Drops the specified Linux capabilities from the container's default set. Entries are capability names like 'ALL' or 'CAP_NET_ADMIN'.
Indicates whether the container runs in privileged mode, granting it access to all host devices and capabilities.

The type of proc mount to use for the ephemeral container. Supported values are DefaultProcMount (default) and UnmaskedProcMount. This field is alpha and only honored when the kubelet enables the ProcMountType feature gate.
If true, the container's root filesystem is mounted as read-only. This prevents writes to the root filesystem; writes must go to a writable volume.
The GID (group ID) to run the container's entrypoint process as. If not specified, the group ID defaults to the image's primary group.
Indicates whether the ephemeral container must run as a non-root user. If set to true, the container will be prevented from running as root and will fail if the image's user is root or unspecified.
The user ID (UID) to run the ephemeral container process as. If unspecified, the pod-level or container-level security context applies.
SELinux options to apply to the ephemeral container's security context. This object defines the SELinux label (user, role, type, and level) for the container.
The SELinux level (also known as sensitivity or MLS/MCS label) that applies to the container.
The SELinux role label for the container. In Kubernetes, seLinuxOptions define the SELinux context, and the role field sets the role portion (e.g., system_u).
The SELinux type label for the context, as defined in SELinuxOptions.
The SELinux user label for the container.
SeccompProfile defines the seccomp profile for the container. It allows specifying the type of seccomp profile (e.g., RuntimeDefault, Unconfined, Localhost) and optionally a localhost profile path.

The path to a seccomp profile on the node, used when the seccomp_profile type is 'Localhost'. This path is typically relative to the kubelet's seccomp profile root directory (e.g., /var/lib/kubelet/seccomp).
The type of seccomp profile to use. Allowed values are 'RuntimeDefault', 'Localhost', and 'Unconfined'. When 'Localhost' is used, the 'localhostProfile' field must be specified.
Specifies Windows-specific security options for the container, such as GMSA credentials and the username to run container processes as.
GMSACredentialSpec is where the GMSA admission webhook (https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/windows-gmsa) inlines the contents of the GMSA credential spec named by the GMSACredentialSpecName field.
The name of the GMSA credential spec to use for the ephemeral container's Windows security context.

Indicates whether the Windows container should be run as a HostProcess container, granting it access to the host's process and network namespaces. This is only applicable to Windows containers running with containerd.
The Windows username to run the container's processes as. This is part of the Windows security context options for ephemeral containers in a DaemonSet pod spec.

Specifies the startup probe for the container. The startup probe indicates whether the application inside the container has started successfully. If it fails, the kubelet kills the container following the container's restart policy. Supported probe types include HTTP, TCP, and exec, and the probe can be configured with fields such as initialDelaySeconds, periodSeconds, timeoutSeconds, and successThreshold.
Exec specifies the action for the startup probe by running a command inside the container. The probe is considered successful if the command exits with status 0.

The command to execute for the startup probe's exec action. It is a list of strings: the first element is the executable and subsequent elements are arguments. The command runs directly inside the container without a shell.
The number of consecutive failures of the startup probe that must occur before the container is considered unhealthy and is restarted. The value must be a positive integer.
GRPC specifies an action involving a gRPC port. This can be used to perform a gRPC health check on the container.
Port number for the gRPC health check. Must be between 1 and 65535.
Service is the name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default behavior is defined by the gRPC health checking protocol.
Specifies the HTTP GET request used by the startup probe to check container health. Includes configuration like target host, port, HTTP path, and headers for the request.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP request. Defaults to the pod IP. You probably want to set 'Host' in httpHeaders instead.
Custom headers to set in the HTTP request. Each header is an object with `name` and `value` fields. Allows specifying multiple headers.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the request.
The value of the HTTP header to send in the request.
Path to access on the HTTP server for the probe. Defaults to '/'.
The port to access on the container. This can be a numeric port number (1-65535) or a named port as defined in the container's ports specification.
The network protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
Scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Allowed values: HTTP, HTTPS.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the startup probe is initiated. This delays the start of the probe to allow the container to initialize.
The number of seconds between each probe execution. The minimum value is 1 second.
The minimum number of consecutive successes required for the startup probe to be considered successful after a failure. For startup probes, this value must be 1 and it defaults to 1.
TCP socket probe action for the startup probe. Specifies the host and port to check, performing a TCP connection attempt to determine if the container has started.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket check. If not specified, the pod's IP address is used.
The TCP port to connect to. Can be a numeric port (e.g., 8080) or a named port defined in the pod's containers.

Optional duration in seconds that the pod needs to terminate gracefully when a startup probe fails. Overrides the pod-level `termination_grace_period_seconds` for the corresponding container; must be a non-negative integer, where zero means immediate termination.
Number of seconds after which the startup probe times out. If the probe does not finish within this time, it is considered failed. Minimum value is 1.
Specifies whether the standard input stream for the ephemeral container is enabled. When true, the container can read from standard input.

Whether stdin is closed after a single attach. If true, stdin is opened on container start, remains open until the first client attaches, then closes when that client disconnects and stays closed until the container restarts.
The name of the container that this ephemeral container attaches to. If unset, it defaults to the first container in the pod.
The path inside the container where a termination message is written. When the container exits, Kubernetes reads this file to include in the pod's status.

Defines how the termination message of the ephemeral container is read. Valid values are 'File' (default, reads the file specified by terminationMessagePath) and 'FallbackToLogsOnError' (uses the last chunk of container logs if the termination message file is empty).
Indicates whether a TTY should be allocated for the ephemeral container. If true, also requires 'stdin' to be true. Defaults to false.
List of block devices to be used by the ephemeral container. Each item specifies a device path and the name of a volume to mount as a block device.
The path inside the container where the raw block device is mounted. This is used when a volume device is specified for a raw block volume.
Name of the volume device. Must match the name of a volume in the pod.
A list of volume mounts to expose to the ephemeral container, specifying the volume name, mount path, and mount options (e.g., read-only, subPath).
Path within the container at which the volume should be mounted. Must not contain ':'.
Controls how volume mounts propagate from the host to the container and vice versa. Valid values are 'None', 'HostToContainer', and 'Bidirectional'. Default is 'None'.
The name of the volume to mount. Must match the name of a volume defined in the pod spec.
If true, the volume is mounted as read-only; the container cannot write to it. Defaults to false.

Controls whether the volume mount is recursive read-only. Allowed values are 'Enabled', 'Disabled', and 'IfPossible', with 'Disabled' being the default when unset. 'Enabled' requires the volume type to support recursive read-only; 'IfPossible' enables it only if the volume type supports it.

The path within the volume from which to mount, rather than the volume's root. This allows mounting a subdirectory of a volume. Must be a relative path and cannot contain '..' to prevent escaping the volume root.
subPathExpr is an expression to compute the subPath directory to mount, using environment variable references (e.g., $(VAR)) to construct the path. It cannot be used together with subPath.
The working directory for the ephemeral container. If not specified, the container runtime default is used.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.host_aliases.hostname: The list of hostnames that should be resolved to the IP address specified in the same hostAlias entry.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.host_aliases.ip: The IP address to add as an alias for the specified hostnames in the pod's /etc/hosts file. Each entry in host_aliases maps an IP to a list of hostnames.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.image_pull_secrets.na: Name of the image pull secret, as defined in the same namespace.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.args: List of arguments to pass to the init container's entrypoint. If the command field is not set, the image's default entrypoint is used.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.comma: Command to run in the init container. This overrides the ENTRYPOINT of the container image. Specified as a list of strings; the first element is the command, and the remaining elements are arguments.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.env: A list of environment variables for the init container. Each variable can be defined with a name and either a direct value or a source (such as a config map, secret, or field reference) from which the value is derived.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.env.n: Name of the environment variable. Must be a valid C identifier, e.g., MY_VAR.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.env.v: The value of the environment variable, provided as a string. This is the direct value that will be assigned to the environment variable in the container's init container.
value_from is an optional field that specifies a source for the environment variable's value. It can reference a ConfigMap, Secret, or a field in the pod spec (e.g., downward API).

ConfigMapKeyRef selects a key from a ConfigMap to populate the environment variable's value. Specify the ConfigMap name and key; the optional field indicates whether the ConfigMap or its key must exist.
The key in the referenced ConfigMap to select the value from.
The name of the ConfigMap from which to pull the value for this environment variable.
Indicates whether the ConfigMap key must exist. If set to true, the container starts even if the key or its ConfigMap is missing; if false (default), a missing key causes an error.

Selects a field of the pod for the environment variable value. Common field paths include metadata.name, metadata.namespace, spec.nodeName, spec.serviceAccountName, status.hostIP, status.podIP, and label/annotation references via metadata.labels['KEY'] or metadata.annotations['KEY'].
The API version of the schema that the fieldPath refers to. Defaults to 'v1' if not specified.
The path to the field to select, such as 'metadata.name' or 'spec.nodeName'.
Specifies whether the referenced key is optional. If true, the container can start even if the key does not exist; if false or omitted, the key must exist.

Specifies a container resource field (e.g., limits.cpu or requests.memory) whose value is used as the environment variable's value. The selector includes the container name, resource, and optional divisor.
The name of the container to which the resource field refers. Defaults to the current container if not specified.
The value by which to divide the selected resource quantity. Defaults to 1 if unset.
The name of the resource to select, such as 'limits.cpu' or 'requests.memory', from the container's resource field reference.
Selects a key of a Secret in the pod's namespace to use as the value for the environment variable.
The key within the Secret to fetch the value from. This must correspond to a valid key in the referenced Secret.
The name of the Secret resource being referenced. Must be a valid Secret name in the same namespace.

Specify whether the Secret or its key must be defined. If set to true, and the secret or key is not found, the environment variable is not set; if false (default), the pod fails to start when the secret or key is missing.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.env_f: List of sources to populate environment variables in the init container. Each source can be a ConfigMap or Secret, or a reference to such resources, and variables are added to the container's environment.
ConfigMapRef is a reference to a ConfigMap from which environment variables are populated. It contains the name of the ConfigMap and an optional flag to indicate if the ConfigMap must exist.
The name of the ConfigMap to reference. The ConfigMap must exist in the same namespace as the pod.

Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap is optional. If true, a missing ConfigMap is ignored and no environment variables are injected from it; if false or unset, the pod fails to start if the ConfigMap does not exist.
An optional prefix to apply to the keys of the referenced ConfigMap or Secret. When set, each environment variable name is prefixed with this value.
Reference to a Kubernetes Secret. The keys in the Secret's data become environment variables in the container. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Name of the Secret to reference for populating environment variables.

Specify whether the Secret must be defined. If set to true, the Secret is optional and its absence does not prevent pod startup; if false or omitted, the Secret must exist or the container fails to start.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.image: The container image to run for this init container, typically specified as a repository, tag, or digest (e.g., busybox:1.36).
Specifies the image pull policy for the container. Valid values are Always, IfNotPresent, and Never. Defaults to Always if image tag is 'latest' or omitted, otherwise IfNotPresent.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.lifec: lifecycle is an object that defines lifecycle hooks for the container, such as postStart and preStop, which allow custom actions to be executed at container startup and before termination, respectively.

The post_start field defines the PostStart lifecycle hook, which is executed immediately after a container is started. It is an object that specifies the handler to run, such as an exec command, HTTP GET request, or TCP socket probe.
Exec specifies the action to be taken as an exec-based lifecycle hook. It runs a command inside the container after it is started (PostStart).
The command to run inside the container for this lifecycle hook. It is represented as a list of strings, where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments.
HTTPGet specifies the HTTP GET request to perform for the post-start lifecycle hook. It defines the endpoint to check and can include path, port, host, and headers.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request sent by the postStart lifecycle hook. Each item defines a header name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to set in the request.
The value of the HTTP header included in the HTTP GET request to the container's postStart lifecycle hook.
The HTTP path (URL path) to send the GET request to when the lifecycle hook is triggered. If not specified, the path defaults to '/'.
The port number or name of the port on the container to send the HTTP GET request to. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535, or a named port defined for the container.
Specifies the protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS; defaults to HTTP.
The URL scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The number of seconds to sleep in the postStart lifecycle hook. This delays subsequent lifecycle actions by the specified duration.
Configuration for a TCP socket probe executed as a post-start lifecycle hook for a container.
The hostname or IP address to connect to. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP.

The TCP port to perform the liveness check on. This can be a numeric port or a named port as defined in the container's ports list. The value must be a valid Kubernetes port number (1-65535) or an IANA_SVC_NAME.

PreStop is a lifecycle hook that is called immediately before a container is terminated. It allows the container to perform graceful shutdown tasks, such as draining connections or saving state, before the container is stopped.
Exec specifies the action to execute a command inside the container when the preStop lifecycle hook is triggered. This allows you to run a command immediately before the container is terminated.

Command is the command line to execute inside the container for the pre-stop lifecycle hook. It is a list of strings; the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments. The command is executed directly without a shell, and the working directory is the container's root.
An HTTP GET request that kubelet sends to the container as part of a lifecycle hook, typically used in preStop to trigger a graceful shutdown or health check.
The hostname of the HTTP server to connect to for the pre-stop lifecycle hook's GET request. If not specified, the pod IP address is used.
List of custom HTTP headers to include in the GET request. Each header is an object with `name` and `value` fields.
The name of the HTTP header to set in the HTTP GET request for the pre-stop lifecycle hook of an init container in a DaemonSet.
The value of the HTTP header field. This is paired with the header name to form a header entry in the HTTP GET request for the container's preStop lifecycle hook.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server for the pre-stop lifecycle hook's HTTP GET request. Defaults to '/' if not specified.
The port number or name to send the HTTP GET request to. It can be an integer port number (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container.
The protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) to use for the HTTP GET request, defaulting to HTTP.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to HTTP. Valid values are HTTP and HTTPS.

The 'sleep' field specifies a SleepAction handler for the preStop lifecycle hook, which pauses the container for a specified duration in seconds before termination, allowing time for graceful shutdown.
The number of seconds the container sleeps before it is terminated, used in the sleep action of the pre-stop lifecycle hook.

tcp_socket is an object that specifies a TCP socket action to be performed during the pre-stop lifecycle hook. It accepts a required port and an optional host, defining the TCP endpoint to connect to before the container is terminated.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket action. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP.
The TCP port number to connect to for the pre-stop lifecycle hook's TCP socket check. The value is a string containing a numeric port (e.g., "8080").
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.liven: Defines a probe that checks whether the container is still alive. If the probe fails, the kubelet restarts the container. This configures the liveness probe for the init container.
Specifies a command to run inside the container. The liveness probe is successful if the command exits with status code 0.

Command is the command line to execute inside the container. The working directory for the command is root ('/') in the container's filesystem. The command is simply exec'd, not run inside a shell. Exit status of 0 indicates success; non-zero is unhealthy.
The number of consecutive failures of the liveness probe before the container is restarted. The minimum value is 1.
grpc configures a gRPC-based liveness probe. It specifies the port to check and optionally the service name for the gRPC health check.
The port number to use for the gRPC health check. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535.
The name of the gRPC service to query for the health check. If not specified, the default is an empty string, which typically refers to the server's default health check service.
Specifies the HTTP GET request to perform as the liveness probe. It configures the HTTP request details such as path, port, and headers used to determine container health.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.

List of custom HTTP headers to include in the probe request. Each header is defined by a name and value pair, allowing the probe to send authentication or other required headers to the target endpoint.
The name of the HTTP header to send in the liveness probe request. This is the header field name (e.g., 'X-Custom-Header') as defined in the HTTPHeader schema.
The value of the HTTP header sent in the liveness probe request.
Path to access on the HTTP server for the liveness probe. Defaults to '/' if not specified.
The TCP port to send the HTTP GET request to. Accepts an integer port number or a named port (string).
The protocol (scheme) used for the HTTP GET request, such as HTTP or HTTPS.
Scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS.
Number of seconds after the container has started before liveness probes are initiated. Defaults to 0.
How often (in seconds) to perform the liveness probe. Defaults to 10 seconds; minimum value is 1.
The minimum number of consecutive successes required for the probe to be considered successful after having failed. For liveness probes, this must be 1. Minimum value is 1.
TCPSocket specifies the TCP socket probe action for the liveness check. It defines the port (and optionally host) that the kubelet will attempt to connect to in order to determine container health.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket check. If not specified, the pod's IP address is used.
The TCP port number to check, either as a numeric value or a name of a port defined in the container. For example, 8080 or 'http'.

The number of seconds to wait for the container to terminate gracefully after sending the termination signal before forcefully killing it. Must be a non-negative integer; 0 means delete immediately. Defaults to 30 seconds if not set.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second, and must be at least 1.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.name: The name of the init container. Must be a valid DNS_LABEL and unique within the pod.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.ports: List of ports exposed by the init container. Each port object can specify the container port number, protocol (TCP or UDP), optional name, and host port mapping.
The port number that the container exposes on its network interface.
The host IP address to bind the container port to on the node. If specified, the container port is accessible only on this IP. Defaults to all interfaces (0.0.0.0) when not set.

The port number on the host node to which the container port is bound. When set, the container can be accessed externally via the node's IP at this port; if unset, the container port is only reachable from within the cluster.
The name of the container port. Must be an IANA_SVC_NAME (up to 15 characters, alphanumeric and hyphens) and unique within the pod. This name can be referenced by services to target this port.
The protocol for the port. Must be UDP, TCP, or SCTP. Defaults to TCP.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.readi: Specifies how kubelet checks the container's readiness. For init containers, this probe is ignored and has no effect.
Exec specifies the action to take, which involves running a command inside the container. The command is an array of strings, with the first element being the command and the rest being arguments.
The command to run inside the container for the readiness check. The probe succeeds if the command exits with status 0.
The number of consecutive failures allowed before the container is marked as unready. Defaults to 3; minimum value is 1.
gRPC specifies the parameters for a gRPC health check used by the readiness probe. It includes the port to check (required) and optionally the service name (defaults to the container's hostname).
The port number of the gRPC service. The probe connects to this port to perform the health check.
The name of the gRPC service to place in the health check request. If empty, the default behavior defined by the gRPC health checking protocol is used.
HTTPGet specifies the HTTP GET request to perform as part of the readiness probe. It defines the request path, port, and optional headers used to check container health.
Host name or IP address to connect to for the HTTP GET probe. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the GET request. Each header is an object with 'name' and 'value' fields.
The name of the HTTP header to set in the request.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the readiness probe request, paired with the corresponding header name.
The HTTP path to request, e.g., /healthz. Defaults to the root path "/" if not specified.
The TCP port number or named port on the container to which the HTTP GET request should be sent. It must be a valid port number (1-65535) or the name of a port defined in the container.
The protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) to use for the HTTP GET request in the readiness probe.
The scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the readiness probe is initiated. Minimum value is 0 (default).
How often (in seconds) to perform the readiness probe. Minimum value is 1; defaults to 10 if not specified.
The minimum number of consecutive successful probe results required for the probe to be considered successful after a failure. For readiness probes, this defaults to 1 and must be at least 1.

Configures a TCP socket probe for the readiness check, which verifies container health by attempting to open a TCP connection to a specified port (and optionally a host). The object defines the port and host for the TCP connection.
The host name to connect to for the TCP socket probe. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
The TCP port to check, specified as a number or a named port defined in the container.
The amount of time in seconds to wait for the container to terminate gracefully after receiving a termination signal, before forcing shutdown. If unset, Kubernetes uses a default of 30 seconds.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second. Must be at least 1.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.resiz: A list of resource resize policies for the container. Each policy specifies a resource name (e.g., cpu, memory) and a restart policy (NotRequired or RestartContainer) that determines whether the container must be restarted when the resource size changes.
The name of the resource (e.g., 'cpu' or 'memory') to which this resize policy applies.

The restart policy for the container when its resources are resized. Valid values are 'NotRequired' (resize can occur without restarting the container) and 'RestartContainer' (the container must be restarted to apply the resize).
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.resou: Compute resources required by the init container, including requests and limits for CPU and memory. The requests field specifies the minimum resources required, and the limits field specifies the maximum resources allowed.
Claims lists the names of resources, defined in spec.resourceClaims, that are used by this container. This is an alpha feature and may change in the future.
The name of the ResourceClaim that this container requires. The claim must be created in the same namespace as the pod before it can be used.

The maximum amount of compute resources (such as cpu and memory) that the init container can use. The map keys are resource names (e.g., 'cpu', 'memory') and the values are Kubernetes quantity strings (e.g., '100m', '1Gi').

A map of resource names (e.g., cpu, memory) to quantities specifying the minimum amount of compute resources required for the init container. If requests are omitted, they default to the container's limits (if set) or an implementation-defined value, and requests cannot exceed limits.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.resta: The list of container exit codes that this restart policy rule matches. Each value is a numeric exit code.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.secur: SecurityContext defines the security options the container should be run with, such as user IDs, SELinux options, capabilities, and read-only root filesystem. If set, the fields of securityContext override the equivalent fields of the PodSecurityContext for this init container.

Controls whether a process can gain more privileges than its parent process. When set to false, the container process is run with the 'no_new_privs' flag, preventing privilege escalation such as setuid or file capabilities.

AppArmorProfile defines the AppArmor profile to be applied to the container. It includes a type (RuntimeDefault, Localhost, or Unconfined) and, when type is Localhost, a localhostProfile field specifying the profile name on the node.
Name of a profile on the node to use. Only relevant when the AppArmor profile type is 'Localhost'.
The type of AppArmor profile to apply. Valid values are `RuntimeDefault`, `Localhost`, and `Unconfined`.
Capabilities to add or drop for the container, given as an object with `add` and `drop` lists of Linux capabilities. This allows fine-grained privilege control for init containers.
Adds the specified Linux capabilities to the container's security context. Each entry is a capability name, e.g., 'NET_ADMIN' or 'SYS_TIME'.
Specifies a list of capabilities to drop from the container's default capability set. Each entry is a Linux capability name (e.g., 'NET_ADMIN').

Indicates whether the init container runs in privileged mode. When true, the container gains elevated permissions, including access to host devices and capabilities, similar to running as root on the host.
Specifies the proc mount type for the container, controlling how the /proc filesystem is exposed within the container.
Indicates whether the container's root filesystem is mounted as read-only. When true, the container cannot write to its root filesystem, enhancing security for init containers.
The GID (group ID) to run the entrypoint of the container process. If not set, the default is the group ID specified in the container image.

Indicates whether the container must run as a non-root user. If true, the kubelet will validate the image at runtime to ensure that it does not run as UID 0 (root) and will fail to start the container if it does.
The UID to run the entrypoint of the init container process. Defaults to the user specified in the image metadata if not set.
SELinux options for the init container. This object specifies the SELinux label (user, role, type, level) that the container's processes will run with.
The SELinux level (MLS/MCS) to apply to the container, such as 's0' or 's0:c1,c2'.
The SELinux role label that applies to the container. This corresponds to the `role` field in Kubernetes' SELinuxOptions.
The SELinux type label applied to the container, e.g., svirt_apache_t. This field is part of the SELinux security context options for the container.
The SELinux user label assigned to the container, which is the user component of the SELinux context (e.g., 'system_u').
seccomp_profile defines the seccomp profile applied to the init container's security context, specifying how system calls are filtered using supported profile types (e.g., RuntimeDefault, Localhost).
The path to the localhost seccomp profile. Used when the seccomp profile type is set to 'Localhost'.
The type of seccomp profile to use. Valid values are: RuntimeDefault, Localhost, and Unconfined. When set to Localhost, the localhostProfile field must also be specified.
WindowsSecurityContextOptions contain Windows-specific options and credentials. This includes settings such as GMSA credentials and runAsUserName for Windows containers.
The path to the GMSA credential spec file. This is used to configure Group Managed Service Accounts (GMSA) for Windows containers in the init container's security context.
The name of the GMSA credential spec to use for the Windows container. This field is part of the Windows security context options for the container.
Indicates whether the container runs as a HostProcess container. When true, the container gains access to the Windows host namespace and resources.
The Windows user name (in the form 'user' or 'domain\user') to run the container's entrypoint process as. If not specified, the default user from the container image metadata is used.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.start: startup_probe is a Kubernetes probe that indicates whether the application in the container is started. If configured, it disables liveness and readiness checks until the startup probe succeeds, ensuring those probes do not interfere with application startup.
Exec specifies the action to take, consisting of a command to be executed inside the container. The probe succeeds if the command exits with status code 0.
Command is the command line to execute inside the container. It is specified as a list of strings; the first element is the command, and the remaining elements are arguments.
failureThreshold is the minimum consecutive failures of the startup probe before it is considered failed. The value must be an integer greater than or equal to 1; the default is 3.
Defines a gRPC action for the startup probe, specifying the port and optional service name to check container health via gRPC.
The port number to connect to for the gRPC health check. Must be a valid TCP port (1-65535).
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default behavior is defined by the gRPC server.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform against the container to check its startup status. The probe succeeds if the response status code is between 200 and 399.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not set. Consider setting the Host header via httpHeaders instead for most use cases.
Specifies custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP request sent by the startup probe. Each entry defines a header name and value.
The name of the HTTP header in a list of headers to send with the probe request.
The value of the HTTP header used in a startup probe's HTTP GET request.
The path to access on the HTTP server for the startup probe's HTTP GET request.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container for the HTTP GET request. Must be a valid integer port number or a named port (as defined in the container's ports).
The network protocol to use for the HTTP request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
Number of seconds after the container starts before the startup probe is initiated. Minimum value is 0 and defaults to 0.
The interval in seconds between successive startup probe checks. Determines how often the kubelet performs the probe on the container.

The minimum consecutive successes required for the startup probe to be considered successful after having failed. Defaults to 1; increasing it requires multiple consecutive successes before the container is marked healthy.
Specifies the TCP socket probe action for the startup probe. The kubelet attempts to open a TCP connection to the specified port to determine container health.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP probe. If omitted, the pod IP address is used.
The TCP port to connect to for the socket probe. Accepts a numeric port (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container.

The number of seconds to wait for the container to terminate gracefully after a startup probe failure, before it is forcibly killed. Overrides the pod-level terminationGracePeriodSeconds for this container.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second; minimum value is 1.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.stdin: Indicates whether the container runtime should allocate a stdin stream for the container. When true, the container's standard input is kept open and available. Defaults to false.
If true, the container's standard input is closed after the first client attaches, preventing subsequent attaches. This requires 'stdin' to be true.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.termi: Path where the container's termination message is written. When the container exits, Kubernetes reads this file to get the termination message. Defaults to /dev/termination-log.

Determines how the container's termination message is captured. Valid values are 'File' (default), which reads from the file specified by terminationMessagePath, and 'Log', which reads from the container's log output.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.tty: Whether this container should allocate a TTY for itself.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.volum: VolumeDevices is the list of block devices to be used by the container. It is used to expose a raw block device to the container.
Path inside the container where the block device will be mounted.
Name of the volume device, which must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's volumes list.
A list of volumes to mount into the init container's filesystem. Each item specifies the volume name and the mount path inside the container.
Path within the container at which the volume should be mounted. Must be an absolute path and must not contain ':'.

Determines how mount propagation works between the host and the container, and between containers sharing the same volume. Allowed values: None (no propagation), HostToContainer (mounts created on the host are visible in the container), and Bidirectional (mounts propagate both ways, requiring privileged containers). Defaults to None.
The name of the volume to mount. Must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec.volumes.
Whether the volume is mounted as read-only. If set to true, the container can only read from the volume, not write to it. Defaults to false.

Indicates whether the read-only mount option is applied recursively to all nested mounts under this volume mount. Must be one of 'Enabled', 'Disabled', or 'IfPossible'. Only supported for volume types that enable recursive mounts, such as CSI volumes.
Specifies a sub-path inside the referenced volume to mount instead of the volume's root. This allows mounting only a subdirectory or file from the volume.
Specifies an alternative to subPath that supports environment variable expansion using $(VAR_NAME) syntax to define the path within the volume to mount.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.worki: The working directory for the init container. If not specified, the container runtime default is used (usually the image's specified working directory). Overrides the image's working directory when set.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.readiness_gates.condi: Specifies the condition type that must be satisfied for the pod to be considered ready. This corresponds to a condition name in the pod's status.conditions, allowing custom readiness conditions beyond the default pod status.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.resource_claims.name: Name of the resource claim. Must be unique within the pod.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.resource_claims.resou: The name of the ResourceClaim object in the same namespace that provides the resource. This references a specific ResourceClaim, and only one of resourceClaimName and resourceClaimTemplateName can be set.
The name of a ResourceClaimTemplate object in the same namespace as the pod. The resource claim is generated from this template, defining the requested resource.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.resources.claims.name: Name of the ResourceClaim object that provides the resources. Must be in the same namespace as the pod.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.scheduling_gates.name: The name of the scheduling gate. Pods are not scheduled until all gates with these names are removed from the pod's spec.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.security_context.sysc: The name of the sysctl parameter to set, for example `kernel.shm_rmid_forced`.
The value to assign to the sysctl setting, expressed as a string.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.tolerations.effect: The taint effect to tolerate. Valid values are 'NoSchedule', 'PreferNoSchedule', and 'NoExecute'. If empty, matches all effects.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.tolerations.key: The taint key that the toleration applies to. An empty key matches all taint keys when the operator is 'Exists'.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.tolerations.operator: The operator represents the relationship between the key and value. Valid values are 'Exists' and 'Equal'. When set to 'Exists', the value should be empty. When set to 'Equal', the value must match the taint value.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.tolerations.toleratio: The number of seconds the pod will tolerate the taint before being evicted, typically used with the NoExecute effect.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.tolerations.value: The taint value the toleration matches. This is used only when the operator is "Equal"; for "Exists" the value must be empty. In the context of a DaemonSet pod spec, it defines which taint value this toleration can tolerate.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.topology_spread_const: A label selector to identify the set of pods that this topology spread constraint applies to. If omitted, the constraint applies to all pods in the namespace.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally a list of values. These expressions are combined with matchLabels to define the label selector for the topology spread constraint.
The label key that the match expression applies to. The expression matches pods with this label key based on the operator and values.
The operator specifies the relationship between the label key and the set of values. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
List of string values that the label key must match when the operator is In or NotIn. Must be empty for Exists and DoesNotExist operators.
A map of label keys to values that the topology spread constraint applies to. Only pods with all specified labels are considered when spreading across the topology domain.

MatchLabelKeys is a set of pod label keys that identifies the pods over which spreading is calculated. If non-empty, the values of these labels from the pod owning this constraint are used to filter the pods matched by the selector; each key must be unique and exist in the pod's labels.
The maximum difference in the number of matching pods between any two topology domains for the workload. Must be greater than zero.

Specifies the minimum number of eligible topology domains that must be used for pod spreading. If the number of eligible domains is less than this value, the global minimum skew is treated as zero when calculating spread.

Specifies how to treat node affinity when calculating pod topology spread skew. Allowed values are "Honor" and "Ignore". When "Honor", nodes with matching node affinity are included; when "Ignore", node affinity is not considered.

Indicates how to handle nodes with taints when calculating pod spread. Accepts 'Honor' to exclude tainted nodes that do not tolerate the pod's tolerations, or 'Ignore' to include all nodes regardless of taints. Defaults to 'Honor'.

The key of node labels. Nodes that have a label with this key and identical values are considered to be in the same topology domain. This key is required for each topology spread constraint and defines how pods are spread across different domains, such as zones or hosts.

Specifies how to handle pods when the topology spread constraint is not satisfied. Allowed values are 'DoNotSchedule' (default), which prevents scheduling, and 'ScheduleAnyway', which schedules the pod regardless.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.aws_elastic_b: Represents an AWS Elastic Block Store volume source that can be mounted into a container within a pod. This field configures the volume to use an AWS EBS volume, allowing persistent storage for the daemon set's pods.
Filesystem type to be used for the AWS EBS volume, such as ext4, xfs, or ntfs. Defaults to ext4 if unspecified.
The partition number of the AWS EBS volume to mount. If specified, only that partition is mounted; otherwise, the entire volume is used.
Indicates whether the AWS Elastic Block Store volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false; set to true to prevent writes.
The unique ID of the AWS EBS volume to mount.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.azure_disk: Configures an Azure Disk volume to be mounted into the pod. This is a volume source that references an Azure Data Disk and contains settings for the disk mount.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.azure_disk.ca: Specifies the caching mode for the Azure disk volume. Allowed values are None, ReadOnly, and ReadWrite; defaults to None if not specified.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.azure_disk.di: The name of the Azure data disk to attach to the pod. Must be the name of an existing Azure disk in the same location as the cluster.
The URI of the Azure blob storage disk to mount. Must be specified when using a blob-based disk, in the format https://<account>.blob.core.windows.net/<container>/<vhd-name>.vhd.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.azure_disk.fs: Filesystem type to mount (e.g., ext4, xfs). Defaults to ext4.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.azure_disk.ki: The kind of Azure Data Disk. Allowed values are 'Shared', 'Dedicated', and 'Managed'. Defaults to 'Shared'.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.azure_disk.re: Mounts the Azure disk as read-only when set to true. Defaults to false (read/write).
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.azure_file: Represents an Azure File volume source, which mounts an Azure File share into the pod. This configuration typically requires a secret name with Azure storage credentials and a share name, and optionally supports read-only mounting.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.azure_file.re: Indicates whether the Azure file share should be mounted read-only. If set to true, the volume is mounted read-only; otherwise it is mounted read-write. Defaults to false.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.azure_file.se: The name of the secret that contains the Azure Storage account name and key, used to authenticate to the Azure file share.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.azure_file.sh: The name of the Azure File share that should be mounted. This corresponds to the shareName field in the Kubernetes azureFile volume source.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.cephfs: Defines a CephFS volume source, used to mount a Ceph Filesystem into the pod. Contains configuration such as monitors, path, user, and secret references.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.cephfs.monito: List of Ceph monitor addresses (hostnames or IPs) for the CephFS volume. Required to connect to the Ceph cluster.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.cephfs.path: Path within the CephFS filesystem to mount into the pod.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.cephfs.read_o: Specifies whether the CephFS volume is mounted as read-only. If true, the volume is read-only; if false (or omitted), it is read-write.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.cephfs.secret: Path to the Ceph keyring file on the host, used for authentication with the Ceph cluster. Either this or secret_ref is required to provide credentials.

secretRef is an optional reference to a Kubernetes Secret that contains the Ceph credentials (keyring) for accessing the CephFS filesystem. The secret must be in the same namespace as the pod; if not specified, Ceph uses the default keyring.
The name of the Kubernetes secret that provides the CephFS credentials.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.cephfs.user: The CephFS user to use when mounting the volume. If unset, defaults to 'admin'.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.cinder: Represents a Cinder volume in OpenStack. Used to attach a Cinder volume to the pod for persistent storage.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.cinder.fs_typ: Filesystem type to mount for the Cinder volume. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system, e.g., ext4, xfs, ntfs. If not specified, ext4 is typically inferred.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.cinder.read_o: Specifies whether the Cinder volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false (read/write). If true, forces the read-only setting in volume mounts.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.cinder.secret: secret_ref is a reference to a Kubernetes secret that contains the authentication credentials (username and password) for the Cinder volume. It is an object with a 'name' field specifying the name of the secret in the same namespace.
The name of the Kubernetes Secret object that contains authentication credentials for the Cinder volume.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.cinder.volume: The unique ID of the Cinder volume to be mounted. This is a required field for Cinder volume sources.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.config_map: config_map configures a volume sourced from a Kubernetes ConfigMap. It specifies the name of the ConfigMap to reference and optionally defines which items (keys) to project as files, including their paths and permissions.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.config_map.de: Sets the default file permission mode (in octal) for all files in the ConfigMap volume. When unspecified, the default is 0644.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.config_map.it: Maps keys from the ConfigMap to specific file paths and optional mode. If unspecified, all keys are projected as files. If specified, only the listed keys are projected, with custom paths and permissions.
The key to select from the ConfigMap's data. The value corresponding to this key will be exposed at the defined path within the volume.
Mode bits used to set permissions on this file, expressed as an octal integer (e.g., 0644).
The relative path of the file within the volume where the value from the corresponding config map key is written.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.config_map.na: Name of the ConfigMap to reference for this volume. The volume will be populated with data from the specified ConfigMap.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.config_map.op: Optional specifies whether the ConfigMap or its keys must be defined. If true, the volume will not fail if the ConfigMap is missing or if any of the specified keys are absent.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.csi: Represents a volume that is provisioned and mounted using a Container Storage Interface (CSI) driver. This configuration includes the driver's name, the volume handle, filesystem type, read-only setting, and any driver-specific volume attributes.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.csi.driver: The name of the CSI driver that manages the volume. This must match the name of a CSI driver installed on the cluster.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.csi.fs_type: Filesystem type to mount for the CSI volume (e.g., ext4, xfs). If omitted, the CSI driver's default filesystem type is used.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.csi.node_publ: A reference to a Secret containing credentials or configuration required by the CSI driver for the node publish (or unpublish) operation. It is optional and typically specified when the driver requires additional secrets at node stage/publish time.
The name of the secret. This secret is referenced for the CSI node publish operation.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.csi.read_only: Indicates if the CSI volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.csi.volume_at: volumeAttributes are arbitrary attributes of the volume that are passed to the external CSI volume driver.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.downward_api: Configures a Downward API volume that exposes pod metadata (such as labels, annotations, and other fields) to the container as files. This allows containers to read information about themselves without using the Kubernetes API.
The default permissions mode (in octal) for files created by the downward API volume. Must be a value between 0 and 0777; defaults to 0644. This setting does not affect directories.
items specifies the list of downward API volume files. Each item defines a file path and a field reference (fieldRef or resourceFieldRef) to expose.

Selects a field of the pod to expose via the downward API volume. Supported fields include metadata.name, metadata.namespace, metadata.labels, metadata.annotations, spec.nodeName, spec.serviceAccountName, status.hostIP, status.podIP, and status.podIPs.
Version of the schema the field_path is written in terms of. Typically the Kubernetes API version, e.g., 'v1'.
The path to the pod field whose value is exposed to the container via the downward API volume, e.g., metadata.name or metadata.namespace.
The file permission mode, represented as an octal number (e.g., 0644). If not specified, the default mode is 0644.
Path is the file path within the downward API volume where the field value will be written. It is relative to the volume's mount point and must not contain '..'.
Selects a resource field of a container (e.g., limits.cpu or requests.memory) to expose to the downward API volume item.
The name of the container to which the resource field reference applies, used to expose that container's resource limits or requests via the downward API.
The divisor for the resource value, used to scale the quantity (e.g., CPU time). Must be a Quantity string (e.g., '1m', '1Ki'), defaults to '1'.
The name of the container resource to expose, such as 'requests.cpu' or 'limits.memory'.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.empty_dir: Represents an emptyDir volume, a temporary directory created empty when the pod is assigned to a node and deleted when the pod is removed. It provides scratch space that does not persist across pod restarts and is shared by all containers in the pod.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.empty_dir.med: Specifies the storage medium for the emptyDir volume. An empty string (default) uses the node's default storage (disk), 'Memory' uses a RAM-backed tmpfs filesystem, and 'HugePages' uses the Linux huge pages filesystem.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.empty_dir.siz: The maximum size of the emptyDir volume, specified as a Kubernetes quantity (e.g., '1Gi'). If unset, the volume is limited by the node's storage.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.ephemeral: Represents an ephemeral volume that is created with the pod and deleted when the pod is removed. This field can be used to define a volume from a generic ephemeral volume or a CSI ephemeral volume.
kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.ephemeral.vol: Defines the PersistentVolumeClaim template that is used to create a PVC for this ephemeral volume. The template specifies the desired characteristics of the PVC, such as storage class, access modes, and resources.
Metadata for the PersistentVolumeClaim created by this ephemeral volume claim template, used to set labels, annotations, and optionally a name for the PVC.

Annotations is a map of string keys and values that attaches arbitrary non-identifying metadata to the volume claim template. This is commonly used to store tooling information or other custom metadata without affecting selection.
The timestamp, in RFC3339 format, indicating when the persistent volume claim generated from this template was created. This field is set by the server and cannot be set by clients.
In Kubernetes ObjectMeta, this field specifies the duration in seconds before the object should be deleted. It is set when a graceful deletion is requested and must be a non-negative integer.

The deletionTimestamp is set when the object is marked for deletion, indicating the time at which it will be (or was) removed, in RFC3339 format. In this context, it applies to the PersistentVolumeClaims generated from the volume claim template.
A list of finalizers for this object. Finalizers are strings that must be removed before the object can be deleted, ensuring pre-delete operations complete.

generateName is an optional prefix used by the API server to generate a unique name if the name field is not provided. The generated name will be the prefix plus a random suffix, and the server handles uniqueness conflicts automatically.
A sequence number representing a specific generation of the desired state. Populated by the system. Read-only.
Labels to assign to the volume claim template's metadata. These labels are applied to the persistent volume claim created from this template, allowing selection and identification of the claim.

A list of ManagedFieldsEntry objects that track the field management operations affecting this metadata. Each entry records the manager, operation, API version, and managed fields (e.g., for server-side apply).

The API version of the resource that the manager used to manage these fields. This is part of the managedFields metadata entry, indicating which API version the managing controller or agent operated with.
FieldsType is the type of the managed fields entry, indicating the serialization format of the FieldsV1 member. For the Kubernetes API, this is typically set to 'FieldsV1'.
This field contains a JSON representation of the managed fields for this entry, encoding which fields are managed by the manager in the v1 format.

The name of the manager (e.g., kubectl, a controller, or an operator) that last applied or updated this managed field. In Kubernetes, each managedFields entry tracks which component owns the fields it manages, and this string identifies that component.
The operation type of the managed field entry, indicating whether the field was applied or updated. Supported values are 'Apply' and 'Update'.

The name of the subresource used to update the object, or empty string if the update was through the main resource. Distinguishes managers even if they share the same name; for example, 'status' for status subresource updates.
Timestamp of when the operation recorded in this managed fields entry was performed.
The metadata name for the volume claim template. This name is not used for the resulting PersistentVolumeClaim; the system generates the PVC name from the pod name and volume name.
The namespace for the volume claim template. For ephemeral volumes, this field must be empty because the resulting PersistentVolumeClaim is always created in the same namespace as the pod.

List of references to the owning objects. Each entry includes fields such as apiVersion, kind, name, uid, and optionally controller and blockOwnerDeletion to specify ownership relationships for garbage collection.
The API version of the owner (referent) object, e.g. 'apps/v1'. This is used together with kind and name to identify the owning object.

Whether this owner reference blocks deletion of the dependent object. If true, the dependent (the volume claim template's metadata) cannot be deleted by the Kubernetes garbage collector until the owner is deleted.
Indicates whether the referenced owner is the managing controller of the object.
The Kubernetes resource kind of the owner object referenced by this owner reference, such as 'DaemonSet'.
The name of the owner object that this reference points to. This corresponds to the metadata.name of the referenced resource.
The UID of the owner object referenced by this OwnerReference. It uniquely identifies the referenced resource in the Kubernetes API.
The resource version of the object, used for optimistic concurrency. This value is set by the server and should not be modified by clients.
