Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform for the startup probe. The request targets the container's IP address and includes configurable host, port, path, and HTTP headers.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
List of custom HTTP headers to attach to the probe request. Each item defines a header name and value to send with the GET request.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the probe request, e.g., X-Custom-Header.
The value of the HTTP header. This is the value associated with the header name in the startup probe's HTTP GET request.
The HTTP path to request on the server. Defaults to '/'.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container during the HTTP GET probe. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535, or the name of a container port.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'; defaults to 'HTTP'.
The URI scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS; defaults to HTTP.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the startup probe is initiated. Defaults to 0 if unspecified.
How often (in seconds) to perform the startup probe. Defaults to 10, and the minimum allowed value is 1.

The number of consecutive successful probe checks required for the startup probe to be considered successful. For startup probes, Kubernetes requires this value to be exactly 1, as a startup probe must succeed on the first check after failure.
The TCP socket check for this startup probe. If the specified port is accepting connections, the probe is considered successful.
Optional host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket health check. If not set, defaults to the pod IP.
The TCP port to connect to for the startup probe. Can be a numeric port (specified as a string) or a named port defined in the container.
The number of seconds the pod is allowed to terminate gracefully before being forcefully killed. Must be a non-negative integer; defaults to 30 seconds.
Number of seconds after which the startup probe times out. If the probe does not finish within this period, it is considered failed.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.containers.stdin: Indicates whether the container runtime should allocate a stdin stream for the container. If set to true, the container can read from standard input.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.containers.stdin_once: If true, the container's standard input is opened on container start, remains empty until the first client attaches, then stays open until the client disconnects, at which point it is closed and remains closed until the container restarts. This field only has effect when stdin is also true.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.containers.terminatio: The path where the container's termination message is written. Defaults to /dev/termination-log.

termination_message_policy sets how the container's termination message is read by kubelet. Valid values are 'File' (default), which reads the message from the file specified by terminationMessagePath, and 'FallbackToLogsOnError', which falls back to the container logs if the message file is empty.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.containers.tty: Indicates whether the container should allocate a pseudo-TTY. Set to true to enable interactive terminal access to the container.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.containers.volume_dev: List of volume devices to expose to the container, allowing raw block device access. Each entry specifies a device path and the name of a volume with the 'block' volume mode.
Path within the container where the volume device is mounted.
The name of the volume that this block device mounts, corresponding to a volume defined in the pod's volumes list.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.containers.volume_mou: List of volumes to mount into the container's filesystem. Each item specifies a volume name, a mount path within the container, and optionally read-only access and sub-path.
The path inside the container at which the volume will be mounted. This is where the volume's data appears in the container's filesystem.
Controls whether and how mounts are propagated between the host and the container. Allowed values: None, HostToContainer, Bidirectional.
Name of the volume to mount. Must correspond to the name of a volume defined in the pod spec.
If true, the volume mount is read-only. If false (default), the volume is mounted read-write.
Path within the volume from which the container's volume mount is mounted.

subPathExpr is similar to subPath, but supports environment variable references using $(VAR_NAME) syntax. It allows dynamically selecting a path within the volume based on container environment variables.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.containers.working_di: The container's working directory. If not specified, the container runtime default is used. Must be an absolute path.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.dns_config.options.na: The name of the DNS resolver option, such as 'ndots', 'timeout', 'attempts', or other valid resolv.conf options.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.dns_config.options.va: The value for the DNS resolver option specified in the name field. This is optional; some options may not require a value.
List of arguments to pass to the container's entrypoint. These override the default arguments provided in the container image.
The command to run in this ephemeral container, overriding the container image's entrypoint. If not provided, the image's default entrypoint is used.
List of environment variables to set in the ephemeral container. Each item defines a variable name and optionally its value or value source (e.g., secret or config map reference).
The name of the environment variable. Must be a valid C identifier (e.g., starts with a letter or underscore, followed by alphanumeric characters or underscores).
Value of the environment variable. This field is optional if 'valueFrom' is specified.
Specifies an optional source for the environment variable's value, such as a ConfigMap, Secret, field reference, or resource field reference. Only one of value or valueFrom may be specified.
Selects a key of a ConfigMap in the pod's namespace.
The key of the ConfigMap entry to select.
Name of the ConfigMap being referenced.
Specifies whether the ConfigMap or its key must be defined. If set to true, a missing ConfigMap or key does not prevent container startup; the value is treated as unset.
Selects a field of the pod (e.g., metadata.name, metadata.namespace, spec.nodeName, status.podIP) and injects its value into the environment variable.
The API version of the schema that fieldPath is written in terms of. Defaults to 'v1' if not specified.
The path of the field to select. For example, metadata.name or metadata.namespace.
Selects a resource field (e.g., limits.cpu, requests.memory) from the container's resource specification to expose as an environment variable.
The name of the container to select the resource field from. If omitted, the pod's default container is used.
Divisor for the resource field value. The resource value is divided by this quantity, which must be a valid Kubernetes quantity (e.g., '1', '100m'); defaults to 1.
The name of the resource to select, such as 'limits.cpu' or 'requests.memory'.
Selects a key from a Kubernetes Secret to populate the environment variable's value. The Secret must exist in the same namespace unless the optional flag is set to true.
The key of the secret to select from. Must be a valid key in the referenced Secret.
The name of the Secret from which the key is selected.

Specifies whether the Secret or its key must be defined. When set to true, the reference is optional and the container can start even if the Secret or key is missing; the environment variable is omitted. When false (default), the referenced Secret must exist.
env_from specifies a list of sources (ConfigMap or Secret) whose key-value pairs are injected as environment variables into the ephemeral container.
Reference to a ConfigMap that populates environment variables in the container. The referenced ConfigMap must exist in the same namespace as the Pod.
The name of the ConfigMap to reference. This ConfigMap's data is used to populate environment variables for the container.
Indicates whether the referenced ConfigMap must be defined. If true, a missing ConfigMap is ignored; if false, the container fails to start when the ConfigMap is absent.

An optional prefix that is prepended to each key in the referenced ConfigMap or Secret when converting it to environment variable names. Keys are uppercased and invalid characters are replaced with underscores before the prefix is applied.
secretRef is a reference to a Secret in the same namespace as the Pod. The data of the referenced Secret is exposed as environment variables via envFrom.
Name of the Secret to use. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Specifies whether the referenced Secret must be defined. If set to true, the Secret is optional and its absence will not prevent the container from starting.
The container image to use for the ephemeral container.
The image pull policy for the ephemeral container. Valid values are Always, IfNotPresent, and Never. Defaults to Always if the image tag is 'latest', otherwise IfNotPresent.
Lifecycle defines lifecycle hooks for the ephemeral container, including postStart and preStop handlers that execute at container startup and shutdown, respectively.
post_start is a lifecycle hook that runs immediately after the ephemeral container is started. It defines a handler (exec, httpGet, or tcpSocket) to perform actions at container start.
The exec-based lifecycle handler, which defines a command to run inside the ephemeral container after it starts, as part of the post-start hook.
The command to run inside the container for the post-start lifecycle exec hook, specified as a list of strings where the first element is the command and the remaining elements are arguments.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform on the container's lifecycle post-start hook. The hook is considered successful if the request returns an HTTP status code between 200 and 399.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP.
Specifies custom HTTP headers to send with the GET request. Each header object contains 'name' and 'value' fields.
The HTTP header field name, e.g., 'Authorization' or 'Content-Type'.
The value of the HTTP header for the postStart lifecycle hook's HTTP GET request.
The path to access on the HTTP server for the HTTP GET request in the post-start lifecycle hook.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container for the HTTP GET request. It can be a numeric port (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container.
Specifies the protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) to use for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to HTTP.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.

Specifies a sleep action to be executed as part of the postStart lifecycle hook. The sleep action pauses execution for a set number of seconds, allowing the container to delay subsequent hook completion.
The number of seconds to sleep as part of the postStart lifecycle hook's sleep action.
Specifies a TCP socket action to be performed as part of the post-start lifecycle hook. This includes checking that a TCP socket is listening on the given port (with optional host).
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket action. If not specified, the pod IP address is used.
Specifies the port number to connect to on the container for the TCP socket. Can be a numeric port (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container.
The pre_stop block configures the preStop lifecycle hook, which is invoked immediately before a container is terminated, allowing for graceful shutdown or cleanup operations.

Exec specifies the command to be run inside the container as the preStop lifecycle hook handler. It represents the ExecAction, which executes a command to perform cleanup or graceful shutdown before the container is terminated.

Command is the command line to execute inside the container, specified as an array of strings. The first element is the command, and remaining elements are arguments. If omitted, the container's default command is used.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform as the pre-stop lifecycle action. The action succeeds if the request returns a 2xx status code.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the GET request. Each header should specify a header name and value.
Specifies the name of an HTTP header to include in the preStop HTTP GET request.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request.
Path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/'. For example, '/healthz'.
Port number or name to access for the HTTP GET request. Can be a numeric port or a named port defined in the container.
The protocol (scheme) used for the HTTP GET request, such as HTTP or HTTPS.
The scheme to use for the HTTP request, either HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP.
Specifies a sleep action for the pre-stop hook, which delays the container's termination by a specified number of seconds to allow graceful shutdown.
The number of seconds the container sleeps before termination, used by the sleep action in the preStop lifecycle hook.
Represents a TCP socket action, defined by a port and optional host, that Kubernetes performs when the pre-stop lifecycle hook is triggered.
The host name to connect to for the TCP socket action. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP.
The TCP port to connect to. Accepts a port number (1-65535) or a named port (IANA_SVC_NAME).
Exec specifies a command to run inside the container for the liveness probe. The probe succeeds if the command exits with status 0, and fails on any non-zero exit code.
Command to execute inside the container for the liveness probe. The first element is the command, and any remaining elements are arguments passed to it.
Minimum consecutive failures for the liveness probe to be considered failed after having succeeded. Defaults to 3; minimum value is 1.
Specifies the gRPC probe configuration for the liveness probe. This probe performs a gRPC health check on the container, requiring a port and optionally a service name.
The port number to send the gRPC health check request to. Must be a valid TCP port (1-65535).
The name of the gRPC service to check. If not specified, the default is an empty string, which means the gRPC server's default health check is used.
The HTTP GET action to perform for the liveness probe. It configures a request to a specific port and path to determine container liveness.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP.
Custom headers to set in the HTTP GET request for the liveness probe. Each header object contains a name and a value.
The header field name for the HTTP header sent in the liveness probe's HTTP GET request. For example, 'Accept' or 'Authorization'.
The value of the HTTP header to be sent in the liveness probe request.
The HTTP path to request on the server for the liveness probe. Defaults to '/'.
The port to access on the container. This is a string that can be an integer port number or the name of a port defined in the container's ports. Valid port numbers range from 1 to 65535.
Protocol for the HTTP request. Must be either 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The URI scheme to use for the HTTP request. Valid values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP' if not specified.
Number of seconds after the container has started before liveness probes are initiated. Must be a non-negative integer (default 0).
The frequency in seconds at which the liveness probe is performed. A higher value means less frequent checks.
Minimum consecutive successes for the probe to be considered successful after having failed. For liveness probes, this value must be 1.
Specifies a TCP socket probe action, which checks the container's health by attempting to open a TCP connection to the port defined in the `port` field of this object.
The host name to connect to for the TCP socket liveness probe. If not specified, it defaults to the pod IP.

The TCP port number to connect to when performing the liveness probe. This can be a numeric port (e.g., '8080') or a named port defined in the container's ports, and must be in the range 1-65535 if numeric.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second. Minimum value is 1.
The name of the ephemeral container. Must be unique within the pod.
List of ports to expose from the container. For ephemeral containers, this field is not allowed and specifying it will be rejected by the API server.
The port number that the container listens on, used to expose the container's service.
The host IP address to bind the port to. Defaults to 0.0.0.0 if not specified.

The port number on the host node that maps to the container port for this ephemeral container. If specified, the container's port is exposed directly on the host's network at this port. Valid range is 1-65535.

The optional name of the container port. Must be a valid IANA_SVC_NAME (up to 15 characters, lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens, not starting or ending with a hyphen). This name can be used to reference the port in other Kubernetes resources, such as services.
The network protocol for this port. Supported values are TCP, UDP, and SCTP; defaults to TCP.
Exec specifies the command to run inside the container for the readiness probe. A successful probe (exit code 0) indicates the container is ready.

The command to run inside the container for the exec readiness probe. It is a list of strings representing the command and its arguments, executed directly without a shell unless the first element is '/bin/sh' or similar. The working directory is root ('/') in the container's filesystem, and the command runs as the container's default user (subject to securityContext overrides).
The number of consecutive failures of the readiness probe before the container is considered not ready. Once the probe fails this many times, the container is removed from service endpoints.
Specifies the gRPC action for the probe, configuring a gRPC health check against the container. It includes parameters such as the port to query (required) and an optional service name.
The port number of the gRPC server to connect to. Required when using a gRPC probe.
Specifies the name of the gRPC service to query for health status. If empty, the health check applies to the entire gRPC server.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to check container readiness. Includes settings such as the path, port, HTTP headers, and scheme.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP.
Optional list of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each header is an object with 'name' and 'value' fields.
Name of the HTTP header to include in the probe request, e.g., 'Authorization'.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the readiness probe request. This is paired with the corresponding header name in the httpHeaders list.
The HTTP path to request when performing the readiness probe. For example, '/healthz'.
The port number or name of the port on the container to connect to for the HTTP GET request. This accepts a numeric value as a string or a named port defined in the container.
The protocol (scheme) used for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the readiness probe is initiated. Defaults to 0.
How often (in seconds) to perform the readiness probe. Defaults to 10 seconds; the minimum value is 1.
Minimum consecutive successes required for the probe to be considered successful after having failed. Defaults to 1. For readiness probes, this value must be 1.
Specifies a TCP socket check for the readiness probe. The kubelet attempts to open a TCP connection to the container on the specified port to determine if the container is ready.
Optional host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket probe. If not specified, the pod IP is used.
The TCP socket port to probe on the container. It can be a numeric port or a named port defined in the container's ports.
Optional number of seconds the pod will wait after receiving a termination signal before it is forcefully terminated. Defaults to 30 seconds if not specified.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second. Minimum value is 1.
List of resource resize policies for the ephemeral container, defining which resources (CPU, memory) can be resized and the restart behavior if a resize fails.
The name of the resource (e.g., cpu or memory) to which this resize policy applies, as part of the Kubernetes ephemeral container resize policy.
Specifies the restart policy when a container's resource is resized. Allowed values are 'NotRequired' and 'RestartContainer'.
Resource requirements for the ephemeral container, defining requests and limits for compute resources such as CPU and memory.

Claims lists the names of resources, defined in spec.resourceClaims, that are used by this ephemeral container. This is an alpha field and requires enabling the DynamicResourceAllocation feature gate.
The name of the ResourceClaim this container references. The ResourceClaim must exist in the same namespace as the pod.

Limits specifies the maximum amount of compute resources allowed for the ephemeral container. Each key is a resource name (e.g., cpu, memory) and the corresponding value is a quantity string (e.g., '100m', '1Gi').

Requests is a map of resource names to quantities, specifying the minimum amount of each resource the ephemeral container needs. For example, 'cpu: 100m' and 'memory: 128Mi'. The keys are standard Kubernetes resource names (cpu, memory, hugepages, etc.) and the values are strings in Kubernetes quantity format.
Specifies the restart policy for the ephemeral container. Allowed values are Always, OnFailure, and Never. Defaults to Always if not set.
A list of integer exit codes that define which container terminations this restart policy rule applies to. If a container exits with one of these codes, the restart policy rule is followed.

SecurityContext holds security configuration for the ephemeral container, including parameters like runAsUser, runAsGroup, capabilities, SELinux options, and whether the root filesystem is read-only. It controls the container's access to the host and privileges at runtime.

AllowPrivilegeEscalation controls whether a process can gain more privileges than its parent process. When set to false, the container's processes are prevented from gaining additional privileges (e.g., via setuid or setgid binaries).
Configures AppArmor for the container. Defines the profile type (RuntimeDefault, Localhost, Unconfined) and optionally references a profile on the node.
The name of the AppArmor profile to be loaded from the node's localhost, used only when the profile type is 'Localhost'.

Type of AppArmor profile to use. Allowed values are 'Localhost' (use the profile specified in localhostProfile), 'RuntimeDefault' (use the container runtime's default AppArmor profile), and 'Unconfined' (disable AppArmor enforcement).
Capabilities to add or drop for the ephemeral container's process. The object contains 'add' and 'drop' lists of Linux capabilities.
The list of Linux capabilities to add to the container's security context. Valid entries are Linux capability names like CAP_NET_ADMIN or CAP_SYS_TIME.
The list of capabilities to drop from the container's permitted capabilities. For example, can drop 'NET_ADMIN' or 'SYS_TIME'.
Specifies whether the container runs in privileged mode. When true, the container has access to all devices on the host and essentially runs as root on the host.

Sets the proc mount type for the ephemeral container. Allowed values are 'Default' and 'Unmasked'; 'Unmasked' removes the masking of /proc to expose all host proc information, while 'Default' applies the standard restrictions.
Mounts the container's root filesystem as read-only. When set to true, the root filesystem cannot be modified, enhancing security by preventing unauthorized changes to container filesystem content.
The GID (group ID) to run the container's entrypoint process with. If omitted, defaults to the container image's group ID.

Indicates that the container must run as a non-root user. If true, the kubelet will validate the image at runtime to ensure that it does not run as UID 0 (root) and will fail to start the container if it does.
The UID (user ID) that the container's entrypoint process will run as. Defaults to the user specified in the container image if not set. Must be a non-negative integer.
SELinux options for the ephemeral container, specifying the level, role, type, and user as part of its security context.
Level is the SELinux level label that applies to the container. For example, s0:c123,c456.
The SELinux role label that applies to the container. It defines the role portion of the SELinux context, such as 'system_r'.
The SELinux type label that applies to the container. This specifies the SELinux type, such as 'container_t'.
The SELinux user label for the container.
SeccompProfile configures the seccomp profile for this ephemeral container. It can specify a runtime default, unconfined, or a localhost profile via its type and localhostProfile fields.

localhostProfile indicates a profile defined in a file on the node should be used. The profile must be preconfigured on the node to work. Must be a descending path, relative to the kubelet's configured seccomp profile location. Must only be set if type is 'Localhost'.
The type of seccomp profile to use. Allowed values are RuntimeDefault, Unconfined, and Localhost.
Windows-specific security options for the container. Configures settings such as GMSA credentials, host process, and the Windows user name.
The name of the GMSA credential spec to use for the container, enabling Windows GMSA authentication.
The name of the GMSA credential spec to use for the Windows container, as defined in the Kubernetes Windows security context options.
HostProcess determines if a container should be run as a HostProcess container. All containers in the pod must have the same value, and the default is false.
The username in Windows to run the entrypoint of the container process. Defaults to the user specified in image metadata if unspecified.

Configures a startup probe for the ephemeral container. This probe determines when the container has started successfully; until it succeeds, liveness and readiness probes are not activated, and if it fails, the container is restarted according to its restart policy. Useful for slow-starting containers.
Exec specifies a command to run inside the container for the startup probe. The probe is considered successful if the command exits with status 0; any other exit code indicates a failure.

Command line to execute inside the container for the startup probe. The working directory is '/' in the container's filesystem. The command is executed directly, not via a shell, so shell constructs like pipes are not supported.
Minimum consecutive failures for the startup probe to be considered failed after having succeeded. Defaults to 3. Minimum value is 1.
grpc specifies a gRPC health check to perform against the container. It is an object containing the port to check and, optionally, the service name.
The port number on which the gRPC server is listening. Must be a valid TCP port (1-65535). This field is required for a gRPC probe.
Specifies the name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default behavior is defined by gRPC.
Configures an HTTP GET request that the startup probe performs against the container. This is an object containing the host, port, path, and optional HTTP headers for the request.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the HTTP GET request. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP.
List of custom HTTP headers to send with the probe request. Each item specifies a header name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to send in the HTTP request.
The value of the HTTP header. This string is sent as the header's value when the probe performs the HTTP request.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server when performing a GET request. Defaults to '/' if not specified.
The port to send the HTTP request to. Accepts either a numeric port (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container.
Protocol for the HTTP GET request. Must be HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP if not specified.
The scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP, and valid values are HTTP and HTTPS.
The number of seconds after the container has started before the startup probe is initiated. Defaults to 0; minimum value is 0.
How often, in seconds, to perform the startup probe. Minimum value is 1; default is 10.
The minimum consecutive successes required for the startup probe to be considered successful after having failed. Defaults to 1 and must be 1 for startup probes.
Configures a TCP socket checker for the startup probe. It defines the port (and optionally host) to check for TCP connectivity, indicating the container has started.
Host name to connect to for the TCP socket probe. If not specified, the pod IP is used.
Number or name of the port to access on the container. The number must be in the range 1 to 65535, or a name must be a valid IANA_SVC_NAME.
The number of seconds after which the startup probe times out. Defaults to 1 second. Minimum value is 1.
Whether this ephemeral container should have a stdin stream allocated for it. When true, the container runtime allocates a stdin channel, enabling interactive access. Defaults to false.

If true, the container runtime closes the stdin channel after the first attach session disconnects, and stdin remains closed until the container is restarted. When false, stdin remains open across multiple attach sessions if stdin is enabled. Defaults to false.
The name of the target container within the pod that this ephemeral container shares its process namespace with. If not specified, the last started container is used.
Path at which the container's termination message is written, used to record the reason for container termination. Defaults to /dev/termination-log.
Provides the policy for how the termination message of the ephemeral container is captured—either from the termination message file or through container logs under error conditions.
Indicates whether a TTY (pseudo-TTY) should be allocated for the ephemeral container. When true, the container will have a terminal attached, enabling interactive sessions.
List of block devices to be used by the ephemeral container. Each item defines the name of a volume and the device path inside the container.
The path inside the container where the volume device is mounted. This is required when specifying a volume device for an ephemeral container.
The name of the volume to use. Must match the name of a volume defined in the pod spec.
List of volume mounts for an ephemeral container. Each item specifies a volume to mount into the container's filesystem, including mount path and read-only options.
Path within the ephemeral container at which the volume should be mounted. Must be an absolute path, e.g., /data.

mount_propagation controls how volume mounts are propagated from the host to the container and between containers. Valid values are None (default), HostToContainer, and Bidirectional. It affects the visibility of mounts in the container.
The name of the volume to mount. This must match the name of a volume defined in the pod spec.
Specifies whether the volume is mounted as read-only. When true, the container can only read from the volume; default is false (read-write).
Configures recursive read-only mounts for this volume mount. Allowed values: Enabled, IfPossible, Disabled.
Path within the volume from which the container's volume is mounted. Defaults to the volume's root if empty.
Specifies the path within the volume to mount, with support for environment variable expansion using $(VAR_NAME) syntax, similar to subPath but allowing dynamic paths.
The working directory for the ephemeral container. If not specified, the container runtime uses the default working directory defined in the container image.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.host_aliases.hostname: The list of hostnames that resolve to the IP address specified in this hostAliases entry. Kubernetes adds these hostnames to the /etc/hosts file of the container.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.host_aliases.ip: The IP address to which the hostnames in this hostAliases entry should resolve.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.image_pull_secrets.na: The name of the image pull secret. Must correspond to a Secret in the same namespace as the pod.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.init_containers.args: Arguments to the command that this init container runs. These are passed to the container's entrypoint process.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.init_containers.comma: The entrypoint array for the init container, overriding the image's ENTRYPOINT. This is a list of strings, e.g., ['/bin/sh', '-c'].
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.init_containers.env: List of environment variables to set in the container. Each item defines a variable name and optionally a value or a source for the value (e.g., config map, secret, or field reference).
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.init_containers.env.n: The name of the environment variable. Must be a valid C identifier (e.g., MY_VAR).
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.init_containers.env.v: The value to set for the environment variable.

Specifies a source for the environment variable's value. It allows referencing a ConfigMap key, Secret key, a field of the pod (e.g., metadata.name), or a resource (e.g., limits.cpu). Only one of configMapKeyRef, secretKeyRef, fieldRef, or resourceFieldRef can be set.
Selects a key from a ConfigMap to populate the value of the environment variable. The object contains the ConfigMap name and the key to retrieve.
The key to select from the referenced ConfigMap.
The name of the ConfigMap being referenced. Must match a ConfigMap name in the same namespace.
Optional specifies whether the ConfigMap or its key must be defined. Defaults to false, meaning the key must exist.
Selects a field of the pod (e.g., metadata.name, status.podIP, spec.nodeName) to use as the value of the environment variable. The specific field path is provided in the nested fieldPath property.
Version of the schema the FieldPath is written in terms of, defaults to 'v1'.
Path of the field to select from the pod spec, such as 'metadata.name' or 'spec.nodeName'.
Indicates whether the referenced file key is optional. If true, the container can start even when the key does not exist; if false, the key must be present.
The name of the volume that contains the file referenced by the file key reference. This volume must be defined in the same pod's volume list.
ResourceFieldRef selects a resource field of the container, such as limits.cpu or requests.memory, for use as the value of the environment variable.
The name of the container for which to select a resource. If omitted, defaults to the container where this environment variable is defined.

Divisor is the divisor for the resource value in a resource field reference. It specifies the scaling factor applied to the selected resource quantity (e.g., '1' yields the raw value, '1k' divides by 1000, '1Mi' divides by 1,048,576). Defaults to '1'.

The resource name to select from the pod's resource specification, such as 'requests.cpu' or 'limits.memory'. This is used in a resource field ref to populate the environment variable's value from a container resource.

Selects a key of a Secret in the pod's namespace. This is a SecretKeySelector object that specifies the Secret name and key to use, and may include an 'optional' flag to control behavior when the Secret or key is missing.
The key name within the referenced Secret to retrieve the value from. Must be a valid secret key.
The name of the Secret to select from.

Specifies whether the Secret or its key must be defined. If true, and the secret or key is missing, the environment variable is omitted and the container can start; if false (default), a missing secret or key causes an error.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.init_containers.env_f: envFrom is a list of sources to populate environment variables in the container. Each entry can reference a ConfigMap or Secret (or all keys), or use a prefix to prepend to variable names.
Reference to a ConfigMap from which to populate environment variables for this container. The ConfigMap is referenced by its name within the same namespace.
The name of the ConfigMap to reference. This ConfigMap must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap must exist. If true, a missing ConfigMap is allowed; if false (default), the ConfigMap must exist or the pod will fail to start.
An optional identifier to prepend to each key of the referenced ConfigMap or Secret. Must be a valid C identifier.

Reference to a Kubernetes Secret in the same namespace, used to populate environment variables for the init container. The Secret's data keys become environment variable names and their values become the variable values.
The name of the Secret to populate environment variables from. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the Pod.
Indicates whether the referenced Secret must be defined. When set to true, the Secret may be absent and the container will still start; when false or unset, the Secret must exist.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.init_containers.image: Specifies when the kubelet should pull the container image for this init container. Valid values are Always, IfNotPresent, and Never. Defaults to Always if the image tag is :latest, otherwise IfNotPresent.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.init_containers.lifec: Lifecycle configuration for the init container, specifying postStart and preStop hooks to execute at container start and shutdown.
post_start defines the postStart hook for the container lifecycle. This hook is executed immediately after the container is started and can be used to run initialization commands or checks.
Exec runs a command inside the container when the postStart lifecycle hook is triggered. The command is specified as a list of strings in the 'command' field.
The command to execute in the container for the postStart lifecycle hook. It is executed directly, not through a shell; the working directory is '/' in the container's filesystem.
Configures an HTTP GET request to be sent to the container as part of the postStart lifecycle hook. The request is sent to a specific endpoint on the container to trigger a post-start action.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request; defaults to the pod IP.
Custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request to the postStart handler. Each header object requires a name and value string.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request.
The value of the HTTP header field.
Path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/'.
The TCP port number or named port on the container to which the HTTP GET request is sent. Specify the port number as a string, or use a named container port.
The protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) to use for the HTTP GET request.
The scheme to use for the connection, either HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP.

Configures a sleep action for the postStart lifecycle hook, pausing container execution for a specified number of seconds before continuing. The nested 'seconds' field defines the duration of the sleep.
The number of seconds to sleep for the sleep lifecycle hook action.
Specifies a TCP socket to connect to as part of the postStart lifecycle hook. The handler attempts to open a TCP connection to the specified host and port.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket check. If not specified, the pod IP address is used.
The TCP port to connect to on the container. Accepts a numeric port or a named port defined in the container's ports.
preStop is a lifecycle hook that is called immediately before a container is terminated. It can be used to gracefully stop the container or perform cleanup actions.
Exec specifies the command to run in the container as part of the preStop lifecycle hook. It is an ExecAction object containing the command to execute.

The command to run in the container during the preStop lifecycle hook. It is an array of strings; the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments. The command is executed directly, not through a shell, and the working directory is root ('/') in the container's filesystem.
Represents an HTTP GET request to perform as the container's preStop lifecycle hook. This object defines the endpoint and headers for the request sent to the container before termination.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP.
List of HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request. Each header object contains `name` and `value` fields.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request for this preStop lifecycle hook.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request.
Path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to `/`.
The TCP port to send the HTTP request to. This can be a numeric port number or a named port defined in the container's port list.
The protocol (scheme) to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS; defaults to HTTP.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS, with HTTP as the default.
Represents a sleep action in the pre-stop lifecycle hook. It specifies a duration in seconds to wait before the container is terminated, allowing for graceful shutdown.
Specifies the number of seconds the container should sleep before it is terminated as part of the preStop hook.

Specifies a TCP socket action for the pre-stop lifecycle hook. This action attempts to open a TCP connection to a specified host and port, and the hook is considered successful when the connection is established.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket check. If not specified, the pod's IP address is used.
The TCP port number to connect to for the preStop lifecycle hook. Can be specified as a numeric port (e.g., "8080") or a named port defined in the container's ports.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.init_containers.liven: Liveness probe configuration for the init container. In Kubernetes, liveness probes are not supported for init containers and this field is ignored.

Exec is the exec-based action for the liveness probe, specifying a command to run inside the container to determine its health status. The command is defined as a list of arguments, which are executed directly in the container.

The command to run inside the container for the exec probe. It is a list of strings, where the first element is the command path and the rest are arguments. The kubelet executes this command periodically to determine whether the container is healthy.
The number of consecutive failures of the liveness probe before the container is restarted. The minimum value is 1; if not specified, the default is 3.
Specifies a gRPC health check action for the liveness probe. It contains a required port number and an optional service name to check, as defined by Kubernetes' GRPCAction.
The port number of the gRPC service to check. This should be the port on which the gRPC server is listening for health checks.
The name of the gRPC service to check in the health check request. If omitted, the probe checks the overall health of the server.
Defines an HTTP GET request used by the kubelet to perform a liveness check on the container. It specifies the path, port, and optional HTTP headers for the request.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET probe. Defaults to the pod IP.
Specifies custom HTTP headers to include in the request sent by the liveness probe. Each header is an object with `name` and `value` fields.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the liveness probe's HTTP GET request. For example, `X-Custom-Header`.
The value of the HTTP header. This is the actual string sent as the header's value; for example, for a header 'Authorization: Bearer token', the value is 'Bearer token'.
Path to access on the HTTP server for the probe request. Defaults to '/' if not specified.
Specifies the port to use for the HTTP GET request. Accepts a numeric port (1-65535) or the name of a container port.
Specifies the protocol used for the HTTP GET liveness probe, typically 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP' if not set.
The scheme to use for the connection, either 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
Number of seconds after the container has started before liveness probes are initiated. Defaults to 0.
How often (in seconds) to perform the liveness probe on the init container.
Minimum consecutive successes for the liveness probe to be considered successful after a failure. For liveness probes, this value must be 1.
Specifies the TCP socket action for the liveness probe. The probe will attempt to open a TCP connection to the container on the specified port to determine if it is healthy.
The host name to connect to for the TCP socket probe. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.

The port number or named port on the container to probe for liveness. In a tcpSocket probe, it specifies the TCP port to connect to; can be a numeric port or a port name defined in the container's ports.
Number of seconds after which the liveness probe times out. Defaults to 1 second; minimum value is 1.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.init_containers.name: The name of the init container. Must be a valid DNS label and unique within the pod. Required.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.init_containers.ports: List of ports exposed by the init container. Each port object specifies a name, container port number, protocol, and optionally host IP and host port.
The port number on which the container listens. In Kubernetes, the containerPort field specifies the network port that the container expects to receive traffic on, with a valid range of 1-65535.
The host IP address to bind the port to. Defaults to 0.0.0.0 (all interfaces).
The port on the host node to which the container port is mapped. If specified, this makes the container accessible from outside the node via the node's IP address.

Name of the port, used for referencing the port in the pod spec. Must be an IANA_SVC_NAME (up to 15 characters, lowercase alphanumeric, hyphens, and dots). Must be unique among all ports in the same container.
The network protocol used by the port. Allowed values are TCP, UDP, and SCTP. Defaults to TCP.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.init_containers.readi: Readiness probe configuration for an init container. It defines a health check that determines when the init container is considered ready, though init containers typically run to completion and this probe is rarely used.
Exec specifies the action to take, which is to run a command inside the container. The exit status of the command is used to determine whether the probe succeeded (exit code 0 indicates success).

The command to execute inside the container for this exec readiness probe. It is a list of strings, where the first element is the executable and subsequent elements are arguments. The probe succeeds if the command exits with status code 0.
Number of consecutive failures of the readiness probe required before the container is considered not ready. Defaults to 3; minimum value is 1.
Specifies a gRPC probe action for this readiness check. It defines the port and optional service name used to perform a gRPC health check against the container.
Specifies the port number to use for the gRPC health check in the container's readiness probe. Must be a valid TCP port number (1-65535).
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, defaults to an empty string.
Performs an HTTP GET request against the container to check its readiness. A response with a status code in the 2xx or 3xx range indicates success.
The hostname to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP. You can set this to override the Host header or connect to a specific host.
Optional list of custom HTTP headers to include in the GET request. Each object specifies a header name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the request.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the readiness probe's HTTP GET request.
The URL path (e.g., /healthz) that the HTTP probe requests from the container. An empty path results in a request to the server root.
The port number or name to use for the HTTP GET request. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or an IANA service name; defaults to the container's first allocated port if not specified.
The HTTP protocol (scheme) used for the request, such as 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP' if not specified.
The URL scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the readiness probe is initiated. This is the initial delay, in seconds, before the first probe runs.
The interval in seconds between each readiness probe execution.

Minimum consecutive successes for the readiness probe to be considered successful after having failed. Defaults to 1. For readiness probes, can be set higher to require multiple successful checks, but must be 1 for liveness and startup probes.

Configures a TCP socket check for the readiness probe. The probe attempts to open a TCP connection to the container on the specified port, optionally using a specified host. The container is considered ready if the connection succeeds.
Host name to connect to for the TCP socket probe. If not specified, the pod IP is used.
The TCP port to check on the container. Can be a port number (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container spec.
Number of seconds after which the readiness probe times out. If the probe does not complete within this duration, it is considered failed. Minimum value is 1; defaults to 1 second if not specified.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.init_containers.resiz: List of resource resize policies for the init container. Each policy specifies a resource name (e.g., cpu, memory) and a restart policy (NotRequired or RestartContainer) that determines whether the container must be restarted when the resource is resized.
The name of the resource (e.g., cpu or memory) to which this resize policy applies. Valid values are "cpu" and "memory".
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.init_containers.resou: Resource requirements for the init container, including requests and limits for compute resources such as CPU and memory.
List of resource claims that can be referenced by the container. Each item contains a 'name' field that refers to a ResourceClaim object in the same namespace.
Name of the ResourceClaim resource that this container requests. The referenced ResourceClaim must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Limits describes the maximum amount of compute resources allowed for the container. Each key is a resource name such as 'cpu' or 'memory', and the value is a quantity string (e.g., '500m', '1Gi').
Map of resource names to quantities, specifying the amount of compute resources requested for the init container (e.g., cpu, memory).
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.init_containers.resta: Specifies the restart policy for the init container. In Kubernetes, this field is only supported for sidecar init containers, and must be set to 'Always' if specified.
The comparison operator that determines how the specified exit codes are evaluated for the restart policy rule. Valid values include 'In' and 'NotIn'.
A list of numeric exit codes that this restart policy rule applies to.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.init_containers.secur: SecurityContext defines the security configuration for the init container, including settings like runAsUser, capabilities, and SELinux options, controlling the access and privileges of the container process.

Controls whether the init container's processes can gain more privileges than their parent (e.g., via setuid/setgid binaries). When false, the container runs with no_new_privs, preventing privilege escalation.

The AppArmor profile to apply to the init container. The type must be 'Localhost', 'RuntimeDefault', or 'Unconfined'. If type is 'Localhost', the 'localhostProfile' field must be set to the name of the profile.
Specifies the name of an AppArmor profile that is pre-loaded on the node. This field is used only when the type is 'Localhost'.
Specifies the type of AppArmor profile to apply to the container. Valid values are: Localhost, RuntimeDefault, Unconfined.
Configures Linux capabilities for the container. Allows adding or dropping specific capabilities via the 'add' and 'drop' subfields.
Adds the specified Linux capabilities to the init container's capability set. Each entry is a capability name (e.g., 'CAP_NET_ADMIN') that will be granted in addition to the default capabilities.
List of Linux capabilities to drop from the container's default set. For example, 'ALL' or specific capability names like 'NET_RAW'.
Indicates whether the container runs in privileged mode. Processes in privileged containers are equivalent to root on the host.
Specifies the proc mount type for the container. Valid values are 'Default' (default behavior) and 'Unmasked' (allows viewing all processes).

Indicates whether the container's root filesystem is mounted as read-only. When set to true, the container cannot write to its root filesystem, which helps prevent modifying system files and improves security.
Specifies the group ID (GID) that the container's main process runs as. If omitted, the default group from the container image is used.
Indicates whether the container must run as a non-root user. If true, the kubelet will reject the container if it is configured to run as UID 0 (root).
The numerical user ID (UID) that the init container's process will run as. If not specified, the default user in the container image is used.
SELinux options for the container, which specify the SELinux labels (user, role, type, and level) applied to the container's processes.
SELinux level label applied to the container, such as s0 or s0:c1,c2.
SELinux role label for the container. This is part of the SELinux options applied to the init container's security context, used to enforce mandatory access control policies.
The SELinux type label for the container, such as 'spc_t' or 'svirt_lxc_net_t'. This is part of the SELinux security context (user:role:type:level).
The SELinux user label applied to the container process.

Configures the seccomp profile for the container. The profile type can be RuntimeDefault, Localhost, or Unconfined; if Localhost, the localhostProfile field specifies the path to the profile on the node.
Specifies the path to a seccomp profile on the node. This field is used only when the seccomp profile type is 'Localhost'.
The seccomp profile type. Valid values are RuntimeDefault, Unconfined, and Localhost.
Windows-specific security options for the container. These options are only applicable to containers running on Windows.
Specifies the Group Managed Service Account (GMSA) credential spec to use, provided as a JSON string. This allows the container to access resources with the specified GMSA identity.
The name of the GMSA (Group Managed Service Account) credential spec to use for the Windows container. This is part of the Windows security context options for the init container.
Whether the container should run as a HostProcess container. Defaults to false.
The username in Windows to run the container's entrypoint process. If unspecified, the container uses the default user.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.init_containers.start: The startup probe configuration for the init container. This object defines the probe that determines when the container has started successfully, using the same probe mechanisms (such as HTTP, TCP, or command execution) as other Kubernetes probes.
Exec specifies the action to perform: running a command inside the container. The command's exit status is used to determine probe success.

Command is the command line to execute inside the container. The exit status of the command is the probe result: 0 indicates success, non-zero indicates failure. The command is executed directly, not through a shell.
The number of consecutive failures of the startup probe that must occur before the container is considered failed and restarted. This value must be an integer.
Specifies a gRPC health check action for this startup probe, allowing the kubelet to verify container health via gRPC according to the gRPC Health Checking Protocol.
The port number on which the gRPC server is listening. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535.
Specifies the name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default is the container name.
Specifies an HTTP GET request performed against the container for the startup probe. The probe is considered successful if the HTTP response code is between 200 and 399.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the startup probe's HTTP GET request. Each item defines a header with a `name` and a `value`.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the startup probe's HTTP request.
The value of the HTTP header that is sent in the startup probe's HTTP GET request. This pairs with the header name to form a key-value pair.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server. For example, '/healthz'.
The port number or named port on the container that the HTTP GET request will be sent to. Must be a valid integer port number or a named port defined in the container.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the startup probe is initiated. If not specified, defaults to 0.
Number of seconds between startup probe attempts. Minimum value is 1; defaults to 10.

Specifies the TCP socket action for the startup probe. The probe attempts to open a TCP connection to the container's IP address on a specified port. If the connection succeeds, the probe is considered successful. Contains 'port' (required) and 'host' (optional) fields.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket probe. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
The TCP port to probe, which can be a numeric port (e.g., 8080) or a named port defined in the container's port list.

The duration in seconds the pod needs to terminate gracefully upon deletion. This value may be decreased in delete requests, and defaults to 30 seconds if not specified. It applies to all containers in the pod, including init containers.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second. Minimum value is 1.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.init_containers.stdin: Indicates whether the container runtime should keep the container's standard input (stdin) open. This allows a process to read from stdin, typically for interactive sessions.

Whether the container runtime should close the stdin channel after it has been opened by a single attach. If true, stdin is opened on container start, remains open until the first client disconnects, and then stays closed until the container restarts. Defaults to false.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.init_containers.termi: Path to a file where the container's termination message is written. Defaults to /dev/termination-log.

Specifies how the termination message is derived. Supported values: 'File' (default) and 'FallbackToLogsOnError'. When set to 'FallbackToLogsOnError', the termination message is read from the container's log if the message file is empty.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.init_containers.tty: Indicates whether a TTY (teletypewriter) should be allocated to the container, enabling interactive terminal access.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.init_containers.volum: The list of block device volume mounts for the init container. Each item maps a volume name to a device path at which the raw block device is exposed inside the container. Typically used when a volume's volumeMode is 'Block'.
The path inside the container where the block device is mounted, such as /dev/xvda. This is the device path that the container will use to access the volume.
The name of the volume that this device refers to. Must match the name of a volume defined in the pod spec.
List of volumes to mount into the init container's filesystem. Each volume mount references a volume defined in the pod spec and specifies the mount path.
The path inside the container at which the volume should be mounted. This is a required field for each volume mount.
Defines how mount propagation is set for this volume mount. Allowed values are 'None', 'HostToContainer', and 'Bidirectional'. If not specified, 'None' is used.
The name of the volume to mount into the init container. This must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec.volumes.
Specifies whether the volume mount is read-only. When set to true, the container can only read from the mounted volume.
Specifies whether the volume mount is recursive read-only. When enabled, the mount and all of its subpaths are read-only. This corresponds to the Kubernetes `recursiveReadOnly` field.
Specifies a sub-path inside the volume to mount instead of the volume's root. The sub-path must already exist before the container starts, and it is relative to the volume's root directory.
Specifies a sub-path inside the volume to mount, with support for environment variable references using $(VAR_NAME) syntax. This is similar to subPath but expands environment variables at runtime.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.init_containers.worki: Container's working directory. If not specified, the container runtime's default is used, which might be configured in the container image. Must be an absolute path.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.readiness_gates.condi: The condition type that must be satisfied for the pod to be considered ready. This corresponds to a condition in the pod's status.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.resource_claims.name: The name of this resource claim, used to reference the claim from container resource claims (e.g., in `resources.claims`).
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.resource_claims.resou: The name of the ResourceClaim referenced in the pod. This name must be unique within the pod and is used by containers to bind to the claimed resource via their resource claim references.
The name of a ResourceClaimTemplate that provides the resource claim for this pod. The template is used to dynamically create a ResourceClaim.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.resources.claims.name: The name of the ResourceClaim resource (in the same namespace) that this container requests.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.scheduling_gates.name: The name of the scheduling gate. The pod will not be scheduled until a matching condition with this name is removed from the pod.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.security_context.sysc: The sysctl parameter name to set, e.g. kernel.shm_rmid_forced.
The value to assign to the sysctl parameter. This is a string, but many sysctls expect numeric-like values (e.g., "0" or "1") depending on the specific parameter.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.tolerations.effect: The effect of the taint that this toleration matches. Allowed values are NoSchedule, PreferNoSchedule, and NoExecute. An empty string matches all effects.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.tolerations.key: The key of the taint that this toleration applies to. If the operator is 'Exists', the key can be empty.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.tolerations.operator: The operator to apply to the key and value. Valid values are 'Exists' and 'Equal'. If 'Exists', the toleration matches if the taint key matches; if 'Equal', the value must also match.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.tolerations.toleratio: The number of seconds a pod tolerates a taint before it is evicted when the toleration effect is NoExecute. If unset, the toleration persists indefinitely.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.tolerations.value: The taint value that the toleration matches. This is required when the operator is 'Equal' and should be empty when the operator is 'Exists'.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.topology_spread_const: LabelSelector is used to find matching pods to which this topology spread constraint applies. If not set, the constraint applies to all pods in the namespace.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and a list of values, enabling complex label selection for the topology spread constraint's label selector.
The label key that the match expression applies to, used to select resources based on their labels.
The operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists and DoesNotExist.

values is a list of string values. When the operator is 'In' or 'NotIn', this list specifies the values the label key must (or must not) match; for 'Exists' or 'DoesNotExist', it must be empty (and is typically omitted).
A map of key-value pairs that must match the pod's labels for the pod to be selected by this topology spread constraint. Equivalent to matchLabels in a Kubernetes LabelSelector.
A list of label keys that specifiy which pods to consider for spreading. Pods having any of these label keys (regardless of value) are included in the topology spread calculation.
The maximum difference in the number of matching Pods between the topology domain with the most Pods and the domain with the fewest. Must be greater than zero.
The minimum number of topology domains that must exist for pod spreading to be applied. If specified, the cluster must have at least this many domains; otherwise, pods are not scheduled.

Indicates how to treat node affinity when calculating pod topology spread skew. Allowed values are 'Honor' (default) and 'Ignore'. With 'Honor', only nodes matching the pod's node affinity are considered; with 'Ignore', node affinity is ignored.
Specifies how to treat nodes with taints when calculating pod topology spread skew. Allowed values are 'Honor' and 'Ignore' (default is 'Ignore').
The key of node labels. Nodes that have a label with this key and identical values are considered to be in the same topology domain.

Indicates how to handle a pod when the topology spread constraint is not satisfied. Allowed values are 'DoNotSchedule' (default) and 'ScheduleAnyway'. 'DoNotSchedule' prevents the pod from being scheduled, while 'ScheduleAnyway' allows scheduling while still attempting to honor the constraint as much as possible.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.aws_elastic_b: Defines an AWS Elastic Block Store (EBS) volume as a source for a Kubernetes volume. This field provides the configuration to attach an EBS volume to the pod.
Filesystem type to mount on the AWS EBS volume, e.g., 'ext4', 'xfs', or 'ntfs'. Must be supported by the host operating system.
The partition number of the AWS EBS volume to mount. If the volume is partitioned, specify the partition number (e.g., 1 for /dev/sdb1).
Specifies whether the AWS EBS volume is mounted as read-only. If true, the volume is mounted read-only; otherwise it can be read-write.
The unique identifier of the AWS EBS volume to be mounted, typically in the form 'vol-xxxxxxxx'.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.azure_disk: Represents an Azure Disk volume source, enabling a pod to mount a Microsoft Azure managed disk as a volume for persistent storage.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.azure_disk.ca: CachingMode specifies the caching policy for the Azure disk. Allowed values are None, ReadOnly, and ReadWrite; if not set, the default is None.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.azure_disk.di: The name of the Azure data disk to mount. This must be the name of a disk in the same resource group as the cluster.
The URI of the virtual hard disk (VHD) for unmanaged disks, or the resource ID for managed disks, that the volume should mount. This identifies the Azure disk to attach.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.azure_disk.fs: Filesystem type to use when mounting the Azure Disk volume. Defaults to 'ext4' if not specified.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.azure_disk.ki: Kind of the Azure disk: Shared (multiple blob disks per storage account), Dedicated (single blob disk per storage account), or Managed (managed disk). Defaults to Shared.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.azure_disk.re: Whether the Azure disk volume is mounted as read-only. If set to true, the volume is mounted with read-only access; otherwise, it is mounted with read-write access.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.azure_file: azureFile represents an Azure File volume source that can be mounted as a volume in a pod, using an Azure Files share.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.azure_file.re: If set to true, the Azure file share is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.azure_file.se: The name of the Kubernetes secret that stores the Azure Storage account name and key used to access the Azure file share.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.azure_file.sh: The name of the Azure File share to mount. This must match an existing share in the Azure storage account.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.cephfs: Configures a Ceph Filesystem (CephFS) volume that mounts a Ceph share into the pod. This is one of the supported volume source types in the volumes list.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.cephfs.monito: Ceph monitors are the addresses (hostnames or IPs) of the Ceph monitor nodes. This field specifies a list of endpoints used to connect to the Ceph cluster.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.cephfs.path: Path within the CephFS volume to mount. If not specified, defaults to the root directory.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.cephfs.read_o: If true, the CephFS volume is mounted as read-only, preventing write access from the pod.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.cephfs.secret: Path to the Ceph keyring file used for authentication. Defaults to /etc/ceph/user.secret.
Reference to a Secret that contains the CephFS credentials (e.g., keyring). The Secret must be in the same namespace as the pod.
Name of the Secret that holds the CephFS authentication credentials. The Secret must be in the same namespace as the pod.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.cephfs.user: The CephFS user to use for authentication. Defaults to 'admin' if not specified.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.cinder: Cinder represents a Cinder volume (OpenStack block storage) that is mounted into the pod. It contains configuration for the Cinder volume source, such as the volume ID, filesystem type, and read-only settings.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.cinder.fs_typ: Filesystem type to mount, such as 'ext4', 'xfs', etc. If not specified, the default filesystem type of the volume is used.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.cinder.read_o: Specifies whether the Cinder volume is mounted as read-only. When set to true, the volume is read-only; otherwise it is read-write.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.cinder.secret: SecretRef is a reference to a Kubernetes Secret that contains authentication credentials for the Cinder volume. This is optional and used to provide credentials when mounting the volume.
Name of the Kubernetes secret containing the Cinder authentication credentials.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.cinder.volume: The ID of the Cinder volume to attach and mount.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.config_map: config_map is a volume source that configures a volume to use a Kubernetes ConfigMap as its content. The specified ConfigMap's data is exposed as files in the volume, enabling pods to consume configuration data.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.config_map.de: Sets the file permission mode (in octal, as a decimal integer) for all files within the ConfigMap volume. If unset, the default mode is 0644.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.config_map.it: A list of key-to-path mappings. If specified, only the listed keys from the ConfigMap are exposed as files at the specified paths. If omitted, all keys are exposed as files using their key names as paths.
The key to select from the ConfigMap data. This is the key within the ConfigMap's data map whose value will be written to the file path specified by the 'path' field.

Optional permission mode bits for the file (octal). Valid values are 0000 to 0777 (decimal 0 to 511). In JSON, the number must be expressed in decimal (e.g., 420 for 0644). If unset, the volume's defaultMode is used.
The relative path within the volume where the file from the corresponding configMap key will be mounted.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.config_map.na: The name of the ConfigMap that provides the volume data. This must match the name of a ConfigMap in the same namespace as the pod.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.config_map.op: Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap and its keys must be defined. If set to true, a missing ConfigMap or missing keys are tolerated (resulting in an empty volume or ignored key); if false or omitted, the Pod fails when the ConfigMap or specified keys are absent.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.csi: Represents a volume that is provisioned by a CSI (Container Storage Interface) driver. This allows Kubernetes to consume storage from a driver that implements the CSI specification, enabling integration with external storage systems.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.csi.driver: Name of the CSI driver to use. This field is required and must match the driver name as registered on the kubelet.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.csi.fs_type: Filesystem type to mount for the CSI volume, such as 'ext4' or 'xfs'. If not specified, it is typically inferred as 'ext4', though the CSI driver may define its own default.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.csi.node_publ: A local object reference to a Kubernetes secret in the same namespace that provides credentials for the CSI driver when publishing the volume on the node. This corresponds to the nodePublishSecretRef field of the CSI volume source.
The name of the Secret that contains the credentials for publishing the volume to the node. This Secret must exist in the same namespace as the Pod.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.csi.read_only: Specifies whether the CSI volume is mounted as read-only. When set to true, the volume is exposed as read-only to the pod; defaults to false.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.csi.volume_at: Map of string keys and values specifying volume attributes for the CSI driver. The meaning of each attribute is driver-specific.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.downward_api: Represents a volume that exposes the downward API data, including pod metadata like labels, annotations, and resource limits, to the container as files.
Optional mode bits used to set permissions on created files by default. Must be an octal value between 0000 and 0777 or a decimal value between 0 and 511. YAML accepts both octal and decimal values, JSON requires decimal values for mode bits. Defaults to 0644.

Optional list of files to create in the volume. Each item consists of a relative path and a fieldRef or resourceFieldRef that specifies which pod field or container resource value to expose at that path.

fieldRef is a reference to a field in the pod's metadata or spec to be exposed, defined by a fieldPath (e.g., metadata.name, metadata.labels['key']) and optionally an apiVersion for the field's schema.
The API version of the referent (e.g., 'v1') that the fieldPath is evaluated against.
The path to the field in the pod's object that will be exposed. For example, 'metadata.name' or 'spec.nodeName'.
Mode bits to use on this file, represented as an integer. If not set, the volume's default mode is used.
The relative path of the file within the volume where the downward API value will be written. The path must not start with '..' and can include directory components.

The resource field selector that selects a container resource field (e.g., limits.cpu or requests.memory) to expose via the downward API. It is represented by a ResourceFieldSelector object with fields for resource, containerName, and divisor.
The name of the container for which the resource value is referenced. If not specified, defaults to the first container in the pod.
Divisor is the divisor for the resource quantity, specified as a Kubernetes quantity (e.g., '1m' for CPU, '1Gi' for memory). It defaults to '1' if not provided.
The name of the container resource to select, such as 'limits.cpu' or 'requests.memory'. This field specifies which resource (request or limit) is exposed via the downward API volume.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.empty_dir: Defines a temporary directory that is created empty when the pod starts and exists for the lifetime of the pod, allowing containers in the pod to share files. This volume is removed when the pod is deleted.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.empty_dir.med: The storage medium for the emptyDir volume. Set to 'Memory' to use a RAM-backed tmpfs, or 'HugePages' to use hugepages. The default (empty string) uses the node's disk.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.empty_dir.siz: The total amount of local storage required for this emptyDir volume, specified as a Kubernetes quantity (e.g., '128Mi'). If not set, the node's default limit applies.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.ephemeral: Configures an ephemeral volume for the pod. This volume type is created and removed with the pod, and can be backed by either a PersistentVolumeClaim template (generic ephemeral volume) or a CSI driver (CSI ephemeral volume).
