kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.ephemeral.vol: A template for a PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC) that defines the volume's storage characteristics, such as access modes, resources, and storage class. When specified, Kubernetes creates a PVC from this template for the ephemeral volume's lifetime.

Metadata for the PersistentVolumeClaim generated from this volume claim template, such as labels and annotations. This is standard Kubernetes object metadata (ObjectMeta) applied to the PVC created by the ephemeral volume.

Annotations is a map of string keys to string values that can be used to attach arbitrary non-identifying metadata to the volume claim template created for this ephemeral volume. This metadata is accessible to clients and tooling but does not affect the volume's behavior.
CreationTimestamp is a timestamp representing the server time when this object was created. It is represented in RFC3339 form (UTC) and is set by the system; clients cannot set it.
The duration in seconds before the object is forcibly deleted, used during graceful deletion.
The time at which the resource is marked for deletion, in RFC 3339 format. This is set by the server when a deletion is requested and is not directly settable by clients.
List of finalizers that must be removed before the object can be deleted. Each finalizer is a string identifier for a controller or owner that must clean up before deletion is allowed.

A prefix used by the Kubernetes API server to generate a unique name for this object if the name field is not provided. The generated name consists of the prefix followed by a random alphanumeric suffix.
A sequence number representing a specific generation of the desired state for the persistent volume claim template. This field is populated by the Kubernetes system and is read-only.
Map of string keys and values that can be used to organize and categorize the PersistentVolumeClaim created from this template. These labels will be set on the generated PVC's metadata.

A list of managed fields entries that map the workflow-id and version to the set of fields managed by that workflow. This is mostly for internal housekeeping and typically should not be set or modified by users.
The API version (e.g., 'apps/v1') of the Kubernetes resource that this managed fields entry belongs to.
Specifies the type of the fields managed by this entry. In Kubernetes, the only supported value is 'FieldsV1'.
fieldsV1 stores the fields owned by the manager in a structured format (like a Trie) represented as a JSON object.
The name of the field manager that last applied changes to this managed field.
The operation performed by the manager on this managed field, typically 'Apply' or 'Update'.
Describes which subresource of the object the managing controller acted on, such as the main resource (empty string), 'status', or 'scale'.
The timestamp at which the operation recorded in the managed field entry was performed. This is a string in RFC3339 format (e.g., 2023-01-01T00:00:00Z).

The name of the volumeClaimTemplate. This name is used as a base for the PersistentVolumeClaim name generated for each pod that uses this ephemeral volume (the PVC name is typically <pod-name>-<template-name>).

The namespace for the volume claim template. In an ephemeral volume, the generated PersistentVolumeClaim is created in the same namespace as the pod, so this field must be empty or set to that namespace.

List of references to the resources that own this object. Used for garbage collection and cascading deletion; each item contains apiVersion, kind, name, uid, and optionally controller and blockOwnerDeletion.
The API version of the referenced owner resource, e.g., 'apps/v1'. This field is used in an OwnerReference to identify the version of the owning object.
If true, prevents the owner from being deleted in foreground deletion until this dependent object is removed. Defaults to false.
Indicates whether the referenced owner is the managing controller of the resource. If true, this owner manages the resource and prevents it from being garbage-collected until the owner is deleted.
The kind of the owner object referenced, such as 'Deployment' or 'ReplicaSet'.
The UID of the referenced owner object. This is a unique identifier assigned by Kubernetes to the object, used to unambiguously identify the owner in the cluster.

ResourceVersion is an opaque string that identifies the internal version of an object. It is used for optimistic concurrency control; clients should treat it as an opaque value and not interpret it. For a volume claim template, this field is part of the standard metadata schema but is typically not set in template definitions.
self_link is a string that contains the URL of the volume claim template for this ephemeral volume within the Kubernetes API.
UID is a system-generated unique identifier for the object. It is read-only and typically assigned by the server when the resource is created.

spec is the specification of the persistent volume claim to be created for the ephemeral volume. It defines the desired characteristics of the volume, such as storage class, access modes, and resources.
Specifies the access modes for the ephemeral volume claim. Allowed values are ReadWriteOnce, ReadOnlyMany, ReadWriteMany, and ReadWriteOncePod.
Specifies the data source for the volume claim, such as a VolumeSnapshot or PersistentVolumeClaim, used to pre-populate the ephemeral volume with data.
apiGroup is the group for the resource being referenced. If apiGroup is not specified, the specified Kind must be in the core API group. For any other third-party types, apiGroup is required.
Kind is the kind of the referenced data source (e.g., VolumeSnapshot or PersistentVolumeClaim).
The name of the data source object referenced by this volume claim template's dataSource.

Specifies a reference to an object that should be used to populate the volume claim, such as a VolumeSnapshot, PersistentVolumeClaim, or any custom resource. Unlike dataSource, dataSourceRef can reference objects in other namespaces and is typically used with volume populator controllers. This field is part of the PVC spec generated for an ephemeral volume.
APIGroup is the group for the resource being referenced. If APIGroup is not specified, the specified Kind must be in the core API group. For any other third-party types, APIGroup is required.
The kind of the referenced data source object. Typical values are 'PersistentVolumeClaim' or 'VolumeSnapshot', matching the resource type of the data source.
The name of the data source object (e.g., VolumeSnapshot, PersistentVolumeClaim) referenced by the dataSourceRef for the ephemeral volume claim.
The namespace of the referenced data source object. When not set, the namespace of the containing PersistentVolumeClaim is used.
Defines the storage resource requirements for the ephemeral volume, such as the requested capacity. Supports requests and limits for storage, e.g., requests: { storage: 1Gi }.

limits specifies the maximum resources for this ephemeral volume claim, as a map of resource names (e.g., 'storage') to quantities (e.g., '1Gi'). In Kubernetes, this is used to cap the volume size or other resource usage for the claim.

Requests describes the minimum resources required. For a volume claim, this typically specifies the desired storage size, e.g., {'storage': '1Gi'}. The keys are resource names like 'storage', and values are Kubernetes quantity strings.
A label query over PersistentVolumes to consider for binding. Only volumes that match the selector are eligible for use by the ephemeral volume claim.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (such as In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and an optional list of values. This enables complex label selection logic for the volume claim template.
The label key that the selector applies to. This is the key of a label that the match expression evaluates against.
The operator that represents the relationship between the key and the set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
A list of values for the label selector expression. When the operator is 'In' or 'NotIn', this list must be non-empty; for 'Exists' or 'DoesNotExist', it must be empty.
A map of string keys and values that defines a label selector. The selector matches resources whose labels contain all specified key-value pairs.
The name of the StorageClass to use for this volume claim. If omitted, the default StorageClass is used.
The name of a VolumeAttributesClass to apply to the volume claim. If specified, the class sets additional attributes on the provisioned volume.
The volume mode that the volume will be mounted in. Supported values are 'Filesystem' (default) and 'Block'.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.fc: Defines a Fibre Channel (FC) volume source. This allows mounting a Fibre Channel storage volume into the pod, typically by specifying target World Wide Names (WWNs), a logical unit number (LUN), and filesystem type.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.fc.fs_type: Filesystem type to be mounted on the Fibre Channel volume (e.g., ext4, xfs). If not specified, Kubernetes attempts to detect the filesystem automatically.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.fc.lun: The LUN (Logical Unit Number) of the Fibre Channel target to mount. This is a required integer.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.fc.read_only: Indicates whether the Fibre Channel volume is mounted as read-only. If true, the volume is read-only; if false or omitted, it is read-write.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.fc.target_wwn: List of Fibre Channel target World Wide Names (WWNs) that specify the devices to connect to. This field is required for FC volumes.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.fc.wwids: A list of Fibre Channel WWIDs (World Wide Identifiers) used to identify the target volume. If specified, this replaces the targetWWNs and lun fields.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.flex_volume: FlexVolume represents a generic volume plugin that is mounted via an exec-based interface. It enables integration with third-party storage systems that implement the FlexVolume API, using driver-specific options.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.flex_volume.d: The name of the FlexVolume driver to use for mounting this volume. This driver must be installed on each node.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.flex_volume.f: Filesystem type to be mounted by the FlexVolume driver, such as ext4, xfs, or ntfs. If unspecified, the driver may use its own default.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.flex_volume.o: Extra command options to pass to the FlexVolume driver, as a map of string keys and values.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.flex_volume.r: When set to true, the FlexVolume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false (read-write).
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.flex_volume.s: Optional reference to a Kubernetes Secret that contains sensitive information (e.g., credentials) needed by the FlexVolume driver. The secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod and is referenced by name.
Name of the Secret resource that contains the secret data to pass to the FlexVolume driver.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.flocker: Volume source that represents a Flocker dataset to be mounted into the pod. Configures the Flocker volume using dataset identifiers or name.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.flocker.datas: The name of the Flocker dataset to mount as a volume. Should be set if dataset_uuid is not set.
The UUID of the Flocker dataset to mount. Either datasetName or datasetUUID must be specified.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.gce_persisten: Configuration for a Google Compute Engine Persistent Disk volume. This volume source mounts an existing GCE persistent disk into the pod, identified by its disk name and with optional filesystem type, partition, and read-only settings.
Filesystem type for the GCE Persistent Disk volume, e.g., 'ext4' or 'xfs'. Defaults to 'ext4' if not specified.
The partition number of the GCE Persistent Disk to mount. If omitted, the entire disk is mounted.
pdName is the unique name of the GCE Persistent Disk resource. It identifies the disk to be mounted in the pod.
Mounts the GCE Persistent Disk as read-only. When true, the volume is mounted read-only; when false (default), it is mounted read-write.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.git_repo: gitRepo represents a volume populated from a git repository. This is a deprecated volume source; use an emptyDir with an init container instead. The object allows specifying the repository URL, revision, and target directory.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.git_repo.dire: The target directory name inside the volume where the git repository will be cloned. If omitted, the repository's name is used.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.git_repo.repo: The repository URL for the git repository to clone into the volume.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.git_repo.revi: The commit hash to check out from the specified Git repository. If not provided, the repository's HEAD is used.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.glusterfs: Glusterfs represents a Glusterfs volume that can be mounted by the pod. It specifies the Glusterfs endpoints and path, and optionally read-only.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.glusterfs.end: The name of the Endpoints object that defines the Glusterfs server addresses for this volume.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.glusterfs.pat: Path to the Glusterfs volume (e.g., /vol1). This field is required when using a glusterfs volume source.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.glusterfs.rea: Specifies whether the GlusterFS volume is mounted as read-only.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.host_path: Defines a hostPath volume that mounts a file or directory from the host node's filesystem into the pod. This allows the pod to access host paths.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.host_path.pat: The path of the directory or file on the host node that will be mounted into the pod. This field is required when using a hostPath volume.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.host_path.typ: The type of the host path. Supported values include '', Directory, DirectoryOrCreate, File, FileOrCreate, Socket, CharDevice, and BlockDevice. An empty string means no check is performed before mounting.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.image: Image volume source configuration. Specifies an OCI image to be mounted as a volume, including the image reference and pull policy.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.image.pull_po: The image pull policy for the image volume source. Allowed values are 'Always', 'IfNotPresent', and 'Never'. Defaults to 'IfNotPresent' unless the image reference uses the ':latest' tag, in which case it defaults to 'Always'.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.image.referen: The image reference (name and tag) of the container image to mount as a volume, for example 'nginx:latest'.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.iscsi: Represents an iSCSI volume source, which allows mounting an iSCSI target (LUN) as a volume in the pod.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.iscsi.chap_au: Enables CHAP authentication for iSCSI discovery. When true, the initiator authenticates the target during the discovery phase.

Indicates whether CHAP (Challenge Handshake Authentication Protocol) authentication is enabled for the iSCSI session. When true, the iSCSI session uses CHAP authentication with the secret specified in the secretRef field.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.iscsi.fs_type: The filesystem type to be mounted (e.g., ext4, xfs). If not specified, the filesystem type of the underlying iSCSI volume is used.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.iscsi.initiat: The custom iSCSI initiator name. If not set, the default initiator name (derived from the system) is used for iSCSI connections.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.iscsi.iqn: The iSCSI Qualified Name (IQN) of the iSCSI target.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.iscsi.iscsi_i: Specifies the iSCSI interface name for the iSCSI transport. Defaults to 'default' if not set.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.iscsi.lun: The LUN (Logical Unit Number) of the iSCSI target. This numeric identifier specifies the logical unit to mount from the target.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.iscsi.portals: List of iSCSI target portals for the volume. Each portal is an IP address or IP:port pair when using non-default ports (default TCP ports are 8600 and 3260).
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.iscsi.read_on: Indicates whether the iSCSI volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false (read-write).
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.iscsi.secret_: References a Kubernetes Secret that contains the CHAP authentication credentials for the iSCSI target. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the Pod.
The name of the Secret that contains CHAP authentication credentials for the iSCSI target. The Secret must be in the same namespace as the Pod.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.iscsi.target_: The iSCSI target portal. The portal is either an IP address or ip_addr:port if the port is other than the default (typically TCP ports 860 and 3260).
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.name: Name of the volume. Must be a unique DNS_LABEL within the pod. This name is used to reference the volume in container volumeMounts.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.nfs: Configures an NFS (Network File System) share as a volume. Includes settings for the NFS server, exported path, and read-only flag.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.nfs.path: Path of the NFS export on the NFS server. This is the directory on the NFS server that will be mounted into the pod.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.nfs.read_only: Forces the NFS export to be mounted with read-only permissions. Defaults to false (read-write).
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.nfs.server: The hostname or IP address of the NFS server that exports the volume.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.persistent_vo: Configures a volume that is backed by a PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC). This allows a pod to use persistent storage by referencing a PVC in the same namespace.
The name of the PersistentVolumeClaim in the same namespace to reference as a volume source.
If true, the persistent volume claim is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.photon_persis: Defines a volume that uses a Photon Controller persistent disk, allowing the container to access a persistent disk managed by Photon Controller.
Filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system. Ex. 'ext4', 'xfs', 'ntfs'. Implicitly inferred to be 'ext4' if unspecified.
The unique identifier of the Photon persistent disk. This is the ID that identifies the disk in Photon Controller, and it is required to mount the volume.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.portworx_volu: Configures a Portworx volume as a pod volume. This block defines a volume backed by a Portworx storage volume.
The filesystem type to mount on the Portworx volume, such as 'ext4' or 'xfs'. If not specified, defaults to 'ext4'.
Specifies whether the Portworx volume is mounted as read-only. If set to true, the volume is mounted with read-only permissions.
The unique identifier of the Portworx volume to be mounted.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.projected: Represents a projected volume source, which can mount multiple volume sources into the same directory. It supports sources such as secret, configMap, downwardAPI, and serviceAccountToken.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.projected.def: Optional mode bits used to set permissions on files created in the projected volume. Must be an octal value between 0000 and 0777 or decimal between 0 and 511. Defaults to 0644.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.projected.sou: sources is the list of VolumeProjection objects that are projected into the volume. Each projection can be a configMap, secret, downwardAPI, or serviceAccountToken.
Configures a ClusterTrustBundle as a source for a projected volume, allowing the pod to access the trust bundle (such as a CA bundle) from a named ClusterTrustBundle object in the cluster.
labelSelector is a standard Kubernetes label selector that filters ClusterTrustBundle resources by labels. Only ClusterTrustBundles matching this selector are projected into the volume.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally a list of values. All requirements must be satisfied for the selector to match.
The label key that the match expression uses to select cluster trust bundles. This key must correspond to a label on the bundle and be a valid Kubernetes label key.
The operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
A list of string values that the label key must match when the operator is 'In' or 'NotIn'. For operators 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist', this list must be empty.

matchLabels is a map of {key,value} pairs. A single {key,value} in the matchLabels map is equivalent to an element of matchExpressions, whose key field is "key", the operator is "In", and the values array contains only "value". The requirements are ANDed.
Name of the referenced ClusterTrustBundle object to project into the volume.
Indicates whether the ClusterTrustBundle can be omitted from the projected volume. If set to true, the projection is skipped when the bundle is absent; if false or unset, the bundle must exist.
The relative path of the file within the projected volume where the cluster trust bundle content is mounted. This path must be a relative path and cannot start with '..'.
The signer name of the cluster trust bundle to project. Selects the trust bundle(s) that match this signer name when multiple bundles exist.
ConfigMap projection to include in the projected volume. Used to project a ConfigMap's data (or specific items) into the volume.

Optional list of key mappings that specify which keys from the referenced ConfigMap to project into the volume, and the paths and file modes for each. If omitted, all key-value pairs are projected as files with key names; if specified, only listed keys are projected.
The key in the ConfigMap to select. This must be a valid key name within the referenced ConfigMap's data.
Optional file mode (permission bits) for the file. If not specified, the default is 0644. Must be a 32-bit integer representing an octal permission value, typically between 0 and 0777.

Path specifies the relative file path (within the volume) where the value of the corresponding key is mounted. It must be a relative path, must not contain '..' or start with '/', and determines the filename as seen in the projected volume.
Name of the ConfigMap to project into the volume. Must be a valid Kubernetes object name.
Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap is optional. When set to true, the volume will not fail if the ConfigMap does not exist.
The `downward_api` source within a projected volume exposes Pod metadata such as labels and annotations as files to the container.
The list of DownwardAPIVolumeFile items that specify the files to project via the downward API. Each item defines a relative file path and the pod field reference to write to that path.
A reference to a pod field whose value is projected into the volume, such as metadata.name or spec.nodeName.
The API version of the schema that the fieldPath refers to. For example, 'v1'.
The path to the pod spec field to be exposed, such as metadata.name or spec.nodeName. It selects a field of the pod specification.
Optional file permissions for the file, specified in octal (e.g., 0644). If unset, the default file mode is used.
Path within the volume where the field value will be exposed as a file. This is the relative path of the file in the projected volume.
Selects a container resource field (such as requests.cpu or limits.memory) to expose in the downward API volume. Only resource limits and requests are supported.
The name of the container to which the resource field reference applies. Required when the resource field refers to a container resource (e.g., limits or requests).
Divisor is the value to divide the resource value by. Must be a valid Quantity, defaults to 1.
The name of the resource to select, such as "limits.cpu" or "requests.memory". This is a required field in the ResourceFieldSelector for downward API volumes.
Path within the projected volume where the certificate chain is exposed. The file at this path contains the full certificate chain.
Specifies the relative path within the projected volume where the certificate's private key file is placed.
The name of the certificate signer that should issue the pod certificate. This is used to select the appropriate signer when requesting a certificate for the pod.
The numeric UID that will own the certificate file projected from this source. If unset, the file is owned by UID 0 (root).
SecretProjection adapts a secret into a projected volume. The secret's data keys are exposed as files in the volume.

A list of key-to-path mappings that specify which secret keys are projected into the volume and the file paths they are exposed at. If items is not set, all keys from the referenced secret are projected.
The key within the referenced Secret that corresponds to the data to project into the volume. This is the name of the entry in the Secret's data map.
The permissions for the file representing the secret key. Must be a numeric value between 0 and 511 (octal 0000-0777) representing Unix file mode bits.
Relative path within the projected volume to which the secret key is mapped. Must be a relative path and must not contain '..' segments.
The name of the Secret to project into the volume. This must match the name of a Secret in the same namespace as the pod.
If true, the referenced secret is not required to exist; if it is missing, the volume is created without files from that secret. Defaults to false, requiring the secret to be present.
Configures a projected volume source that injects the service account token into the pod. The token can be customized with fields such as audience, expirationSeconds, and path.
The audience (aud) claim for the service account token, specifying the intended recipient. The token is valid only for this audience, such as the Kubernetes API server or a specific service.
The expiration time of the projected service account token, in seconds. Must be between 600 and 86400 (10 minutes to 24 hours), and defaults to 3600 (1 hour).
The relative path within the projected volume at which to mount the service account token.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.quobyte: Configuration for a Quobyte volume source, which mounts a Quobyte distributed storage system into the pod.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.quobyte.group: Group to map volume access to. Defaults to no group.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.quobyte.read_: Whether to mount the volume as read-only. Defaults to false.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.quobyte.regis: The Quobyte registry to connect to, as a host or host:port, or a comma-separated list of registries.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.quobyte.tenan: The tenant name that owns the Quobyte volume in the backend; used with dynamically provisioned Quobyte volumes.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.quobyte.user: User to map volume access to. Defaults to the volume name if not set.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.quobyte.volum: The name of the Quobyte volume to mount.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.rbd: rbd represents a Rados Block Device (RBD) volume source, allowing a pod to mount an RBD image into the container.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.rbd.fs_type: Filesystem type of the RBD volume that Kubernetes will mount (e.g., ext4, xfs). If not set, the filesystem type is determined by the image's existing filesystem.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.rbd.image: The rados image name. This is the name of the RBD image to mount as a volume.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.rbd.keyring: The path to the keyring file for RBD user authentication. Defaults to /etc/ceph/keyring.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.rbd.monitors: Monitors is a list of Ceph monitor addresses (host:port) used to connect to the Ceph cluster for the RBD volume.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.rbd.pool: The Ceph pool name where the RBD image resides. Defaults to 'rbd' if not specified.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.rbd.read_only: If set to true, the RBD volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.rbd.secret_re: Reference to a Kubernetes secret that provides the Ceph authentication key for the RBD volume.
Name of the Kubernetes Secret that holds the Ceph authentication credentials for the RBD volume.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.rbd.user: Specifies the RADOS user name used for authentication with the Ceph cluster. Defaults to "admin".
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.scale_io: ScaleIO represents a ScaleIO persistent volume source. This block configures the ScaleIO volume to be used as a volume in the pod.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.scale_io.fs_t: Filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system, e.g., ext4, xfs. Defaults to ext4.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.scale_io.gate: The host address of the ScaleIO API gateway.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.scale_io.prot: The name of the ScaleIO Protection Domain for the configured storage.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.scale_io.read: Marks the ScaleIO volume as read-only. When set to true, the volume is mounted with read-only permissions.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.scale_io.secr: secret_ref is a reference to a Kubernetes Secret that contains the ScaleIO admin password. It must be in the same namespace as the Pod, and is required for authentication with the ScaleIO system.
Name of the Secret object that contains authentication credentials for ScaleIO volume access.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.scale_io.ssl_: Enables or disables SSL communication with the ScaleIO Gateway. When true, the volume plugin connects to the gateway over SSL.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.scale_io.stor: Storage mode for the ScaleIO volume. Allowed values are 'ThinProvisioned' (default) and 'ThickProvisioned'.
The name of the ScaleIO storage pool in which the volume is created or from which it is provisioned.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.scale_io.syst: The name of the ScaleIO storage system.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.scale_io.volu: Name of the ScaleIO volume, as defined in the ScaleIO storage system.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.secret: secret is a volume source that references a Kubernetes Secret object, allowing the Secret's data to be mounted as files into the pod.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.secret.defaul: Specifies the default permission mode (in octal) applied to files within the secret volume. Defaults to 0644 if unspecified.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.secret.items: Optional list of key-to-path mappings for the secret volume. Each item specifies a key from the secret, the file path where that key should be mounted, and an optional permission mode. If omitted, all keys in the secret are mounted as files using their key names.
The key in the secret's data that should be exposed as a file. The file path is specified by the corresponding 'path' field in the same item.
The permission mode for the file, specified as a numeric value in octal (e.g., 420 for 0644). If omitted, the volume's defaultMode is used.
The relative path of the file to which the corresponding secret key is mapped within the volume's mount path. Must not contain '..' or start with '../'.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.secret.option: Specifies whether the referenced Secret must be defined. When true, the volume can still be used even if the Secret does not exist.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.secret.secret: The name of the Secret to mount as a volume. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.storageos: Defines a StorageOS volume source for the pod, providing configuration for mounting a StorageOS volume.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.storageos.fs_: Filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system. If not specified, the filesystem type is inferred from the volume.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.storageos.rea: Indicates whether the StorageOS volume is mounted as read-only. When set to true, the volume cannot be written to; default is false.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.storageos.sec: Reference to a Kubernetes Secret that contains StorageOS API credentials. If not set, default credentials will be attempted.
The name of the Secret that contains the StorageOS API credentials.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.storageos.vol: The name of the StorageOS volume to mount. This must match an existing volume in the StorageOS system.
volumeNamespace specifies the namespace of the StorageOS volume. If not set, it defaults to the Kubernetes namespace of the pod.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.spec.volumes.vsphere_volum: vsphereVolume represents a vSphere volume to be mounted into the container. It configures a vSphere datastore volume as a storage source for the pod.
Filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system. Ex. "ext4", "xfs", "ntfs". Implicitly inferred to be "ext4" if unspecified.
The storage policy ID based on which storage is provisioned for the vSphere volume.
The name of the vSphere storage policy to be applied to the volume. This policy determines storage characteristics such as performance and availability.
The datastore path that identifies the vSphere volume to mount, e.g., '[datastore1] vmdisk'.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.status.conditions.last_transition_time: last_transition_time is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. It is a string representing the timestamp in RFC3339 format, as defined in Kubernetes deployment status conditions.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.status.conditions.last_update_time: The last time the condition was updated, as a timestamp in RFC3339 format.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.status.conditions.message: A human-readable message providing details about the current condition, such as the reason for the deployment's state.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.status.conditions.reason: A brief, machine-readable reason for the condition's last transition, typically in CamelCase.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.status.conditions.status: The status of the condition, one of True, False, or Unknown.
kubernetes_apps_deployment.status.conditions.type: Type of the condition, e.g., Available, Progressing, or ReplicaFailure, indicating the specific aspect of deployment status being reported.

kubernetes_apps_replica_set.metadata.managed_fields.api_version: The API version of the resource that this manager operates on.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.metadata.managed_fields.fields_type: The type of the fields managed in this entry, such as 'FieldsV1'.

kubernetes_apps_replica_set.metadata.managed_fields.manager: The name of the manager (e.g., kubectl, a controller) that owns the managed fields entry.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.metadata.managed_fields.operation: The method used to apply the managed fields, typically 'Update' or 'Apply'.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.metadata.managed_fields.subresource: The subresource this managed field entry applies to, such as 'status' or empty string for the main resource.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.metadata.managed_fields.time: Time is the timestamp of when the ManagedFields entry was last updated. It is represented as an RFC3339-formatted string.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.metadata.owner_references.api_version: The API version of the owner resource referenced by this owner reference (e.g., 'apps/v1'). This specifies the group and version of the resource kind.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.metadata.owner_references.block_owner_de: Determines whether this owner reference blocks deletion of the owner until the dependent object is removed. If true, the owner cannot be deleted until this dependent is deleted or this field is set to false.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.metadata.owner_references.controller: Indicates whether the owner reference is the managing controller of this resource.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.metadata.owner_references.kind: The kind of the owner object, such as 'ReplicaSet' or 'Deployment'. This is a required field in OwnerReference.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.metadata.owner_references.name: The name of the referenced owner object, as defined in the Kubernetes object's metadata.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.metadata.owner_references.uid: The UID of the owner object referenced by this owner reference. This uniquely identifies the owning resource in the cluster.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.selector.match_expressions.key: The label key that the selector expression applies to.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.selector.match_expressions.operator: The operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.selector.match_expressions.values: A list of values that the key must match when the operator is 'In' or 'NotIn'. This field is used in a match expression for the label selector of a ReplicaSet.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.metadata.managed_fields.ap: The API version used by the manager to modify the object. This field is part of a managed fields entry that tracks field ownership and management in Kubernetes.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.metadata.managed_fields.fi: The type of the fields in the managedFields entry, indicating the structure of the fieldsV1 field (e.g., 'FieldsV1').
fields_v1 is a JSON representation of the fields owned by the manager. It contains the exact set of fields managed by this entry, serialized as a JSON object.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.metadata.managed_fields.ma: The name of the manager (e.g., a controller or user) that last modified the fields managed by this entry. This is part of the Kubernetes managedFields mechanism for tracking field ownership.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.metadata.managed_fields.op: Operation is the type of operation which lead to this ManagedFieldsEntry being created. The only valid values for this field are 'Apply' and 'Update'.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.metadata.managed_fields.su: Specifies the subresource (e.g., 'status') that this managed fields entry applies to, or an empty string for the top-level resource.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.metadata.managed_fields.ti: The timestamp of when these managed fields were set, in RFC3339 format. It is always empty if the operation is 'Apply'.
The API version of the owner object referenced by this owner reference (e.g., 'apps/v1'). This identifies the group and version of the referenced resource.

kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.affinity.node_affinit: The node selector term that specifies the preference for node affinity scheduling. It contains matchExpressions and matchFields fields that define the node selection constraints.
A list of node selector requirements that define which nodes are considered preferred. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator, and a list of values to match against node labels.
The Kubernetes label key that the node affinity match expression applies to. For example, 'disktype' or 'kubernetes.io/os'.
The operator represents the relationship between the key and the set of values. Allowed values: In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, Lt.

A list of values that the node's label key must match, depending on the operator. For operators In and NotIn, this list enumerates the allowed or disallowed values; for Exists and DoesNotExist, it must be empty.

A list of node selector requirements that specify node fields (e.g., metadata.name) to match for this node affinity preference. Each requirement defines a field key, operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optional values.
The key that the match requirement applies to, such as a node label or field name used in the node selector term.
The operator represents the relationship between the match label key and a set of values. Allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt.

The list of values for the node selector requirement. The allowed values depend on the operator: for In and NotIn, this must be a non-empty list of valid label values; for Exists and DoesNotExist, this must be empty; for Gt and Lt, this must contain exactly one numeric string value.
The weight of the node affinity preference, used to calculate the relative importance of this preference. Must be an integer between 1 and 100, inclusive.

A list of label selector requirements that constrain which nodes match this selector term. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, Lt), and optional values, and all requirements are ANDed together.
The label key that the node selector requirement applies to. The node must have this label key for the requirement to match.
Specifies the operator for the match expression. Allowed values: In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, Lt.

A list of string values for a node selector requirement. When the operator is In or NotIn, this list must be non-empty and the label key must match one of these values; when the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist, this list must be empty.

A list of node selector requirements that match on node fields (e.g., metadata.name). Each requirement specifies a key, an operator, and a list of values, similar to matchExpressions but for node fields.
The key is the name of the node field (e.g., metadata.name) that this selector requirement matches against.
Specifies the operator to use when matching a node selector field against values.

The list of values that the node field (identified by 'key') must match. The operator (e.g., In, NotIn) defines how these values are used; for operators like Exists or DoesNotExist, the list must be empty.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.affinity.pod_affinity: Defines a pod affinity term for a preferred scheduling rule. This includes a label selector, optional namespaces, and a topology key that specify which pods the affinity applies to and the scope of the affinity.

A label query over the pods to form the affinity term. It specifies the pods whose labels must match for the affinity rule to apply, using standard label selector semantics (matchLabels and matchExpressions).

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a label key, an operator (such as In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and, for In/NotIn, a list of string values. Only pods whose labels satisfy all requirements are selected.
The label key that the selector will match against. This is the key part of a label selector match expression, used to select pods by their labels.
The operator represents the relationship between the label key and the set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
List of values for the label selector match expression. For the In and NotIn operators, this list must be non-empty; for the Exists and DoesNotExist operators, it must be empty.
A map of key-value pairs that the target pod's labels must match. If specified, all specified labels must be present on the pod for this affinity term to be considered.

Specifies a list of label keys whose values from the incoming pod are used to construct a label selector for pod affinity. These keys are combined with the labelSelector to determine which pods are considered for affinity.
A list of pod label keys. When set, the affinity/anti-affinity term will only evaluate candidate pods whose label values for these keys differ from the new pod's label values.
A label selector used to select the namespaces that are considered when matching the pod affinity term. If omitted, only the pod's own namespace is considered.

A list of label selector requirements for matching namespaces. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and, for In/NotIn, a set of values. All requirements must be satisfied for the namespace to be selected.
The label key that the selector operates on. In a match expression, this is the key of the label to match against, such as 'app' or 'environment'.
The operator represents the relationship between the label key and the set of values. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.

values is a list of string values used by the match expression. When the operator is 'In' or 'NotIn', this list must be non-empty and contains the label values to match against. When the operator is 'Exists' or 'DoesNotExist', this list must be empty.
A map of label keys to values used to select namespaces. For the pod affinity term, only namespaces that have all specified labels will be considered when applying the preferred scheduling rule.
List of namespaces that the pod affinity term applies to. If unspecified, the namespace of the pod where the affinity is defined is used.
The label key that defines the topology domain used to match pods. Nodes must share the same label value for this key to be considered in the same topology domain (e.g., 'kubernetes.io/hostname').
Weight associated with the corresponding pod affinity term, in the range 1-100. Higher weights give the term more influence during scheduling.
Label selector used to identify the set of pods that the required pod affinity term applies to. It uses standard Kubernetes label matching rules to select pods based on their labels.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (such as In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and a list of values. The pod affinity rule is satisfied when the target pod's labels match all requirements in this list.
The label key that the selector applies to. It should be a valid Kubernetes label key, matching the key of a label on the pod.
The operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.

A list of string values that corresponds to the values in a label selector match expression. If the operator is 'In' or 'NotIn', this list must be non-empty; if the operator is 'Exists' or 'DoesNotExist', this list must be empty. The values are matched against the value of the specified label key.

matchLabels is a map of key-value pairs. A single {key,value} in the matchLabels map is equivalent to an element of matchExpressions, whose key field is "key", the operator is "In", and the values array contains only "value". The requirements are ANDed.

A list of pod label keys. Values from the incoming pod for these keys are merged into the label selector to match existing pods, enabling pod affinity/anti-affinity grouping based on dynamic pod labels.

A label selector to filter the namespaces that the affinity/anti-affinity term applies to. The term will match pods running in namespaces that match the label selector. If not specified, the pod's own namespace is used.

A list of label selector requirements that namespaces must satisfy to be eligible for the affinity rule. Each requirement defines a key, operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optional values. All expressions are ANDed together.
The label key that the selector matches on. In this context, it is used within namespaceSelector.matchExpressions for pod affinity rules, selecting namespaces by their labels.
Operator for the match expression, determining how the key is matched against the values. Allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
A list of values that the key must match according to the operator. For 'In' and 'NotIn' operators, this array contains the allowed values; for 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist', it must be empty.

match_labels is a map of label keys to values used to select namespaces by their labels. It specifies label requirements that the namespace objects must satisfy to be included in the namespace selector for this pod affinity rule.

A list of namespaces that the labelSelector should match. If not specified, it defaults to the namespace of the pod where the affinity term is defined, restricting pod affinity/anti-affinity to pods running in those namespaces.

The node label key that defines the topology domain for this pod affinity term (e.g., kubernetes.io/hostname). Pods are placed only on nodes that share the same value for this label as the matching pods.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.affinity.pod_anti_aff: Specifies the pod affinity term used in a preferred anti-affinity rule. It defines the group of pods (via label selector) and the topology key that determines the domains (e.g., nodes) where co-location with those pods should be avoided during scheduling.
Label selector used to identify the set of pods that this preferred anti-affinity term applies to. Supports matching on labels with `match_labels` and `match_expressions`.
A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and a list of values. The selector matches when all requirements are satisfied.
The label key that the selector expression applies to. In Kubernetes label selector matchExpressions, 'key' identifies the label on the resource that the operator and values are evaluated against.

The operator represents the relationship between the label key and the set of values in a label selector match expression. Allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist, where Exists and DoesNotExist do not require values.
A list of string values that the label selector's key must match. Required when the operator is 'In' or 'NotIn'; ignored for 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist'.
A map of key-value pairs. This label selector requires that the target pod has all of these label keys and values for the anti-affinity term to match.

A set of pod label keys used to select which pods will be considered for this affinity term. For each key, the value from the incoming pod's labels is merged with the labelSelector as 'key in (value)' to match existing pods. Keys that do not exist in the incoming pod labels are ignored.
NamespaceSelector is a label selector for the namespaces that the pod affinity/anti-affinity term applies to. If omitted, it defaults to the namespace of the pod where the affinity term is defined.

A list of label selector requirements for namespace selection. Each requirement defines a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally a list of values. The namespace selector matches namespaces that satisfy all specified requirements.
The label key that the selector applies to. This key must match a label on the namespace to select namespaces for the pod anti-affinity term.

The operator represents the relationship between the key and a set of values. Must be one of In, NotIn, Exists, or DoesNotExist. When the operator is In or NotIn, the values field must be set; if the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist, values must be empty.
A list of values for the label selector match expression. Required when the operator is 'In' or 'NotIn'; must be empty when the operator is 'Exists' or 'DoesNotExist'.
A map of key/value pairs that must be matched by the labels on a namespace for that namespace to be selected. Only namespaces that have all specified labels are considered.
A list of namespaces to which the label selector applies. If not set, the selector matches pods in the same namespace as the subject pod.
The key to use for the topology domain (e.g., kubernetes.io/hostname). Pods are considered to be in the same or different topology domains based on the value of this node label.
Weight associated with this preferred pod anti-affinity term, used to calculate the overall preference score. Must be an integer from 1 to 100.
A label query over the pods to select them for this pod anti-affinity term. The anti-affinity rule applies to pods matching these labels.
A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and a list of values. All requirements are combined with a logical AND.
The label key that the selector applies to. For example, in a selector like 'app=foo', the key is 'app'.
The operator to use for the label selector match expression. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
The list of values that the label selector expression matches when the operator is In or NotIn. For other operators, this field is ignored.

A map of key/value pairs that must match the pod's labels for the selector to apply. In this required PodAntiAffinity rule, the scheduler will not place the pod on the same topology domain (e.g., node) as any pod matching these labels.

A list of label keys. The labels with these keys from the pod being scheduled are combined with the label selector to restrict the set of pods that this anti-affinity term applies to. This helps narrow the scope of the anti-affinity rule to pods that share specific label values with the incoming pod.

A list of label keys that must not match the labels of the incoming pod. If a key is present in the incoming pod's labels, this term is ignored, preventing the anti-affinity constraint from applying to that key.
A label selector that restricts the pod anti-affinity rule to pods running in namespaces matching the specified labels. If not set, the rule applies only to the pod's own namespace.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement consists of a key, an operator (In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and an optional list of values. The namespace selector matches namespaces whose labels satisfy all specified expressions, thereby scoping the pod anti-affinity rule to those namespaces.
The label key used by this match expression to select namespaces in the pod anti-affinity rule. It must be a valid Kubernetes label key.
The operator represents the relationship between the label key and a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
Values is a list of string values. If the operator is In or NotIn, this list must be non-empty. If the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist, this list must be empty.
A map of key/value pairs used to match labels on namespaces. The pod anti-affinity constraint applies only to pods running in namespaces that have all specified label keys and values.
The namespaces field specifies the namespaces in which the label selector for the pod anti-affinity should be evaluated. If omitted, it defaults to the namespace of the pod that owns the affinity.
The topology key that defines the domain for pod anti-affinity, such as 'kubernetes.io/hostname' to spread pods across nodes or zones.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.containers.args: Arguments to the container's entrypoint. The list of strings passed to the command specified in the image or the container's command field, overriding any default arguments.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.containers.command: Command to run in the container, overriding the image's default entrypoint. Specified as a list of strings, where the first element is the executable and subsequent elements are arguments.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.containers.env: List of environment variables to set in the container. Each entry defines a variable name and value or a reference to a source for the value.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.containers.env.name: The name of the environment variable, as defined in Kubernetes. Must be a valid C identifier (e.g., MY_VAR).
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.containers.env.value: The value of the environment variable. This is optional and can be omitted if `valueFrom` is specified.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.containers.env.value_: Source for the environment variable's value. Selects a key from a ConfigMap or Secret, or references a pod field or resource, instead of defining the value literally. Must specify one of configMapKeyRef, secretKeyRef, fieldRef, or resourceFieldRef.
Selects a key from a ConfigMap to use as the value of the environment variable. The referenced ConfigMap must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
The key within the ConfigMap to select the value from.
The name of the ConfigMap to select from.
Indicates whether the ConfigMap or its key must be defined. If true, the container starts even if the referenced ConfigMap or key is missing.
Selects a field of the pod (e.g., metadata.name, metadata.namespace, spec.nodeName, status.podIP) to populate the environment variable's value.
The API version of the schema that fieldPath is written in terms of (e.g., 'v1'). If omitted, defaults to 'v1'.
The path to the field in the Kubernetes API that will be used as the value. For example, `metadata.name` or `metadata.namespace`.
Indicates whether the referenced key is required to exist. When set to true, the container will start even if the key is not present; when false or unset, the key must exist in the referenced file.
Selects a resource field of the container, such as limits.cpu or requests.memory, to expose as the environment variable's value. Only resource limits and requests are currently supported.
The name of the container whose resource field is referenced. If omitted, the resource field refers to the pod itself.

The divisor for the resource field reference, expressed as a Kubernetes quantity (e.g., '1', '1k', '1Mi'). The resource value is divided by this divisor before being set as the environment variable value.
Resource is the name of the resource being referenced, such as 'limits.cpu' or 'requests.memory'.
SecretKeyRef selects a key of a Secret in the pod's namespace. It contains the name of the Secret and the key to retrieve, enabling the container to consume that value as an environment variable.
The key of the secret to select from. Must be a valid secret key, such as the name of a key in the secret's data.
The name of the Secret resource that contains the key. This must be the name of a Secret in the same namespace as the pod.
Specify whether the Secret or its key must be defined. If set to true, an empty value is used when the secret or key is not found. Defaults to false.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.containers.env_from: List of sources to populate environment variables in the container. Each entry can reference a ConfigMap or Secret (or a prefix to add to variable names), allowing all key-value pairs from those sources to be injected as environment variables.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.containers.env_from.c: Refers to a ConfigMap whose key-value pairs are exposed as environment variables in the container. The referenced ConfigMap can be specified by name, and its entries become environment variables unless overridden by later envFrom entries or explicit env settings.
The name of the ConfigMap to reference. The keys of this ConfigMap become environment variables in the container.
Specifies whether the ConfigMap must be defined. If set to true, the ConfigMap may be absent and missing entries are ignored; if false, the ConfigMap must exist.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.containers.env_from.p: An optional identifier to prepend to each key in the ConfigMap or Secret. Must be a C_identifier.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.containers.env_from.s: Reference to a Kubernetes Secret from which to populate environment variables in the container. Typically contains the name of the Secret and an optional flag to indicate whether the Secret must be defined.
Name of the Secret to use. Must be a valid Kubernetes object name (e.g., a lowercase RFC 1123 subdomain).
Specifies whether the Secret must be defined. If true, the Secret may be absent and the environment variables from it are omitted. Defaults to false.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.containers.image: The container image to run in this container, e.g., 'nginx:latest'.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.containers.image_pull: Specifies when the kubelet should pull the container image. Allowed values are Always, IfNotPresent, and Never; if omitted, Kubernetes applies its default behavior based on the image tag.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.containers.lifecycle: Lifecycle configuration for the container, defining hooks such as postStart and preStop that execute during container startup and shutdown.
Defines the handler for the postStart lifecycle hook, which is executed immediately after the container is started. The handler can be one of exec, httpGet, or tcpSocket.

Exec specifies the command to be run in the container as part of the post-start lifecycle hook. The command is executed directly inside the container, and its exit status determines whether the hook is considered successful.
The command to run inside the container during the postStart lifecycle hook. It is expressed as an array of strings, where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments.

Performs an HTTP GET request to a container endpoint as a post-start lifecycle hook. Success is determined by an HTTP response code in the 200–399 range; the handler configuration includes host, port, path, scheme, and headers.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP; consider setting the Host header via httpHeaders instead.
List of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request made by the post-start lifecycle hook. Each entry defines a header name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request. Must be a valid HTTP header name (e.g., 'X-My-Header').
The value of the HTTP header field.
The path to access on the HTTP server for the HTTP GET request. For example, /healthz.
The port number or name of the HTTP GET request. Accepts a numeric port as a string (e.g., "8080") or a named port defined in the container's ports.
The protocol (scheme) to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are `HTTP` and `HTTPS`; defaults to `HTTP`.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Valid values are HTTP and HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP.
SleepAction specifies a sleep action for the postStart hook, with a required `seconds` field indicating the duration in seconds to sleep.
The number of seconds to sleep for the sleep action in the postStart lifecycle hook.

Specifies a TCP socket action to be performed during the postStart lifecycle hook. The container runtime attempts to open a connection to the specified port (and optional host) to determine if the hook succeeds.
The host name or IP address to connect to. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP.
The TCP port to connect to on the container. It can be a numeric port number or a named port (as a string).

Defines the pre-stop lifecycle hook, which is executed immediately before a container is terminated. It can contain an exec command, an HTTP GET request, or a TCP socket check to perform cleanup or graceful shutdown.
Exec specifies the action to take, which is to execute a command inside the container. This is an ExecAction object that contains the command to run as part of the preStop lifecycle hook.

Command is the command line to execute inside the container for the preStop lifecycle hook. It is run directly, not via a shell, and must complete before the container is terminated; the list's first element is the executable, with subsequent elements as arguments.
Defines an HTTP GET request that Kubernetes sends to the container before it is stopped. This hook allows the container to perform cleanup by receiving an HTTP GET on the specified endpoint.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request sent to the container's lifecycle pre-stop hook. Each header consists of a name and a value.
The name of the HTTP header for the preStop lifecycle hook's HTTP GET request.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the request.
Path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/' if not specified. This is the URL path for the HTTP GET request sent to the container.
Port number or name of the port to access for the HTTP GET request in the preStop hook. Must be an integer port number or a named port defined in the container's ports.
The protocol (scheme) to use for the HTTP GET request. In Kubernetes, this is typically 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'.
The scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS.

Defines a sleep action for a preStop lifecycle hook, causing the container to pause for a specified number of seconds before being terminated. The object contains a required 'seconds' field that sets the duration of the sleep.
The number of seconds the container sleeps during the preStop hook, delaying termination to allow graceful shutdown or cleanup.

Specifies a TCP socket handler for the preStop lifecycle hook, which opens a TCP connection to a given port on the container. The handler triggers the preStop action by successfully connecting to the specified port, typically used to signal an application to shut down gracefully.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket action. If omitted, defaults to the pod IP.
The TCP port to connect to for the preStop lifecycle hook. This can be a numeric port or a named port defined in the container. If empty, defaults to the container's first defined port.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.containers.liveness_p: Defines the liveness probe for the container. The kubelet periodically executes the probe and restarts the container if the probe fails.
Exec specifies the command to execute inside the container. The probe is considered successful if the command exits with status code 0.
Command to run inside the container. The first element is the executable, and subsequent elements are arguments. A non-zero exit code indicates failure for the liveness probe.
The number of consecutive failures allowed before the liveness probe is considered failed and the container is restarted. Defaults to 3, minimum value is 1.
grpc configures a gRPC-based liveness probe. It contains the port to query and an optional service name.
The port number on which the gRPC health check is performed. If not specified, defaults to the first port in the container's port list. Must be a valid port number (1-65535).
Service is the name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default behavior defined by gRPC is used.
Specifies the HTTP GET request to perform for the container's liveness probe. This includes the path, port, and optional headers for the health check.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP probe. Defaults to the pod IP.
A list of HTTP headers to send in the HTTP GET request for the liveness probe. Each header is defined as an object with a name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the request.
The value of the HTTP header that will be sent in the liveness probe's HTTP GET request.
The path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/'.

The port number or name of the port on the container to which the HTTP GET request should be sent for the liveness probe. This can be a numeric port (e.g., "8080") or a named port defined in the container's ports.
The protocol (scheme) to use for the HTTP GET request, typically HTTP or HTTPS.
The URL scheme (HTTP or HTTPS) to use for the HTTP GET request in the liveness probe. Defaults to HTTP.
Number of seconds after the container has started before liveness probes are initiated. Defaults to 0.
Specifies the frequency (in seconds) at which the liveness probe is performed. Defaults to 10 seconds; the minimum value is 1.
Minimum consecutive successes required for the liveness probe to be considered successful after it has failed. Defaults to 1, and must be 1 for liveness probes.
Configuration for a TCP socket probe in a liveness check. Specifies the host (optional) and port (required) to attempt a TCP connection to determine container health.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket probe. If not specified, the pod IP address is used.
The TCP port to probe. Provide a port number (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container's ports. This field is required for tcpSocket probes.

Number of seconds after which the liveness probe times out. If the probe does not complete within this duration, the probe is considered failed and the container is restarted according to the failure threshold.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.containers.name: The name of the container. This must be unique within the pod and must be a valid DNS label.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.containers.ports: Specifies the list of container ports to expose. Each port object defines the container port number and optionally the protocol (TCP or UDP), a name, and a host port mapping.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.containers.ports.cont: The port number on the container to which the service will connect. Must be a valid TCP/UDP port (1-65535).
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.containers.ports.host: The IP address of the host to bind the port to. If not specified, the port is bound to all host interfaces.
The port on the host node that the container port is exposed on. When set, the container is accessible from outside the cluster via the node IP and this port.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.containers.ports.name: Optional name for the container port. Must be an IANA_SVC_NAME and unique among all ports in the pod. If specified, it can be referenced in service definitions.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.containers.ports.prot: Protocol for the container port. Valid values are 'TCP', 'UDP', and 'SCTP'. Defaults to 'TCP' if not specified.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.containers.readiness_: Defines a probe that determines when the container is ready to accept traffic. If the probe fails, the container is removed from service endpoints until it succeeds again.
Exec specifies the action to take in the container, which is executed to determine the container's readiness. The container is considered ready if the command exits with 0.
The command to execute inside the container. The exit code of the command is used to determine the probe result: 0 indicates success, any non-zero code indicates failure.
The number of consecutive failed probe attempts after which the container's readiness is considered failed and the container is removed from service endpoints. Must be an integer greater than 0.
Specifies the gRPC health check parameters used by the readiness probe, including the gRPC service and port to contact.
The port number on which the gRPC server is listening. The readiness probe connects to this port to perform the gRPC health check.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default is an empty string, which causes the gRPC server to return its default health status.
Configures an HTTP GET request used by the readiness probe to check the container's health. The probe succeeds if the HTTP response status code is in the 200-399 range.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the Pod IP; if specified, it overrides the host header.
Custom headers to set in the HTTP request. Each item defines a header name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request for the probe.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the request.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server when performing the readiness probe. For example, /healthz.
The port to connect to on the container for the HTTP GET probe. Can be a numeric port or a named port defined for the container.
Protocol for the HTTP GET request. Valid values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS', with 'HTTP' as the default.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request, either HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP if not specified.
Number of seconds after the container starts before the first readiness probe is initiated. Defines a delay to allow the application to become ready before probe checks begin.
How often (in seconds) to perform the probe. Defaults to 10 seconds, minimum value is 1.

The number of consecutive successful probe responses required for the container to be considered ready after having been in a failed state. For readiness probes, this must be 1 (the default and only allowed value).
TCP socket probe action that checks whether a TCP connection can be established to the container on the specified port. It contains fields for the port and optionally the host to connect to.
Specifies the hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket readiness probe. If omitted, the pod IP is used.
The TCP port that the readiness probe checks. Can be a numeric port or a named port on the container.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second; minimum value is 1.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.containers.resize_pol: A list of container resize policies. Each policy specifies a resource name (e.g., cpu, memory) and a restart policy ('Always' or 'OnFailure') that determines whether the container should be restarted when that resource is resized. Used for in-place pod resize.
The name of the container resource (e.g., cpu or memory) to which this resize policy applies.

Defines the restart behavior for a container when its resource resize policy is triggered. In Kubernetes, valid values are 'NotRequired' (no restart) and 'RestartContainer' (restart the container to apply the resize).
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.containers.resources: Compute resources required by the container, specifying resource requests and limits (e.g., CPU and memory) for scheduling and runtime enforcement.
Claims lists the ResourceClaim objects that declare which cluster resources this container requires. Each entry references a ResourceClaim by name in the same namespace.
Name of the ResourceClaim that this container requests. This must match the name of a ResourceClaim object in the same namespace.

The maximum amount of compute resources allowed for the container. Keys are resource names such as 'cpu' and 'memory'; values are Kubernetes quantity strings, for example '500m' for CPU or '1Gi' for memory.
Map of resource names (e.g., cpu, memory) to the minimum amount of compute resources required for the container. The scheduler uses this to decide which node to place the pod on.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.containers.restart_po: Restart policy for the pod containing this container, defining when the kubelet should restart it. Allowed values are Always, OnFailure, and Never.
The operator used to compare the container's exit code against the list of exit codes defined in this restart policy rule.
The list of numeric exit codes that this restart policy rule matches. When a container exits with one of these codes, the rule applies.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.containers.security_c: SecurityContext holds security configuration for a container, such as runAsUser, capabilities, readOnlyRootFilesystem, and SELinux options. When both SecurityContext and PodSecurityContext are set for a container, the container-level settings take precedence.
Controls whether a process can gain more privileges than its parent process. When false, the container is prevented from privilege escalation, such as via setuid or setgid binaries.
Defines the AppArmor profile applied to the container. The object includes a type field (e.g., RuntimeDefault, Localhost, Unconfined) and an optional localhostProfile used when type is Localhost.
The name of an AppArmor profile stored on the node's local filesystem, used when the profile type is set to 'Localhost'.
Specifies the AppArmor profile type: `RuntimeDefault`, `Localhost`, or `Unconfined`. When `Localhost` is used, the `localhostProfile` field must also be set.
Linux capabilities to add or drop for the container. The `add` and `drop` fields specify lists of capabilities to grant or remove relative to the default set.
Add specifies a list of Linux capabilities to add to the container's effective capability set, granting additional privileges beyond the defaults.
The 'drop' field is a list of Linux capabilities to remove from the container's default capabilities. For example, 'ALL' drops all capabilities.
Run container in privileged mode, granting extended privileges such as access to all host devices and capabilities.
procMount denotes the proc mount to use for the containers. The default is 'Default'; the only other option is 'Unmasked'.
Mounts the container's root filesystem as read-only, preventing writes to the root filesystem.
Specifies the GID (group ID) to run the container process with. Must be a non-negative integer; if unset, the runtime default group is used.
If true, the container must run as a non-root user. The kubelet will validate the image or container's user at runtime and will refuse to start the container if it runs as root.
The UID to run the container's main process as. If specified, the container will run as that user ID (e.g., 1000).
SELinux options for the container, specifying the SELinux context (user, role, type, and level) applied to the container's process.
The SELinux level label (e.g., 's0:c123,c456') applied to the container for MLS/MCS confinement.
The SELinux role label that applies to the container. This is part of the SELinux context and is used to enforce mandatory access control policies.
The SELinux type label assigned to the container, such as 'spc_t' or 'svirt_lxc_net_t'.
The SELinux user label for the container, such as 'system_u'. This corresponds to the user portion of an SELinux context.
