Configures the seccomp profile for the container. The object typically includes a `type` field (e.g., RuntimeDefault, Unconfined, Localhost) and, when type is Localhost, a `localhostProfile` field specifying the profile path.
localhost_profile specifies the path to a seccomp profile on the node's filesystem, used when the seccompProfile type is set to Localhost.
Type indicates which kind of seccomp profile will be applied. Valid values are Localhost, RuntimeDefault, and Unconfined.

Windows-specific security settings for this container. These options are honored only on Windows nodes, and if not set, the pod-level windows_options are used; if both are set, this container-level setting takes precedence.
The GMSA credential spec as a JSON string, used to configure the Windows container. This is mutually exclusive with the GMSA credential spec name.
The name of the GMSA credential spec to use for the container's security context. This is part of the Windows options for the security context.
If set to true, the container runs as a Windows HostProcess container, allowing it access to host resources and process namespace.
The Windows username used to run the container's main process. If not specified, the default is set by the container image.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.containers.startup_pr: Defines the startup probe for the container. It indicates whether the application in the container is started, and can be used to handle slow-starting containers. If configured, the liveness and readiness probes are not activated until the startup probe succeeds.
Exec specifies a command to run inside the container. The exit status of the command is used to determine probe success (0) or failure (non-zero).
The command to run inside the container for the startup probe. It is a list of strings; the first element is the command and the remaining elements are arguments to the command.
The number of consecutive failures required for the startup probe to be considered failed. Once this threshold is reached, the container is terminated according to the restart policy. Defaults to 3.
Defines a gRPC health check for the startup probe. It specifies the port to check and optionally the service name for the gRPC health check.
Port number to use for the gRPC probe. Must be set to the port on which the gRPC service is listening.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default behavior is defined by the gRPC health checking protocol.
Defines an HTTP GET request used by the startup probe to check container health. It configures parameters such as the request path, port, headers, and scheme.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request in the startup probe. If not set, it defaults to the pod IP address.
List of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request for the startup probe. Each item defines a header name and value, allowing the probe to send additional or overriding headers.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request, for example 'X-Custom-Header'.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the startup probe's HTTP GET request.
Path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/'.
The port to access on the container for the HTTP GET request. Accepts a port number (1-65535) or an IANA_SVC_NAME port name.
The protocol (scheme) to use for the HTTP GET probe request, such as HTTP (default) or HTTPS.
The URI scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP when not specified.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the startup probe is initiated.
period_seconds defines how often the kubelet performs the startup probe, in seconds. Defaults to 10; minimum value is 1.
Minimum consecutive successes for the startup probe to be considered successful after having failed. Defaults to 1.
Configures a TCP socket probe for the startup probe. Contains the host and port to check for a TCP connection.
Optional host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket probe. If not specified, defaults to the pod's IP address.
The TCP port to connect to. Can be a numeric port (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container's ports.
Number of seconds after which the startup probe times out. If the probe does not return within this period, the container is considered to have failed the probe.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.containers.stdin: Whether this container should have a stdin stream allocated. This allows the container to read from standard input. Defaults to false if not specified.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.containers.stdin_once: When true, the container runtime closes the stdin channel after a single client attaches, causing stdin to be closed after the first attach session ends. If false (default), stdin remains open across multiple attaches and never receives EOF for processes reading from stdin.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.containers.terminatio: Path where the container's termination message is written. Defaults to /dev/termination-log.
Defines how the container's termination message is recorded. Allowed values: 'File' (default) or 'FallbackToLogsOnError'.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.containers.tty: Indicates whether a pseudo-TTY should be allocated for the container, enabling interactive terminal sessions.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.containers.volume_dev: volume_devices is a list of volume devices that map raw block devices to the container. Each item in the list defines a device name (matching a volume name) and a path within the container where the device is exposed.
The path inside the container where the block device is to be mounted or exposed.
Name of the volume device. Must match the name of a volume in the pod.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.containers.volume_mou: List of volumes to mount into the container's filesystem. Each entry specifies the name of a volume, the mount path within the container, and additional options such as read-only or subPath.
Path within the container at which the volume should be mounted.

Controls how volume mount propagation is handled between the host and container. Allowed values are None (no propagation, default), HostToContainer (host mounts are visible in the container), and Bidirectional (mounts propagate both ways).
The name of the volume to mount. Must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec.
Specifies whether the volume is mounted as read-only. When true, the container can only read from the volume and cannot write to it.
Determines whether the read-only setting for the volume mount is applied recursively to all subdirectories, not just the mount point itself.
Path within the volume from which to mount the volume into the container. Used to reference a subdirectory or file within the volume instead of its root.

This field allows the subPath (the path within the volume from which to mount) to be defined using environment variable references. The syntax $(VAR_NAME) is expanded before mounting, enabling dynamic subpaths based on environment variables. It is an alternative to subPath when variable expansion is needed.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.containers.working_di: Container's working directory. If not specified, the container runtime's default is used. This corresponds to the `workingDir` field in the Kubernetes container spec.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.dns_config.options.na: The name of the DNS resolver option to configure. Common options include 'ndots' and 'timeout'.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.dns_config.options.va: The value for a DNS resolver option, as part of a key-value pair in the pod's DNS configuration. The option name is specified by the corresponding 'name' field. This field may be omitted for boolean options that don't take a value.
Arguments to the entrypoint of the ephemeral container. This is the list of strings passed as arguments to the container's command, overriding any default arguments in the image.
The command to run in the ephemeral container, equivalent to the Docker ENTRYPOINT. Overrides the image's entrypoint; the array is passed directly to the runtime without a shell.
List of environment variables to set in the ephemeral container. Each entry specifies a variable name and optionally a value or value source.
Name of the environment variable, used to reference it within the container.
The value of the environment variable. This is a literal string value assigned to the variable. Alternatively, the value can be sourced from a reference using the 'valueFrom' field.
Source for the environment variable's value. Selects a key from a ConfigMap or Secret, or a field of the pod (e.g., metadata.name, spec.nodeName). Cannot be used with the 'value' field.
Selects a key from a ConfigMap to populate an environment variable. The object specifies the ConfigMap name and the key, and optionally whether the key is required.
The key within the referenced ConfigMap to select the value for this environment variable.
Name of the ConfigMap being referenced.
Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap key must exist. When true, the key is optional and missing it will not cause an error; when false (default), the key must be present.

Selects a field of the pod (e.g., metadata.name, spec.nodeName, status.podIP) to expose as the environment variable's value. The fieldRef object must specify a fieldPath, and optionally an apiVersion for the field definition.
APIVersion is the version of the schema the fieldPath is written in terms of. If not specified, the version of the schema of the object is used.
The path to the desired field in the pod's specification, such as `metadata.name`, `metadata.namespace`, or `spec.nodeName`. This field is required and follows the Kubernetes FieldRef syntax.
The key within the referenced file that maps to the value to be used for the environment variable.
Specifies whether the referenced key must exist. If true, a missing key will not cause an error and the environment variable will be omitted from the container's environment.
The name of the volume that contains the file referenced as an environment variable value.
Reference to a container resource field (e.g., limits.cpu or requests.memory) whose value is used to populate this environment variable.
The name of the container to select the resource field from. Required if the resource is a container-specific resource; otherwise defaults to the current container.
Divisor is the divisor for the resource value. Defaults to 1 if not specified. Must be a valid quantity string (e.g., '1', '100m').
The name of the resource to select, such as 'limits.cpu' or 'requests.memory'.

secretKeyRef selects a key of a Secret in the Pod's namespace to use as the value for the environment variable. The referenced Secret must exist in the same namespace as the Pod, otherwise the container may fail to start depending on the optional field's value.
The key of the secret to select. Must be a valid secret key.
The name of the Kubernetes Secret from which the key is selected.

Specify whether the Secret or its key must be defined. If set to true, the reference is optional and the environment variable is left unset if the Secret or key is missing; if false (default), the Secret and key must exist.
A list of sources to populate environment variables in the ephemeral container, such as ConfigMap or Secret references.
The reference to a ConfigMap in the pod's namespace. When specified, the ConfigMap's data keys become environment variables in the ephemeral container.
The name of the ConfigMap to reference for environment variables.
Indicates whether the referenced ConfigMap must be defined. If set to true, the ConfigMap may be absent and the container will still start; if false (default), the ConfigMap must exist.
An optional identifier that is prepended to each key from the referenced ConfigMap or Secret when creating environment variables.
Reference to a Secret whose data should be exposed as environment variables. The Secret's keys become environment variable names in the container.
The name of the Secret resource to use as the source for environment variables.
Specify whether the referenced Secret must be defined. If set to true, the Secret is optional and the container can start even if the Secret does not exist.
The container image to use for the ephemeral container.

The image pull policy for the ephemeral container. Allowed values are Always, IfNotPresent, and Never. If not specified, the behavior defaults to IfNotPresent unless the image tag is 'latest' or the image is not tagged, in which case it defaults to Always.
Lifecycle defines lifecycle hooks for the ephemeral container, such as postStart and preStop events that are executed during container startup and shutdown.
postStart is a lifecycle hook that runs immediately after a container is created. This object specifies the handler to execute, such as an exec command, HTTP GET request, or TCP socket check.
Exec specifies the action to run a command inside the container. The command is executed in the container's default working directory.

The command to execute for the postStart lifecycle hook. The first element is the executable, and subsequent elements are arguments. It is run directly, not inside a shell, with the container's root ('/') as the working directory.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform as the post-start lifecycle handler. Defines the endpoint and parameters for the request.
The hostname to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
Custom HTTP headers to include in the GET request. Each header is an object with a `name` and `value` field.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the GET request, such as 'Authorization' or 'Content-Type'.
The value of the HTTP header field.
Path to access on the HTTP server for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to '/'.
The port number or named port on the container to access for the HTTP GET request. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or an IANA_SVC_NAME if using a named port.
Protocol for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The URI scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS; if not specified, defaults to HTTP.

The sleep handler specifies a duration to pause the container process after startup. It is a lifecycle postStart handler that contains a 'seconds' field (int64) defining the sleep duration in seconds.
Specifies the duration in seconds for the sleep action in the post-start lifecycle hook. This value is required and must be a non-negative integer.

Defines a TCP socket action for the postStart lifecycle hook. The container runtime attempts to open a TCP connection to the specified host and port; a successful connection indicates the container is ready.
The host name or IP address that the TCP socket action connects to.
The TCP port to connect to. Accepts a numeric port or a named port defined in the container's port list.

PreStop is a lifecycle hook that is executed immediately before a container is terminated. It is an object defining the action to perform, such as an exec command, HTTP GET request, TCP socket probe, or sleep, as specified in the Kubernetes lifecycle handler.
Exec specifies the command to execute inside the container as part of the preStop lifecycle hook. This is an ExecAction that runs a command when the container is about to be terminated.

The command line to execute inside the container for the preStop lifecycle hook. It is provided as a list of strings, where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments. The command is executed directly, not via a shell, so shell features like pipes or redirects require invoking a shell explicitly. A zero exit status is required for the hook to succeed.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to execute as part of the container's pre-stop lifecycle hook.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP; set the 'Host' header via httpHeaders instead if needed.
Custom HTTP headers to send in the GET request. Each item in the list defines a header with a name and value.
The HTTP header name. Header names are case-insensitive.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request for the pre-stop lifecycle hook.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server when issuing the preStop lifecycle HTTP GET request.
The port number (as a string) or named port on the container to which the HTTP GET request is sent. Must be a valid TCP port number (1-65535) or the name of a port defined in the container's ports.
Protocol for the HTTP GET request. Must be HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP.
The scheme (HTTP or HTTPS) to use for connecting to the host; defaults to HTTP.
The sleep action to be executed in the preStop lifecycle hook. It uses a SleepAction object containing the `seconds` field to specify the duration of sleep in seconds.
Specifies the duration in seconds that the preStop lifecycle hook sleeps before the container is terminated.
Defines a TCP socket action to be performed by the pre-stop lifecycle hook, connecting to a specified port and host to signal the container before termination.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket. If not specified, the pod IP is used.
The TCP port to connect to for the preStop hook. Can be a port number (1-65535) or an IANA service name.
Exec specifies the action to take in a liveness probe. It defines the command to execute inside the container; the probe is considered successful if the command exits with status 0.
Command is the command line to execute inside the container, specified as a list of strings. The first element is the command and remaining elements are arguments.
Minimum consecutive failures for the liveness probe to be considered failed after having succeeded. Defaults to 3. Minimum value is 1.
Specifies a gRPC-based health check for the liveness probe. This object defines the gRPC port and optional service name to connect to for the probe.
The port number on the container that the gRPC liveness probe connects to. This is the port where the gRPC service is listening.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If this is not specified, the default behavior is defined by the gRPC health check protocol.
The HTTP GET action to perform for the liveness probe. Specifies the request path, port, and optional headers used to check container health.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
Custom headers to set in the HTTP request. Each item defines a header name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to set in the HTTP GET request for the liveness probe.
The value of the HTTP header to send in the liveness probe request.
The HTTP path to request in the HTTP GET request. Defaults to '/'.
The port on the container to which the HTTP GET request is sent, specified as a number or a named port within the container. For liveness probes, this must reference a port exposed by the container.
Protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Valid values are HTTP (default) and HTTPS.
The scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Valid values are HTTP and HTTPS.
Number of seconds after the container has started before liveness probes are initiated. Defaults to 0.
How often (in seconds) to perform the liveness probe. Defaults to 10 seconds. Minimum value is 1.
The number of consecutive successful probe results required after a failure for the liveness probe to be considered successful. For liveness probes, Kubernetes requires this value to be 1.
Specifies a TCP socket action for the probe. This configures the kubelet to check container health by attempting to open a TCP connection to a specific port (and optionally host) on the container.
Host is the host name to connect to for the TCP socket probe; it defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
Number or name of the port to access on the container. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or a port name defined in the container's ports list.
Specifies the number of seconds the pod is allowed to terminate gracefully before being forcefully killed. A value of zero means immediate deletion.
Number of seconds after which the liveness probe times out. Must be greater than or equal to 1. Defaults to 1 second if not specified.
The name of the ephemeral container. This name is used to identify the container within the pod.
A list of ports to expose from the ephemeral container. Each item defines a network port with properties such as the container port number, protocol, and optional name and host port.
The port number that the ephemeral container exposes to the network.
The host IP address to bind the port to. If not specified, the port binds to all interfaces (0.0.0.0).
The port on the host node to which the container port is mapped. If specified, the container port is accessible on the host at this port. Must be a valid port number (1-65535).
The name of the port, optional but if specified must be a valid IANA_SVC_NAME (up to 15 characters, lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens). This name must be unique within the pod.
The network protocol for this port. Allowed values are TCP, UDP, and SCTP.
Readiness probe configuration for this ephemeral container. Determines when the container is considered ready to accept traffic, based on the probe's success criteria.
Exec specifies the exec handler for this probe, which runs a specified command inside the container. A non-zero exit code indicates a probe failure.
The command to execute in the container for the exec probe, specified as a list of strings (the first element is the executable, followed by arguments).
The minimum consecutive failures for the probe to be considered failed after having succeeded. Defaults to 3; minimum value is 1.
grpc specifies the GRPC-based probe action. It includes the port to connect to and an optional service name for the probe.
The TCP port number to use when connecting to the gRPC server for this readiness probe. Valid values are 1-65535.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default behavior defined by the gRPC health checking protocol is used.
httpGet specifies the HTTP GET request to perform on the container's health check endpoint. It includes parameters such as path, port, and headers to use when checking container health.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET probe. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
Custom headers to set in the HTTP request. Each item contains a name and value pair.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the probe request. For example, "X-Custom-Header".
Path to access on the HTTP server.
The TCP port to query for the HTTP GET probe. This can be a numeric port or a named port defined in the container.
The protocol scheme to use for the HTTP GET request, either 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the readiness probe is initiated. Defaults to 0.
How often (in seconds) to perform the probe. Defaults to 10 seconds. Minimum value is 1.
The minimum consecutive successes required for the readiness probe to be considered successful after it has failed. Defaults to 1 and must be at least 1.

Specifies a TCP socket check for the probe. The kubelet attempts to open a TCP connection to the container's IP address at the given port; the probe is considered successful if the connection is accepted.
The host name or IP address to connect to. If not specified, uses the pod IP.
The TCP port to check for the readiness probe. Specify a numeric port (e.g., 8080) or a name of a port defined in the container.
Specifies the duration in seconds the container is allowed to terminate gracefully after a readiness probe fails, overriding the pod-level terminationGracePeriodSeconds if set.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second.

Defines the resize policy for the ephemeral container's resources. Each item specifies a resource name (e.g., cpu, memory) and a restart policy (NotRequired or RestartContainer) that controls whether the container is restarted when that resource is resized.
The name of the resource (e.g., cpu or memory) to which this resize policy applies.

Specifies the restart policy to apply when the container's resource size is changed. Allowed values are 'NotRequired' (the container can be resized without restart) and 'RestartContainer' (the container must be restarted to apply the new resource size).
Resource requirements for the ephemeral container, specifying requests and limits for compute resources such as CPU and memory.

List of resource claims that the ephemeral container requires. Each claim specifies a named resource defined by a ResourceClaim object, which must be available and bound before the container starts. This is an alpha feature used for advanced resource allocation.
Name of the ResourceClaim that this container references.
Request is the name of a specific request within the referenced ResourceClaim. If empty, the name of the ResourceClaim is used as the request name.

Limits describes the maximum amount of compute resources allowed for the ephemeral container. The key is a resource name (e.g., cpu, memory) and the value is a Kubernetes quantity (e.g., '100m', '1Gi').
Requests describes the minimum amount of compute resources required for the ephemeral container. This is a map of resource names (e.g., cpu, memory) to quantities, such as "100m" or "1Gi".
Operator used to compare the container exit code against the values in `exit_codes` (e.g., equality or inequality).
Security context defines privilege and access control settings for the ephemeral container, such as user and group IDs, Linux capabilities, SELinux options, and read-only root filesystem.
AllowPrivilegeEscalation controls whether a process can gain more privileges than its parent process. When set to false, the container is prevented from gaining additional privileges.

AppArmor profile settings applied to the ephemeral container. Supports defining a profile type (e.g., RuntimeDefault, Localhost, Unconfined) and an optional localhost profile name when type is Localhost.
Specifies the name of an AppArmor profile available on the node. This field is only required when type is 'Localhost'.
Type of AppArmor profile to use. One of: Localhost, RuntimeDefault, Unconfined. When set to Localhost, the localhostProfile field must be specified.

The capabilities field configures Linux capabilities for the ephemeral container, allowing specific capabilities to be added or dropped. It is part of the security context and is represented as an object with 'add' and 'drop' lists.
Specifies the Linux capabilities to add to the container's capability set, as a list of capability names.
Specifies Linux capabilities to remove from the container's default capability set. Each item is a capability name, such as 'ALL' or 'NET_ADMIN'.
Indicates whether the container runs in privileged mode, granting it access to all host devices and capabilities beyond the default allowed set.
Specifies how the /proc filesystem is exposed to the container's process, configured within the security context.
If true, the container's root filesystem will be mounted as read-only, preventing writes to the root filesystem.
Specifies the group ID (GID) with which to run the container's entrypoint process. This must be a numeric ID and overrides any group specified in the container image.

Indicates that the container must run as a non-root user. If true, the kubelet will validate the image at runtime to ensure that it does not run as UID 0, in which case the container will fail to start.
The numeric user ID (UID) that the container's processes run as. Overrides the user specified in the image; for example, 1000 or 0 for root.
SELinux options for the container, specifying the SELinux label (user, role, type, and level) that will be applied to the ephemeral container.
SELinux level label that applies to the container. It is a string that specifies the SELinux level, such as 's0:c123,c456'.
Role is a SELinux role label that applies to the container.
The SELinux type label for the container's security context, as part of the SELinux options. This specifies the type portion of the SELinux security policy applied to the ephemeral container.
The SELinux user label applied to the container's process.
The seccomp profile for the ephemeral container, defined in its security context. This object configures how system call filtering is applied to the container.
Path to a local seccomp profile. Used when the seccompProfile type is 'Localhost'. The profile must exist on the node's filesystem.
The type of seccomp profile to apply to the ephemeral container. Valid values are RuntimeDefault, Unconfined, and Localhost. When set to Localhost, the localhostProfile field must also be specified.
Windows-specific security context options for the container. This field is applicable only to Windows containers and includes settings such as credential spec and run-as-user.
Specifies the inline GMSA credential spec to use for the container. This is the content of the GMSA credential spec file, rather than a reference to a named GMSA spec.
The name of the GMSA (Group Managed Service Account) credential spec to use for the container. This references a pre-defined GMSA credential spec resource in the cluster.
Specifies whether the container should run as a HostProcess container. HostProcess containers run directly on the host and have access to host resources.
Sets the Windows user name under which the ephemeral container process runs. If unset, defaults to the user in the container image; a value here overrides any pod-level Windows options.

startup_probe defines a probe that indicates whether the container has successfully started. It allows kubelet to delay liveness checks for slow-starting containers, preventing restarts during startup.
Exec specifies the action to take in the container. It defines the command to run inside the container to determine if the startup probe is successful.
The command to run inside the container as part of the exec startup probe. It is a list of strings, where the first element is the command and the rest are arguments.
Minimum consecutive failures for the probe to be considered failed after having succeeded. Defaults to 3. Minimum value is 1.

Specifies a gRPC health check for the probe. The object includes the port (required) and optional service name used to perform the gRPC health check, following Kubernetes' built-in gRPC health checking protocol.
The port number on which the gRPC health check service is listening. Must be set to the port of the container's gRPC service.
The name of the gRPC service to check, placed in the HealthCheckRequest. If omitted, the gRPC default behavior is used.
Specifies the HTTP GET request to perform for this probe. Defines parameters such as path, port, and headers for the request.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
List of custom HTTP headers to include in the GET request of the startup probe. Each item specifies a header name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to be set in the HTTP request for the probe.
The value of the HTTP header to send in the startup probe's HTTP GET request.
The HTTP request path to probe, e.g., '/health'. If not specified, defaults to '/'.
The TCP port to send the HTTP GET request to. It can be a numeric port or a named port defined in the container.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request, either HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP' when not specified.
Number of seconds to wait after the container has started before initiating the startup probe.
How often (in seconds) to perform the startup probe. Minimum value is 1; defaults to 10.
The minimum consecutive successes required for the startup probe to be considered successful after a failure. Defaults to 1; for startup probes, the value must be 1.
Configures a TCP socket probe. The kubelet attempts to open a TCP connection to the container on the specified port; the probe succeeds if the connection is established.
The hostname or IP address to connect to. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP.
The TCP port number or named port on the container to probe. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535 or an IANA_SVC_NAME (port name). This field is required.
The number of seconds to wait for the container to terminate gracefully after a startup probe failure, overriding the pod's terminationGracePeriodSeconds if set.
Number of seconds after which the startup probe times out and is considered failed. Defaults to 1 second, and the minimum value is 1.
Whether the ephemeral container should allocate a buffer for standard input. If not set, reads from stdin in the container will always result in EOF. Defaults to false.
If true, the container's standard input will be closed after the first attach. This is only valid when stdin is set to true, and defaults to false.
Name of the target container that this ephemeral container shares its process namespace with. If not provided, the ephemeral container targets the Pod's first container.
Path where the container's termination message is written. Defaults to /dev/termination-log if not set.

Defines how the termination message of the container is read. Valid values are 'File' (default) meaning the termination message is read from /dev/termination-log, and 'FallbackToLogsOnError' meaning that if the termination message file is empty, the last portion of container logs is used.
Whether to allocate a TTY (pseudo-terminal) for the ephemeral container. If true, the container gets an interactive terminal. Defaults to false.
List of block device mappings for the ephemeral container. Each item specifies the name of a volume and the path inside the container where the device is exposed.
The path inside the container where the raw block device is mounted. Required when using volumeDevices to expose a block device to the container.
The name of the volume device, which must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec.
List of volume mounts for the ephemeral container. Each mount specifies a volume to mount into the container's filesystem, including the volume name and mount path.
The path within the ephemeral container at which the volume should be mounted. Must be an absolute path.
Mount propagation mode for the volume. Determines how mounts are propagated from the host to the container and between containers. Allowed values are None, HostToContainer, and Bidirectional.
The name of the volume to mount. Must match the name of a volume defined in the pod spec.
Indicates whether the volume mount is read-only. If true, the mount is read-only; if false, it is read-write.

Enables recursive read-only behavior for the volume mount. Supported values: Disabled, Enabled, IfPossible. If Enabled, all submounts are read-only. If IfPossible, the mount may be recursive read-only when the kernel supports it.
Mounts a sub-path of the referenced volume instead of its root, allowing a container to use a specific directory within a volume.

Specifies a path within the volume from which to mount, similar to subPath, but it can include environment variable references (e.g., $(POD_NAME)) that are expanded before mounting. Allows dynamic selection of the sub-path based on pod or container environment variables.
The working directory for the ephemeral container. Defaults to `/` if not specified. The container's current directory is set to this path when started.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.host_aliases.hostname: The list of hostnames to be resolved to the IP address specified in the same hostAlias entry.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.host_aliases.ip: The IP address for the host alias. Kubernetes adds an entry to the pod's /etc/hosts mapping this IP to the specified hostnames.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.image_pull_secrets.na: Name of the image pull secret to use. The referenced Secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod and is used for authenticating with image registries.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.args: List of arguments to pass to the init container's entrypoint. These override the default arguments from the container image.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.comma: Command to run in the container, overriding the image's default entrypoint. This is equivalent to Docker's ENTRYPOINT and is specified as a list of strings.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.env: List of environment variables to set in the init container. Each entry defines a variable name and either a direct value or a valueFrom source.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.env.n: The name of the environment variable to set in the init container. Must be a valid C identifier (e.g., alphanumeric characters and underscores, not starting with a digit).
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.env.v: The value of the environment variable. This can be a plain string or contain $(VAR_NAME) references to other variables.

EnvVarSource represents a source for the value of an environment variable. It can reference a ConfigMap key, a Secret key, a field of the pod (e.g., metadata.name), or a container resource (e.g., limits.cpu).
Selects a key from a ConfigMap to use as the environment variable value. This references a specific ConfigMap and key within it.
The key to select within the referenced ConfigMap.
Name of the ConfigMap from which to select the key value.
Specifies whether the ConfigMap key is required. If set to true, a missing key will not cause an error; the value will be left unset.
Selects a field of the pod (e.g., metadata.name, metadata.namespace, spec.nodeName) to use as the value for the environment variable. The selector includes apiVersion and fieldPath fields.
API version of the referent. If not specified, defaults to 'v1'.
The path to the field of the pod to select, such as metadata.name, metadata.namespace, spec.nodeName, spec.serviceAccountName, or status.podIP.

Indicates whether the referenced key must exist. If set to true, the environment variable may be left unset when the key is absent; if set to false (default), the container will fail to start if the key is missing.
The name of the volume that contains the referenced file.

Selects a resource field of the container (e.g., CPU or memory limits/requests) whose value is used as the value of the environment variable. The resource field reference is resolved from the container's resource specification.
The name of the container from which to select the resource value. Optional for environment variables; defaults to the container where the field is set.
Divisor is the value by which the resource quantity is divided. If unspecified, defaults to 1.
The resource name to select, e.g., 'limits.cpu', 'limits.memory', 'requests.cpu', or 'requests.memory'.

Selects a key of a Secret in the same namespace as the pod. This object contains the name of the Secret and the key whose value is used as the environment variable's value, with an optional 'optional' field indicating whether the key must be defined.
The key of the Secret to select from. Must be a valid Secret key.
Name of the Secret from which to retrieve the value. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Indicates whether the secret key must exist. If set to true, the key is optional; if false, the referenced key must exist in the secret.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.env_f: List of sources to populate environment variables in the init container. Each source can reference a ConfigMap or Secret, optionally with a prefix, and duplicate keys are resolved with later sources taking precedence.
The ConfigMap to select from. The data of the selected ConfigMap is added as environment variables in the container.
The name of the ConfigMap to reference. The referenced ConfigMap must exist in the same namespace.
Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap must be defined. If set to true, the ConfigMap is optional and its absence will not cause the container to fail to start.
An optional identifier to prepend to each key in the referenced ConfigMap or Secret. Must be a valid C identifier (e.g., 'MY_' becomes 'MY_KEY').
Reference to a Kubernetes Secret. The keys of the Secret are exposed as environment variables to the container.
Name of the Secret. Must be the name of a Kubernetes Secret object in the same namespace as the pod.
Specify whether the Secret must be defined.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.image: The container image to use for the init container (e.g., busybox:1.36). This is a required field in Kubernetes container definitions.

The image pull policy for the init container. Allowed values are 'Always', 'IfNotPresent', or 'Never'. 'Always' always pulls the image, 'IfNotPresent' pulls only if the image is not already present on the node, and 'Never' never pulls the image and relies on the image being locally available.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.lifec: Lifecycle describes actions that the container management system should take in response to container lifecycle events. It specifies handlers such as postStart and preStop.
The post_start hook is executed immediately after the container starts. If this hook fails, the container is killed and restarted according to its restart policy.
ExecAction configuration for the postStart lifecycle hook. Defines the command to execute in the container after it is started.
The command to execute in the container. It is an array of strings, where the first element is the executable and subsequent elements are arguments; the command is run directly without a shell.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform when the container is started. The request is used to determine whether the postStart lifecycle hook succeeded.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP request. If not specified, the pod IP is used.
Custom headers to set in the HTTP request. HTTP allows repeated headers.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request.
The value of the HTTP header. It is the actual data sent in the header.
The URL path for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to '/' if not specified.
The port number or named port to connect to for the HTTP GET request.
The protocol (scheme) to use for the HTTP GET request, such as 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request, either HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP.

The `sleep` field defines a SleepAction that causes the container lifecycle hook to wait for a specified number of seconds before proceeding. It is an object with a `seconds` field that denotes the sleep duration in seconds.
Seconds is the number of seconds to sleep during the sleep action of a postStart lifecycle hook.
Specifies a TCP socket action to be performed after the container starts. The tcpSocket handler contains host and port fields to define the connection target.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket action. If not specified, the pod IP is used.
The TCP port to connect to. This can be a numeric port number (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container's specification.
PreStop is a lifecycle hook that is called immediately before a container is terminated. It allows the container to perform graceful shutdown or cleanup before receiving the termination signal.

Exec specifies the exec action for the pre-stop lifecycle hook. It runs the given command inside the container before termination, with the command defined in the 'command' field as a list of strings.

Command is the command line to execute inside the container. It is specified as a list of strings, where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments. This command is run as part of the pre-stop lifecycle hook using the exec action.

Performs an HTTP GET request to a container's endpoint as the action for the pre-stop lifecycle hook. It defines the HTTP request parameters, such as the path and port, that will be sent to the container before it is terminated.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP; you may set this to override the host header and connection target.
Custom headers to set in the HTTP GET request. Each header is an object containing the header name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the GET request.
The HTTP header value to send in the pre-stop lifecycle hook's HTTP GET request.
Path to access on the HTTP server.
The port number or name of the container port to send the HTTP GET request to. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or an IANA service name.
The URL scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
Sleep is a lifecycle handler action that pauses the container for a specified number of seconds before termination. This object contains a `seconds` field that defines the sleep duration.
The number of seconds to sleep before the container is terminated as part of the preStop lifecycle hook.

Defines a TCP socket action for the pre-stop lifecycle hook. The hook attempts to connect to a specified port on the container's IP address, with an optional host override, to handle graceful termination.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket check. If omitted, defaults to the pod IP address.
The TCP port number (1-65535) or named port to connect to for the preStop lifecycle hook. This field accepts either an integer port or a string name of a port defined in the container.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.liven: Defines the liveness probe for the init container. The kubelet uses the probe to determine when to restart the container if it becomes unhealthy, based on the container's restart policy.
Exec specifies a command to run inside the container to determine its health. The container is considered healthy if the command exits with status 0.

The command and arguments to execute in the container for this liveness probe. This is the ExecAction's command; it is run directly, not via a shell, so shell features like pipes or variables are not available. The working directory is the container's root ('/').
Number of consecutive failures required for the liveness probe to be considered failed. After this many failures, the container is restarted. The minimum value is 1.
grpc is the gRPC-specific probe configuration. It defines the port to connect to and, optionally, the service name to check, allowing liveness checks via gRPC health checking.
The port number of the gRPC service to check for the liveness probe. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535.
The name of the gRPC service to check for liveness. If not specified, the probe checks the health of the entire gRPC server.
The HTTP GET action used to perform the liveness check on the init container.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
List of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request made by the liveness probe. Each object typically contains 'name' and 'value' fields.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the GET request from the probe. This is the key in the key-value pair defined in the httpHeaders list.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the probe request. This is paired with the header's name.
The HTTP path to access on the server. Defaults to '/' if not specified.

The port number or name of the port on the container to send the HTTP GET request to. For liveness probes, this must be a valid integer port (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container's containerPort list. This field is required for httpGet probes.
The protocol to use for the HTTP request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS' (case-insensitive). Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Valid values are HTTP and HTTPS.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the liveness probe is initiated. Defaults to 0.
How often, in seconds, to run the liveness probe. Minimum value is 1; default is 10.
Minimum consecutive successes required for the probe to be considered successful after having failed. For liveness probes, this value must be 1.
Configures a TCP socket probe that attempts to open a connection to a specific port on the container. If the connection succeeds, the probe is considered successful.
The hostname or IP address to connect to. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
The TCP port to connect to for the liveness probe. Accepts a port number (e.g., '8080') or a named port defined in the container.

The number of seconds the pod is allowed to terminate gracefully after a liveness probe failure before being forcefully killed with SIGKILL. If not set, the pod-level termination grace period is used; a value of 0 means immediate termination.
The number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second, and the minimum allowed value is 1.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.name: Name of the init container. Must be unique within the pod.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.ports: List of network ports to expose from the init container. Each port entry specifies a containerPort, protocol (TCP/UDP/SCTP), optional name, hostPort, and hostIP; primarily informational and used for network policy enforcement.
The port number that the container listens on. Must be a valid TCP/UDP port between 1 and 65535.
The host IP address to bind the hostPort to. If unset, defaults to 0.0.0.0 (all interfaces).
The port number on the host to map to the container port. If specified, must be a valid port number (1-65535). When omitted, defaults to the containerPort value.
The name of this container port. This must be an IANA_SVC_NAME and unique within the pod.
The protocol used for the container port. Must be one of TCP, UDP, or SCTP. Defaults to TCP if not specified.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.readi: The readiness probe for the container. For init containers, this field is ignored because init containers run to completion and do not support readiness probes.
Exec specifies a command to run inside the container. The probe succeeds if the command exits with a status code of 0, and fails for any non-zero exit code.

The command to run inside the container for the readiness probe. It is a list of strings; the first element is the command path and the rest are arguments. The command is executed directly without a shell; a non-zero exit status indicates failure.
The number of consecutive failures of the readiness probe that must occur for the container to be marked as not ready. The default value is 3, but it can be set to any positive integer.
GRPCAction specifies an action involving a gRPC port. It configures the readiness probe to perform a gRPC health check.
The port number of the gRPC service to connect to for the readiness probe.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If empty, the health check is for the whole service.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform for the readiness probe. The probe will access the container at the given port and path and consider it ready on a successful HTTP response.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
Specifies a list of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request sent by the readiness probe. Each header is an object with a name and a value.
The name of the HTTP header. This is part of a list of HTTP headers to send with the request.
The value part of a key-value pair for an HTTP header to send in the probe's GET request.
Path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/'.
The port number or name of the port on the container to connect to for the HTTP GET probe. Accepts a numeric port (1-65535) or an IANA service name.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request, typically HTTP or HTTPS.
The URL scheme to use for the HTTP GET request (e.g., HTTP or HTTPS).
Number of seconds after the container has started before the readiness probe is initiated. Defaults to 0.
How often (in seconds) to perform the readiness probe. Defaults to 10 seconds; minimum value is 1.

The minimum consecutive successes required for the readiness probe to be considered successful after it has failed. The default and minimum value is 1; larger values cause the probe to wait longer before marking the container ready.
Specifies a TCP socket action for the readiness probe. The probe attempts to open a TCP connection to the container's port, with optional host, to determine readiness.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket check. If not specified, the pod's IP address is used.
The TCP port to check for the readiness probe. It can be a port number or a named port defined in the container's ports.
The number of seconds after which the readiness probe times out. If the probe does not finish within this duration, it is considered failed. Defaults to 1 second.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.resiz: Defines the resize policy for container resources, allowing in-place resizing of resource requests/limits. Each object specifies a resource (e.g., cpu, memory) and a restart policy: Always, OnEviction, or Never.
The name of the resource to which the resize policy applies, such as cpu or memory.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.resou: Resource requirements for the init container, specifying requests and limits for compute resources such as CPU and memory.
List of ResourceClaim requirements for this container. Each entry specifies a ResourceClaim name that the container requires, used with the Dynamic Resource Allocation feature.
The name of the PersistentVolumeClaim to reference. This must match the name of a PersistentVolumeClaim in the same namespace.
Request is the name of the resource request within the ResourceClaimStatus. If omitted, it defaults to the name of the ResourceClaim.
Limits specifies the maximum amount of compute resources allowed for the init container. Each key is a resource name (e.g., cpu, memory) and the value is a quantity string such as '100m' or '1Gi'.
Requests specifies the minimum amount of compute resources required for the init container. The map's keys are resource names (e.g., cpu, memory) and values are resource quantities as strings.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.resta: Defines the restart policy for this init container. Allowed values are "Always" (runs as a sidecar for the duration of the pod) and "Never" (default, runs to completion exactly once per pod lifecycle). Only valid for init containers.
Defines how the exit codes in this rule are compared to the container's actual exit code to determine if the restart policy applies.
Specifies the list of numeric exit codes that trigger this restart policy rule.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.secur: SecurityContext defines the security settings (e.g., user, group, capabilities, SELinux options) for this init container. It controls the privilege and access control settings that apply to the container's processes.

AllowPrivilegeEscalation controls whether the process can gain more privileges than its parent process. When set to false, the container runs with the no_new_privs flag, preventing privilege escalation. The default is true, but setting it to false is recommended for security.
AppArmor profile settings for the container. Specifies the AppArmor profile to apply, including the type (e.g., RuntimeDefault, Localhost, Unconfined) and optionally the localhost profile name.

The name of the AppArmor profile to load when the type is Localhost. This field is used only when the appArmorProfile type is set to Localhost, and it specifies the profile name available on the node.
Specifies the type of AppArmor profile to apply to the container. Valid values are `RuntimeDefault`, `Localhost`, and `Unconfined`.
Linux capabilities to add or drop for the container, defining privileged operations the container is allowed to perform.
Adds the specified Linux capabilities to the container's effective capability set. For example, adding 'NET_ADMIN' grants network administration privileges.
Specifies a list of Linux capabilities to drop from the container's default set. For example, 'ALL' drops all capabilities.

Specifies whether the container should run in privileged mode. When true, the container's processes have nearly all capabilities as processes on the host, essentially disabling isolation and granting extended privileges.
Sets the proc mount type for the container. Allowed values are 'Default' (mask /proc for security) and 'Unmasked' (expose all processes). Defaults to 'Default' if not specified.
Indicates whether the container's root filesystem is mounted as read-only. When set to true, the container cannot write to its root filesystem, which is a common security hardening measure.
Specifies the group ID (GID) that the container's main process should run as. This is an integer value, typically a Unix group ID.
Indicates whether the container must run as a non-root user. If set to true, the container will not be allowed to run as root (UID 0), and the Kubernetes runtime will enforce this.
The numeric UID that the init container's process will run as. If set, it overrides the user specified in the container image.
SELinux options specify the SELinux context (label) applied to the container, including user, role, type, and level.
The SELinux level label applied to the container, as part of the SELinux options in the container's security context.
The SELinux role label assigned to the container. Part of the SELinux context used for role-based access control.
The SELinux type label, which defines the type domain for the process. In Kubernetes, it is part of the SELinux security context options.
The SELinux user label for the container. This is part of the SELinux options applied to the container's security context.

Configure the seccomp profile for the init container's security context. This object supports a `type` field (e.g., `RuntimeDefault`, `Localhost`, `Unconfined`) and an optional `localhost_profile` path to a custom seccomp profile.
The path to a seccomp profile in the node's local filesystem. This must be set when the seccomp 'type' is 'Localhost'.
The type of seccomp profile to apply. Allowed values are RuntimeDefault, Localhost, and Unconfined. When set to Localhost, the localhostProfile field must also be specified.
WindowsOptions holds Windows-specific security settings for the container, such as GMSA credentials and Windows user name. It is only applicable when the container runtime is Windows.
The name of a GMSA credential spec to use for the Windows container. This option is specific to Windows security contexts and references a pre-configured GMSA credential spec resource.
The name of the GMSA credential spec to use for the Windows container. This references a GMSA credential spec configured in the cluster.

HostProcess determines if a container should be run as a 'Host Process' container. When set to true, the container runs as a host process container on the Windows node. All containers in a pod must have the same effective HostProcess value.

The username to run the container's entrypoint process as for Windows containers. This is part of the WindowsSecurityContextOptions and is an alternative to the runAsUser field, which is not supported for Windows. The value should be in the format DOMAIN\User or User@Domain.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.start: Defines the startup probe settings for the init container. In Kubernetes, probes are not supported for init containers, so this field is not permitted and will be rejected by the API server.
Exec specifies the action to take by running a command inside the container. A successful command (exit code 0) indicates the probe passes.
The command to execute inside the container for this exec-based startup probe. It is run directly without a shell; a nonzero exit status indicates that the probe failed.
The number of consecutive failures required for the startup probe to be considered failed after which the container will be restarted. Minimum value is 1; default is 3.
gRPC probe configuration. Contains the port and optional service name used to perform a gRPC health check on the container.
Port number that the gRPC probe should connect to. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC health check request. If not specified, the default is the pod's name.
Performs an HTTP GET request against the container. The `http_get` configuration defines the endpoint (port and path) and optional headers used by the startup probe to check container health.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
List of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request for the startup probe. Each item defines a header name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the request. This is the header field name, such as 'Authorization' or 'X-Custom-Header'.
The value of the HTTP header for the GET request sent by the probe. This is a string and is used along with the header name to set the request header.
Path to access on the HTTP server, e.g., '/healthz'.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container. This is a string that can be a numeric TCP port (1-65535) or the name of a port defined in the container's ports list.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Valid values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS', with a default of 'HTTP'.
The scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Valid values are HTTP and HTTPS.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the startup probe is initiated. Defaults to 0, and must be a non-negative integer.
How often (in seconds) to perform the startup probe. Defaults to 10 seconds. Minimum value is 1.
Minimum consecutive successes required for the startup probe to be considered successful after having failed. For startup probes, this value must be 1; defaults to 1 if not specified.

Defines a TCP socket check used as the handler for the startup probe. The probe attempts to open a TCP connection to the specified port on the container, indicating readiness when the connection succeeds.
The host name to connect to for the TCP socket probe. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
The TCP port to connect to for the probe. Can be a numeric port or a named port.
The number of seconds after which the startup probe times out. The value must be at least 1.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.stdin: Whether this container should allocate a buffer for stdin in the container runtime. If this is not set, reads from stdin in the container will always result in EOF. Defaults to false.
When true, the container's stdin is closed after the first attach (or immediately if no attach). Defaults to false.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.termi: Path where the container's termination message is written. The kubelet reads this file to fetch the termination message when the container exits, and it defaults to /dev/termination-log.

Defines how the termination message of the container is populated. Valid values are 'File' (default) and 'FallbackToLogsOnError'. When set to 'File', the termination message is read from the file /dev/termination-log; when set to 'FallbackToLogsOnError', the last chunk of container log output is used if the termination message file is empty.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.tty: Indicates whether a pseudo-TTY should be allocated for the container. When set to true, the container gets a terminal attached, consistent with Docker's -t flag.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.volum: List of block devices to be used by the container, mapping each named volume to a raw block device path inside the container. This enables access to raw block volumes, as opposed to filesystem-mounted volumes.
The path inside the container at which the volume device is mounted.
The name of the volume device, which must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's volumes.

Specifies a list of volumes to mount into the init container's filesystem. Each volume mount must reference a volume defined in the Pod spec, and includes the mount path and mount options such as read-only or subPath.
Path within the container where the volume is mounted. Must be an absolute path, such as /data.
Controls how mount propagation is handled for this volume mount. Allowed values are None, HostToContainer, and Bidirectional.
The name of the volume to mount. This must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec.
Mounts the volume as read-only when true; defaults to false, allowing read-write access.
Path within the volume from which the container will be mounted. If not specified, the volume's root is mounted.

sub_path_expr specifies a sub-path within the volume to mount, with support for environment variable references (e.g., $(VAR_NAME)). It is an alternative to the static subPath field, allowing dynamic paths based on environment variables.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.worki: The container's working directory. If not specified, the default is '/'. Must be an absolute path.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.readiness_gates.condi: The name of a custom condition that must be satisfied for the pod to be considered ready. This is the key of a condition that a controller adds to the pod's status; the pod becomes ready only when all readiness gate conditions are true.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.resource_claims.name: The name of the resource claim, which must be unique within the pod and is referenced by containers to use this claim.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.resource_claims.resou: The name of the ResourceClaim resource that this pod requests. Must match the name of a ResourceClaim object in the same namespace.

The name of a ResourceClaimTemplate that is used to generate a ResourceClaim for this pod. When set, the ResourceClaim is created and deleted automatically for the pod's lifetime; mutually exclusive with resource_claim_name.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.resources.claims.name: Name of the ResourceClaim that this container references. The named ResourceClaim must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.resources.claims.requ: The name of the resource claim to request for the container, as specified in the pod's resource requirements.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.scheduling_gates.name: The name of the scheduling gate. This name uniquely identifies the gate within the pod spec and must be a valid DNS subdomain name. It is used to reference and remove the gate before scheduling.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.security_context.sysc: The name of the sysctl parameter, such as 'kernel.shm_rmid_forced'.
The value to set for the named sysctl parameter.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.tolerations.effect: The taint effect to match, such as NoSchedule, PreferNoSchedule, or NoExecute. If omitted, the toleration matches all effects.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.tolerations.key: The key of the taint that this toleration matches. If empty, matches all taints.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.tolerations.operator: The operator used to match the taint key. Allowed values are 'Equal' and 'Exists'. Defaults to 'Equal'.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.tolerations.toleratio: The duration in seconds for which the pod will tolerate a taint with a NoExecute effect, after which the pod will be evicted if the taint persists. This field is optional and only applies when the toleration's effect is NoExecute.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.tolerations.value: The value to match against the taint key when the operator is Equal. Must be left empty when the operator is Exists.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.topology_spread_const: Label selector is used to find matching pods. Pods that match this label selector are counted to determine the number of pods in each topology domain.
A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and an optional list of values.
The label key that the selector requirement applies to. In a match expression, this is the key of the label that must match the operator and values.
The operator represents the key's relationship to a set of values. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
A list of string values that the key must match. Required for operators In and NotIn; must be empty for Exists and DoesNotExist.
Label selector for topology spread constraints, expressed as a map of key/value pairs. All matchLabels requirements are ANDed to select the pods the constraint applies to.

List of pod label keys used to select the group of pods over which spreading is calculated. The topology spread is computed over pods that match these label keys with the labels of the pod being scheduled.

The degree to which Pods may be distributed unevenly. Must be greater than zero. The actual skew is calculated as the difference between the number of matching Pods in the most and least loaded topology domains.

An optional field specifying the minimum number of eligible domains required for the topology spread constraint to take effect. If the number of eligible domains is less than min_domains, the constraint is ignored (treated as having a global minimum of 0).

Indicates how to treat a node's nodeAffinity when computing pod spread. Valid values are 'Honor' (only nodes satisfying nodeAffinity are considered) and 'Ignore' (nodeAffinity is ignored). Defaults to 'Honor'.
Indicates how to treat tainted nodes when considering pod topology spread constraints. Allowed values are 'Honor' and 'Ignore'; if not set, the default is 'Ignore'.

The key of node labels that defines the topology domains for spreading pods. Nodes sharing the same value for this key are considered in the same domain, and pods are spread evenly across these domains.

Indicates how to handle a topology spread constraint when it cannot be satisfied. Valid values are 'DoNotSchedule' (default) and 'ScheduleAnyway'. 'DoNotSchedule' prevents scheduling the pod if the constraint cannot be met, while 'ScheduleAnyway' allows scheduling with best-effort spreading.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.aws_elastic_b: Defines an AWS Elastic Block Store (EBS) volume to be mounted into the pod. This volume source references an existing EBS volume by its ID and attaches it to the node.
Filesystem type to use when mounting the AWS EBS volume (e.g., ext4, ext3, xfs). If not specified, defaults to ext4.
The partition in the EBS volume from which to mount the volume. If omitted, the first partition is used by default; if the volume has no partitions, the whole volume is mounted.
If true, the EBS volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false if not specified.
The unique identifier of the AWS EBS volume to mount, typically in the format 'vol-xxxxxxxx'.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.azure_disk: azureDisk represents an Azure Data Disk mount on the host and bind mount to the pod.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.azure_disk.ca: Caching mode for the Azure disk. Allowed values: None, ReadOnly, ReadWrite. If not specified, the default is None.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.azure_disk.di: The name of the Azure data disk to mount. This is the disk name as it appears in the Azure resource, used to identify the VHD blob in storage.
The URI of the Azure disk to mount as a volume, corresponding to the diskURI field in the Kubernetes azureDisk volume source.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.azure_disk.fs: Filesystem type to mount, such as ext4, xfs, or ntfs. Defaults to ext4 if not specified.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.azure_disk.ki: Kind of the Azure disk. Possible values are 'Shared', 'Dedicated', or 'Managed'. Defaults to 'Shared'.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.azure_disk.re: Specifies whether the Azure disk volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.azure_file: azureFile is a volume source that represents an Azure File Service mount, allowing a pod to mount an Azure file share as a volume.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.azure_file.re: Specifies whether the Azure File share is mounted as read-only. When set to true, the volume cannot be written to from the pod.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.azure_file.se: The name of the Kubernetes Secret that contains the Azure Storage Account name and key for authenticating to the Azure file share.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.azure_file.sh: Name of the Azure File share to mount.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.cephfs: CephFS represents a Ceph Filesystem mount that lasts the lifetime of a pod. CephFS volumes do not support ownership management or SELinux relabeling.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.cephfs.monito: Required: A collection of Ceph monitor addresses (host:port) for the CephFS volume.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.cephfs.path: Path within the CephFS filesystem to mount. If not specified, defaults to the root directory '/'. This is the path on the Ceph cluster that will be exposed as the volume.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.cephfs.read_o: If true, the CephFS volume is mounted as read-only. This prevents writes to the volume from the pod.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.cephfs.secret: Path to a secret file on the CephFS filesystem that contains the authentication credentials for accessing the CephFS volume.
Reference to a Kubernetes Secret containing CephFS authentication credentials (keyring). The secret is used to authenticate to the Ceph cluster.
The name of the Kubernetes secret that contains the CephFS credentials.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.cephfs.user: The RADOS user name used for CephFS authentication. Defaults to 'admin'.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.cinder: Cinder represents a Cinder volume (OpenStack block storage) to be mounted into the pod. This volume is attached to the node and then mounted into the container filesystem.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.cinder.fs_typ: Filesystem type to mount on the volume, such as ext4 or xfs. If not specified, the system will use the default filesystem type of the underlying Cinder volume.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.cinder.read_o: Makes the Cinder volume read-only when mounted. Defaults to false (read-write).
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.cinder.secret: secret_ref is an optional reference to a Kubernetes secret that holds authentication credentials for the Cinder volume provider. It is used when the Cinder volume requires authentication.
The name of the secret that contains authentication credentials for the Cinder volume.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.cinder.volume: The ID of the Cinder volume to mount. This is the unique identifier of the volume in OpenStack Cinder.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.config_map: config_map configures a volume sourced from a Kubernetes ConfigMap. It defines how the ConfigMap's data is exposed as files in the volume, including the ConfigMap name, default file permissions, and optional item mappings.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.config_map.de: Optional: mode bits used to set permissions on files created in the config map volume. Must be an octal value between 0000 and 0777 or a decimal value between 0 and 511. Defaults to 0644.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.config_map.it: Optional list of key-to-path mappings. Each item specifies a key from the ConfigMap and the corresponding path to expose it at within the volume. When omitted, all keys in the ConfigMap are written as files.
The key in the ConfigMap data to mount as a file. Must be a valid ConfigMap key.
Optional mode bits used to set permissions on this file, as an octal integer (e.g., 0644). If not set, the volume's defaultMode is used.
The relative path of the file to map the key to. Must not start with '/' or contain '..'.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.config_map.na: Name of the ConfigMap that supplies the volume data. This must match the name of a ConfigMap in the same namespace as the pod.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.config_map.op: If true, the referenced ConfigMap (or its keys) may be absent; the volume will be empty in that case. If false, the ConfigMap and keys must exist; otherwise the pod fails to start.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.csi: Specifies a volume that is backed by a CSI (Container Storage Interface) driver. This allows pods to mount storage from a CSI driver, which exposes external storage systems to Kubernetes.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.csi.driver: driver specifies the name of the CSI driver that provides the volume. This value must match the name of a CSI driver installed on the cluster.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.csi.fs_type: Filesystem type to mount. If not specified, the volume provider determines the default filesystem.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.csi.node_publ: A reference to a Secret object in the same namespace that contains credentials required by the CSI driver to publish the volume on the node.
The name of the Secret in the pod's namespace that provides sensitive data for the CSI node publish operation.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.csi.read_only: Specifies whether the CSI volume is mounted as read-only. When set to true, the volume is read-only; otherwise it is read-write. Defaults to false.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.csi.volume_at: Attributes of the volume to be used by the CSI driver. The keys and values are driver-specific and defined by the CSI driver implementation.
kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.template.spec.volumes.downward_api: Configures a volume that uses the Kubernetes downward API to expose pod metadata, such as labels, annotations, or resource limits, to containers as files.
Optional file mode (permission bits) applied to files in the downward API volume. Defaults to 0644 when not set.
The list of files to project into the volume. Each item maps a field reference to a specific file path, allowing selective inclusion of Downward API data.
