The number of seconds between each startup probe execution.
Minimum consecutive successes for the probe to be considered successful after having failed. Defaults to 1 and must be 1 for startup probes.
Specifies a TCP socket check for the startup probe. The probe attempts to open a TCP connection to the specified port on the container.
The TCP port to connect to. Accepts a numeric port number or an IANA port name (e.g., 'http' or '80').
Number of seconds after which the startup probe times out. Defaults to 1 second, minimum value is 1.
kubernetes_apps_stateful_set.spec.template.spec.containers.stdin_once: If true, the container's standard input is opened only once for the first attach session and then closed after that session detaches, rather than remaining open for multiple attaches. Defaults to false.
kubernetes_apps_stateful_set.spec.template.spec.containers.terminatio: Specifies the path of a file where the container's termination message is written. The kubelet reads this file to retrieve the message when the container exits. Defaults to /dev/termination-log.
kubernetes_apps_stateful_set.spec.template.spec.containers.tty: Whether to allocate a pseudo-TTY for the container. When true, the container gets a terminal device.
kubernetes_apps_stateful_set.spec.template.spec.containers.volume_dev: List of volume devices (block devices) to be used by the container. Each device specifies a volume name and the path inside the container where the device is mounted.
The name of the volume device, which must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec.
kubernetes_apps_stateful_set.spec.template.spec.containers.volume_mou: The name of the volume to mount. This must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec.volumes.
If set to true, the volume will be mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
Specifies whether read-only mounts should be handled recursively. This field is alpha-level and only honored by servers that enable the RecursiveReadOnlyMounts feature gate.
Path within the volume from which to mount the volume. Defaults to the volume root if not specified.
kubernetes_apps_stateful_set.spec.template.spec.containers.working_di: The container's working directory. If not specified, the container runtime's default is used.
kubernetes_apps_stateful_set.spec.template.spec.dns_config.options.va: The optional value for the DNS option. This field is not required for all DNS options and can be omitted when the option does not need a value.
The command to run in the ephemeral container. This is a list of strings that overrides the default entrypoint of the container image.
List of environment variables to set in the ephemeral container. Each item is an EnvVar object with a name and a value or valueFrom source.
Name of the environment variable. Must be a valid C identifier (e.g., a name consisting of letters, digits, and underscores, not starting with a digit).
The value of the environment variable. This is a string that is assigned to the environment variable named in the corresponding 'name' field within the same env entry.
Source for the environment variable's value, such as a reference to a ConfigMap key, Secret key, field, or resource field. Cannot be used if the 'value' field is set.
The key in the ConfigMap to select. Must be a valid key within the referenced ConfigMap.

Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap key is optional. If true, a missing key results in an empty value for the environment variable and does not prevent the container from starting. If false or omitted, the key must exist or the container creation fails.
The path to the pod field to select. For example, metadata.name or spec.nodeName. Valid paths are defined by the Kubernetes field reference.
The name of the container to select the resource field from. If not specified, the container where the environment variable is defined is used.
The resource to select, such as 'limits.cpu' or 'requests.memory'.
Selects a key of a Secret in the pod's namespace to populate the environment variable with its value.
The name of the Secret to select a key from. This must be the name of a Secret in the same namespace as the pod.
Indicates whether the Secret key must be defined. If true and the key does not exist, the environment variable is omitted; if false and the key is missing, the pod fails to start.
Reference to a ConfigMap whose key-value pairs become environment variables for the ephemeral container. It supports specifying the ConfigMap name and an optional flag to tolerate missing ConfigMap.
Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap must be defined. If set to true, the ConfigMap may be missing; if false or unset, the ConfigMap must exist.
The name of the Secret that provides environment variables to the container. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the StatefulSet.
Indicates whether the referenced Secret must be defined. If set to true, the Secret may be absent and the container will still start.
The container image to use for this ephemeral container, as defined in the ephemeral container spec.

The image pull policy for the ephemeral container. Allowed values: Always, IfNotPresent, Never. Controls when the kubelet pulls the image: Always pulls every time, IfNotPresent pulls only if the image is not already present, Never never pulls and only uses local images.

postStart is a lifecycle hook that runs immediately after an ephemeral container is created. It defines an action to execute, such as an exec command, an HTTP GET request, or a TCP socket check, via a handler object.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP address.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the GET request. Each header is defined by a name and a value.
The value of the HTTP header to send in the GET request. This is the string value paired with the header name, such as the token in an Authorization header.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server for the HTTP GET request.
The sleep action for the post-start lifecycle hook, which pauses the hook for a specified duration. The duration is configured in seconds within this object.
The hostname or IP address to connect to. If not specified, the pod IP is used.
The TCP port number (as a string) or name of a port defined in the container, used for the postStart lifecycle hook's TCP socket action.
Exec specifies an action that runs a command inside the ephemeral container when the pre-stop lifecycle hook is triggered. The command to execute is defined in the 'command' field of this object.
Performs an HTTP GET request to the specified path and port on the container when the pre-stop lifecycle hook is triggered. This action defines the HTTP request details for the pre-stop hook.
The value of the HTTP header used in the pre-stop HTTP GET request. This is part of a key-value pair defined in the httpHeaders list.
Path to access on the HTTP server for the HTTP GET request.
Protocol for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The URI scheme for the HTTP GET request, either 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP' if not specified.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket action. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP address.
Configuration for the liveness probe of the ephemeral container. Kubernetes does not execute probes for ephemeral containers, so this field has no operational effect.
The number of consecutive probe failures allowed before the container is restarted. For a liveness probe, exceeding this threshold triggers a container restart.
Custom headers to send with the HTTP GET request. Each header is an object with 'name' and 'value' fields.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the liveness probe request.
Path to access on the HTTP server.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the liveness probe is initiated.
TCP socket probe configuration for the liveness check. Specifies the host and port to connect to; a successful connection indicates the probe is healthy.
The name of the ephemeral container.
The name of the port. Must be a valid IANA_SVC_NAME and unique within the pod. Named ports can be referenced by services.
Readiness probe for the ephemeral container, determining when the container is ready to accept traffic. If the probe fails, the container is considered not ready.
The name of the HTTP header to send in the HTTP GET request of the readiness probe.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to / if not specified.
The number of seconds between each readiness probe execution. Defaults to 10 seconds if not specified.

Resource requests for this ephemeral container. Keys are resource names (e.g., cpu, memory) and values are Kubernetes quantity strings (e.g., 100m, 1Gi) specifying the minimum amount of resources required.
The operator used to compare the container exit code against the specified values. Valid values are 'In' and 'NotIn'.
The user ID (UID) to run the container process as. If unspecified, defaults to the user defined in the container image metadata.
The port number on which the gRPC server is listening. The probe connects to this port on the container's IP address. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535.
If true, the ephemeral container's stdin is closed after the first time it is attached to, allowing only a single interactive session. Defaults to false.
kubernetes_apps_stateful_set.spec.template.spec.host_aliases.hostname: The list of hostnames to be resolved to the IP address of this host alias entry in the pod's /etc/hosts file.
kubernetes_apps_stateful_set.spec.template.spec.init_containers.lifec: The postStart lifecycle hook, executed immediately after a container is started. Defines actions (e.g., exec command or HTTP GET request) to run before the container's main process continues.

Specifies an HTTP GET request that the kubelet sends to the container as part of the preStop lifecycle hook, allowing custom actions before container termination. The request is defined by parameters such as path, port, host, scheme, and headers.
